search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratap Soya-2(RKS-18) (Soybean)

Search status: four web searches were run in the first batch. A second batch was blocked by a tool-usage limit, so no further searches were possible. Coverage is therefore thin, and several headings have no verified evidence.

Name handling: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Pratap Soya-2(RKS-18)". The only page found that names this variety spells it "Pratap Soya 2 (RKS 18)". All findings below refer to that name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming this variety with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. The DOD variety page found (https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Soyabean.aspx) describes Pratap Soya 45 (RKS-45), not this variety, so it was discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The DOD page mentioning girdle beetle resistance concerns RKS-45 (Pratap Soya 45), not RKS-18, so it was discarded -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Soyabean.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No yield, maturity or trial data for this variety was retrieved.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage recorded as "MALS-450 x Monetta" in a soybean SSR diversity study that lists Pratap Soya 2 (RKS 18) among 38 genotypes -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4312325/
- Note: the brief gives the parent as "MACS-450", while this source spells it "MALS-450". The discrepancy is unresolved; check the CSC notification or the PMC source before relying on either spelling.
- No breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL or marker study specific to this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No page naming a lead breeder for this variety was retrieved. The variety is listed with the institution in the brief (MPUAT, Udaipur Agricultural Research Station, Ummedganj, Kota). No retrieved page confirmed this from an independent source.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for this variety was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Only one page naming this variety was found: the SSR diversity study above (year and journal not captured in the retrieved snippet; see PMC4312325 for the full citation). Authors: not captured. Title: not captured. Journal: not captured. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4312325/
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, ICAR report or conference paper specific to this variety was found. A climate-smart soybean eBook (https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf) appeared in results, but the snippet did not name this variety, so it was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The DOD soybean page (https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx) lists recommended varieties RKS-24, RKS-45, JS-20-29, JS-20-34, NRC-86 and Raj Soya-24. RKS-18 is not among them, so no seed-availability evidence for this variety was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for the states in the brief (Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu). The DOD page found refers to other varieties, and no page confirming state recommendations for RKS-18 was retrieved. Verify against the CSC release minutes or the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in).

Recommended next steps: confirm the parentage spelling, look up the Seednet entry (A0410075) and the CSC notification for the release year (2007), and check KrishiKosh and the MPUAT/ARS Kota pages directly, since the search tool was limited.

basic_info.institution: JAWAHAR LAL NEHRU KRISHI VISHWA VIDYALAYA, JABALPUR, (MP)

drought.details: A 53-genotype morpho-physiological drought study classed JS 97-52 as drought tolerant and reported the highest relative water content (68.72%) among genotypes tested under drought. The same study is also reported in a second source as one of four drought-tolerant genotypes. Under shading of 35%, 50% and 75%, seed yield fell by 24%, 47% and 62% in JS 97-52, a smaller fall than in JS 95-60 (51%, 82%, 92%); this is a light-stress comparison and is not a direct drought measure. Mechanisms beyond relative water content were not described in the digest.

heat.details: No heat-tolerance evidence was found for this variety. A Chhattisgarh sowing-date trial reported higher radiation- and heat-use efficiency in JS 97-52, but this describes resource-use efficiency under sowing-date treatments and is not evidence of heat tolerance.

salinity.details: No salinity-tolerance evidence was found for this variety in the searched sources.

flood.details: The notified-variety table credits JS 97-52 with tolerance to excessive soil moisture. A waterlogging screen treated JS 97-52 as the tolerant reference, with NRC 128 on par with it. The digest does not give quantitative waterlogging data for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Evidence is mixed and partly conflicting. (1) Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): the notified-variety table lists resistance to YMV, but a YMV screen of soybean genotypes classed JS 97-52 as highly susceptible (one of three highly susceptible entries). This is a direct conflict and should be verified before relying on YMV resistance. (2) Collar rot: listed as resistant in the notified-variety table. (3) Charcoal rot: the YMV screen rated JS 97-52 as moderately resistant to charcoal rot (a CR check); a separate field study classed it as highly susceptible to a root-rot/charcoal-rot-type disease, but the snippet does not name the disease clearly, so this conflict is unresolved. (4) Rhizoctonia aerial blight: moderate resistance per the notified-variety table. (5) General: JNKVV describes JS 97-52 as a multiple-resistant, high-yielding cultivar. The original variety record also lists resistance to RRR, BP, CLS and TLS; the digest contains no independent evidence for these, so they are not confirmed here.

pest_resistance.summary: The notified-variety table lists moderate resistance to insects. The original variety record also lists moderate resistance to stem fly, girdle beetle and defoliators, but the digest does not separately confirm these pests. A secondary commercial listing that claimed tolerance to green semilooper, girdle beetle and charcoal rot was excluded because it is a commercial product page and its attribution could not be verified.

agronomic_details.yield: Official recommended average yield in the original variety record is 2200-2500 kg/ha. The digest lists a yield potential of 2500-3000 kg/ha (from the notified-variety table and a commercial source). In a Chhattisgarh kharif 2011 trial, JS 97-52 gave about 52 q/ha (about 5200 kg/ha), the highest among the varieties tested. In a North Eastern Himalayas zinc bio-fortification trial, seed yields were 1.87 Mg/ha (2018) and 1.69 Mg/ha (2019).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the multi-year North Eastern Himalayas trial (2018 and 2019), which reports yields for both years without a stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for kharif cultivation in the listed states. ICAR lists it for the Central and North Eastern Zone. Suitable for early to timely sowing per the original record. The Chhattisgarh plains trial found the highest yield under a 20 June sowing, with a 10 June sowing statistically at par.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Chhattisgarh plains, kharif 2011, sowing-date by variety trial: JS 97-52 gave the most pods per plant (80.3) and the highest seed yield (about 52 q/ha) against JS-335 and JS 93-05. The highest yield was under a 20 June sowing, with a 10 June sowing at par. Higher radiation- and heat-use efficiency was reported. (2) North Eastern Himalayas, 2018 and 2019, zinc bio-fortification trial: seed yields of 1.87 and 1.69 Mg/ha for JS-97-52. (3) Weed study: JS 97-52 had the highest weed-smothering efficiency among the varieties tested, with maturity at 101 days. (4) Shading trial (35%, 50%, 75%): seed yield fell by 24%, 47% and 62% in JS 97-52 versus 51%, 82% and 92% in JS 95-60. (5) Maturity reported as about 100 days in the notified-variety table and 105-110 days in a climate-smart soybean e-book, so the stated maturity range is inconsistent across sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. An SSR marker diversity study placed JS 97-52 among genotypes suggested as parents for resistance breeding, but no specific SSR marker names, positions or alleles were reported.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL evidence specific to JS 97-52 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Soybean 97-52 (JS 97-52), Soybean, JNKVV Jabalpur, released 2008

Name note: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "Jawahar Soybean 97-52 (JS 97-52)", so all evidence below refers to that one name. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no Seednet-sourced finding is included.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A 53-genotype morpho-physiological drought study classed JS 97-52 as drought tolerant, and it showed the highest relative water content (68.72%) among the genotypes tested under drought -- https://www.academia.edu/120304147/Morphological_and_Physiological_Performance_of_Indian_Soybean_Glycine_max_L_Merrill_Genotypes_in_Respect_to_Drought
- The same drought study is also reported at https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4550 (JS97-52 among four drought-tolerant genotypes)
- The notified-variety table credits JS 97-52 with tolerance to excessive soil moisture -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- A waterlogging screen treated JS 97-52 as the tolerant reference, with NRC 128 on par with it -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8613251/
- Under shading of 35%, 50% and 75%, seed yield fell by 24%, 47% and 62% in JS 97-52, a smaller fall than in JS 95-60 (51%, 82%, 92%) -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jac.12783
- No heat- or salinity-tolerance or submergence evidence was found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The notified-variety table lists resistance to yellow mosaic virus (YMV) and collar rot, and moderate resistance to Rhizoctonia aerial blight and to insects -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- JNKVV describes JS 97-52 as a multiple-resistant, high-yielding cultivar -- https://www.jnkvv.org/
- CONFLICT: a YMV screen of soybean genotypes classed JS 97-52 as highly susceptible (one of three highly susceptible entries), which contradicts the YMV resistance claim above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344403409_Morphological_and_Molecular_Screening_of_Soybean_Genotypes_against_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus_Disease
- The same YMV screen rated JS 97-52 as moderately resistant to charcoal rot (a CR check) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344403409_Morphological_and_Molecular_Screening_of_Soybean_Genotypes_against_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus_Disease
- A separate field study also classed JS 97-52 as highly susceptible to a root-rot/charcoal-rot-type disease; the snippet does not name the disease clearly -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354339719_Evaluation_of_Diversity_among_Soybean_Genotypes_via_Yield_Attributing_Traits_and_SSR_Molecular_Markers
- A PPQS integrated pest management listing treats JS 97-52 as tolerant to green semilooper, girdle beetle and charcoal rot (secondary commercial source) -- https://arowest.com/edible-oils/soybean-oil/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A kharif 2011 sowing-date trial in the Chhattisgarh plains found JS 97-52 gave the most pods per plant (80.3) and the highest seed yield, about 52 q/ha, against JS-335 and JS 93-05 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/292313605_Effect_of_sowing_date_and_types_of_varieties_on_yield_attributes_of_Soybean_in_the_Chhattisgarh_plains_zone
- The same trial reports the highest yield under a 20 June sowing, with the 10 June sowing statistically at par -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/292313605_Effect_of_sowing_date_and_types_of_varieties_on_yield_attributes_of_Soybean_in_the_Chhattisgarh_plains_zone
- The same trial also found higher radiation- and heat-use efficiency in JS 97-52 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/292313605_Effect_of_sowing_date_and_types_of_varieties_on_yield_attributes_of_Soybean_in_the_Chhattisgarh_plains_zone
- A zinc bio-fortification trial in the North Eastern Himalayas (2018 and 2019) recorded seed yields of 1.87 and 1.69 Mg/ha for JS-97-52 -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-17007-z
- A weed study reports JS 97-52 had the highest weed-smothering efficiency among the varieties tested, with maturity at 101 days -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue6/PartU/7-6-201-799.pdf
- Maturity is given as about 100 days in the notified-variety table and as 105-110 days in an e-book on climate-smart soybean practice -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx ; https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Climate%20Smart%20Soybean%20Production%20Technologies.pdf
- Yield potential is listed at 2500-3000 kg/ha, with oil content about 17.48% (the DOD table's columns appear swapped) -- https://blucrafts.com/oilseeds/soybean/ ; https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage is recorded as PK 327 x L 129 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344403409_Morphological_and_Molecular_Screening_of_Soybean_Genotypes_against_Yellow_Mosaic_Virus_Disease
- The same parentage appears in a diversity-panel listing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354339719_Evaluation_of_Diversity_among_Soybean_Genotypes_via_Yield_Attributing_Traits_and_SSR_Molecular_Markers
- JS 97-52 is used as a parent in many crosses (for example JS 97-52 × EC 538,828 and JS 97-52 × JS 335) in a waterlogging-tolerance breeding case study -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8613251/
- An SSR marker diversity study placed JS 97-52 among genotypes suggested as parents for resistance breeding -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354339719_Evaluation_of_Diversity_among_Soybean_Genotypes_via_Yield_Attributing_Traits_and_SSR_Molecular_Markers
- No QTL, gene, or genome-resource evidence specific to JS 97-52 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- JNKVV describes itself as developing the Jawahar soybean varieties, and lists JS 97-52 as released in 2008 -- https://www.jnkvv.org/
- The notified-variety table lists the released centre as DSR Indore and JNKVV, Jabalpur -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Soyabean.aspx
- The ICAR National Soybean Research Institute variety list shows JS 97-52 notified in 2008 for the Central and North Eastern Zone -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- No named lead breeder was found in any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Directorate of Farms, JNKVV, Jabalpur (institute-level contact; it handles breeder seed production): email seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com, mobile 8770867088 -- http://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
- Institute website: https://www.jnkvv.org/ (

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: •	CZ (Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Marathwada and Vidarbha region of Maharashtra and Bundelkhand region of U.P.) •	NEHZ (Assam, Manipur and Meghalaya). •	EZ (Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Bihar).  Suitable for medium to high
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: •	It is of medium with strong stem, does not lodge. •	It is resistant to shattering up to seven days after maturity. •	Suitable for timely sown 20 June to 5 July. •	45 cm Row to Row and 5-7 cm plant to plant distance •	70-75 kg seed is recommended. •	It performs well under recommended dose of fertilizers 20 N, 60 P2O5, 20 K2O and 20 S kg/ha
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	White flower  2.	Rounded ovate leaf 3.	Glabrous pods and stem 4.	Black hilum
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: It has given the higher yield performance tested over three years and different locations of Central Zone in coordinated trials indicated that it is tolerant to abiotic stresses in all the three zones.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
In CZ reaction to major diseases: Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) during 2015-16, the proposed variety JS 20-116 has recorded Absolute Resistant (AR) at Sehore and Amravati, highly resistant (HR) reaction at Jabalpur. During 2016-17, JS 20-116 recorded HR and R reaction at Amravati and Sehore respectively, similarly found HR reaction at Jabalpur and Amravati during 2017-18. For Charcoal Rot the proposed entry showed AR reaction at Amravati, HR reaction at Jabalpur during 2015-16. During 2016-17 it showed AR reaction at Jabalpur and Amravati. In the year 2017-18, AR reaction recorded at Sehore and HR reaction at Amravati.

In NEHZ, recation to major diseases: The propsed variety showed AR reaction for Pod blight (ct.) at Medziphema and MR at B. Chariali, AR at Umiam (2015-16) and HR reaction at B Chariali Umiam and Medziphema during the year 2016-17, it has also showed HR reaction at B. Chariali (2017-18). For BLB the proposed entry showed AR reaction at Umiam in 2015-16.

In EZ reaction to major diseases: JS 20-116 has shown Moderately Resistance (MR) reaction at Dholi against Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) during all the three years i.e. 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18 whereas, the check variety JS 335 and the qualifying variety RVS 2010-11 recorded Susceptible (S) and Moderately Susceptible (MS) reaction, respectively during 2015-16 at Dholi. For Indian Bud Blight (IBB) at Raipur, the proposed variety showed Absolute Resistant (AR) reaction during 2015-16.

Reaction to disease consortium of NEHZ: The proposed variety JS 20-116 has showed resistant high yielding (R-HY) and Susceptible high yielding S-HY (T) reaction at B. Chariali in the year 2017-18 and 2016-17, respectively.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests:
In CZ, Reaction to Insect pest: During 2015-16, JS 20-116 has shown HR reaction against Stem fly at Amravati, R reaction at Parbhani and MR at Sehore during 2016-17 and MR reaction at Parbhani and Sehore during tehyear 2017-18. The proposed entry has shown MR reaction at Amravati during 2015-16, MR at Sehore during 2016-17, HR at Kota and MR at Amravati and Sehore during 2017-18 against Girdle Beetle. For defoliators, MR reaction at Amravtai during 2015-16, MR reaction at Sehore and Kota during 2017-18. It has shown HR reaction for Green Semiloopers at Sehore in 2017-18 and MR reaction at Indore for Tobacco cater pillars in 2016-17.

IN NEHZ, Reaction to insect-pest: JS 20-116 had shown resistant reaction (R) for Stem fly and Defoliator at Imphal in the year 2017-18. It has recorded moderately resistant (MR) against Aphids at Imphal (2015-16 & 2017-18) and Resistant (R) at Medziphem (2017-18). It has recorded Resistant reaction (R) at Medziphema and Moderately Resistant (MR) at Imphal during 2017-18 for Leaf Webber. For Tobacco cater pillar the proposed variety showed Moderately resistant reaction (MR) at Imphal (2016-17 and 2017-18). It is found to be Highly resistant (HR) against Bihar hairy cater pillar in 2017-18 and Moderately resistant (MR) during 2016-17 at Imphal. In the year 2017-18, it has shown HR reaction to Leaf hopper and Blister Beetle and Resistant reaction (R) to pod bug at Medziphema.

In EZ, Reaction to insect-pests: during 2015-16 at Raipur the proposed variety JS 20-116 recorded 0.0 reaction against Girdle beetle and 2.5 against defoliators. Whereas, the check varieties JS 335 (1.0), RKS 18 (1.0) and JS 97-52 (1.5) and the qualifying variety RVS 2010-1 (0.5) reaction against Girdle beetle. In case of defoliators JS 335 recorded 3.5, RKS 18 (4.5), JS 97-52 (2.0) and qualifying variety RVS 2010-1 (16.5) during 2015-16.

Reaction to Insect-pest Complex CZ: Ultimately, against insect pest complex it has rated as Resistant High Yielding (R-HY) at Amravati, Parbhani, Kota and Indore during 2016-17 and R-HY at Sehore during 2017-18 whereas, susceptible high yielding (S-HY) at Kota during 2017-18.

Reaction to Insect-Pest Complex NEHZ: Proposed Variety has been rated as Resistant High Yielding (R-HY) at Imphal in the year 2017-18.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE --
The ICAR-style abiotic-stress review lists JWALAMUKHI (PSCL-5015) among Indian abiotic stress-tolerant sunflower varieties, but the snippet I could read does not say which stress (drought, heat, salinity, etc.) it is credited for -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/1150022
No stress-specific trial data for this variety found in the other results.

DISEASE AND PEST --
No evidence found. The four searches returned no disease or pest resistance data naming Jwalamukhi.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
Jwalamukhi described as a medium-tall hybrid, about 170 cm plant height, ready in about 120 days, average yield about 7.3 q/acre, oil content about 42% -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/sunflower
Listed among popular sunflower varieties without agronomic detail -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/how-to-grow-sunflower-a-short-guide/
An Indian extension-demonstration study reports Jwalamukhi as the most popular hybrid among both FLD and non-FLD farmers (56% and 60%), so it was widely adopted in that sample -- https://acspublisher.com/journals/index.php/ijee/article/download/5889/5258/5857
Multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) --
No evidence found for parentage (SF OIA/SF OIR), breeding method, breeding-line codes, QTL or genome resources. Parentage in the input record has not been verified by any page returned.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION --
No evidence found. No page named a lead breeder or scientist for Jwalamukhi (PSCL-5015). The Proagro Seed Co. attribution comes from the input record only; no search result confirmed it.

CONTACT DETAILS --
No evidence found. No breeder, institute or company contact for this variety appeared in results. The only address on record is the input's "PROAGRO SEED CO. LTD. 8-1-39, TOLICHOWKI HYDERABAD-500 008," which is unverified.

PUBLICATIONS --
No evidence found for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers that name this variety. The IJEE adoption study above (URL https://acspublisher.com/journals/index.php/ijee/article/download/5889/5258/5857) is a journal article, but the authors, year and title were not in the retrieved text and should be filled in from the source before citing.

SEED AVAILABILITY --
No evidence found. The only seed-sale result (an IndiaMART listing for "Surajmukhi" seeds) concerns a different, unnamed product and was discarded. No Seednet, NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Jwalamukhi was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES --
A breeding-technique slide deck lists Jwalamukhi among preferred hybrids for Andhra Pradesh -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/sunflower-breeding-technique/244371036
This is a secondary training slide, not a CSC or gazette notification, so the input field "Unknown" should be treated as still unresolved.

NAME NOTE --
Under every heading, the evidence refers to "Jwalamukhi" with "PSCL-5015" in the abiotic-stress and agronomy pages. No result used the Seednet form "JWALAMUKHI (PSCL-5015)" verbatim, and none used the CSC minutes name separately, so the two names could not be checked against each other.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MLSFH-47 (AH-11-34), Sunflower

Name note: The release-minutes name and the Seednet name are identical ("MLSFH-47 (AH-11-34)"). Across four searches, the only pages that mention this variety name in a sunflower context used the shorter form "MLSFH-47". None mentioned "AH-11-34" or variety code A0411014. The findings below therefore refer to MLSFH-47 as a name only.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned nothing on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for MLSFH-47.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page named MLSFH-47 with disease or pest resistance data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Sunflower agronomy slides give general hybrid spacing (hybrids at 60 x 30 cm, varieties at 45 x 30 cm) and line-sowing advice, but do not name MLSFH-47 in the spacing or sowing guidance. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/sunflowersunflowersunflowersunflower-1-pptx/272193622
No multi-location trial or yield data for MLSFH-47 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage given in the brief (8A x XR-52, female 8A, male R52) did not appear in any search result. Nothing on QTL, markers or genome resources for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No page named a lead breeder or developing scientist for MLSFH-47. The only institutional link is the brief's own record (Research & Maintenance Division, Mahendra Hybrid Seeds Co. Ltd, Jalna), and no search page confirmed it.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, address or contact page for Mahendra Hybrid Seeds' Research & Maintenance Division or for any breeder was returned. The brief's address (A-10/11, Old MIDC Area, Jalna-431203, M.S.) is unverified by search.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The searches returned no papers, AICRP or ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, or conference papers on MLSFH-47. Generic sunflower breeding reviews (e.g., ResearchGate "Achievements of sunflower breeding" and "Breeding Strategies for Sunflower Helianthus annuus L. Improvement") appeared but do not mention this variety, so they are not listed as evidence.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for seed sellers, NSC/State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU stocks. Commercial sunflower seed pages returned were for unrelated products (US seed retailers).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The brief lists this as "Unknown". Undated, unofficial slide compilations list MLSFH-47 among preferred hybrids in three states:
- Maharashtra: "...PAC-1091, MLSFH-47, KBSH-44..." -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/sunflowersunflowersunflowersunflower-1-pptx/272193622
- Karnataka: "...DSH-1, MLSFH-47, KBSH-41..." -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/sunflowersunflowersunflowersunflower-1-pptx/272193622
- Andhra Pradesh: "...PAC-1091, MLSFH-47, KBSH-44, Pro.Sun.09..." -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/sunflower-breeding-technique/244371036

These slides are secondary training material with no date or original source. They should be treated as weak evidence and checked against the official ICAR/AICRP sunflower recommendation documents and Seednet entry before the record is finalised.

Summary: The web search could not verify most fields in this record. Only the state-level preferred-hybrid listings are supported by evidence. Breeder, contact, parentage, trial, stress and publication fields need official sources such as the Seednet entry for code A0411014, the Mahendra company website, or the AICRP on Sunflower reports.

drought.details: No stress-specific drought tolerance test or statement was found for DRSF-113. The variety is described as suited to rainfed situations, ideally suited to late-sown conditions in black soils and to residual moisture conditions (input variety record). The digest notes that adaptation is described as rainfed but that stress-specific tolerance was not stated in any retrieved page. Rainfed suitability is adaptation information and is not treated here as evidence of drought tolerance.

heat.details: The input variety record states that physiological analysis for high temperature tolerance indicated consistently higher tolerance for three years, and that DRSF-113 was concluded to be a stress tolerant genotype. The digest did not find any retrieved page supporting this claim, and no magnitude or comparator is given. The elevated CO2 study (open-top chambers, 550 +/-50 umol/l) reports yield and biomass increases but is explicitly not a stress-tolerance test and is not used as heat evidence. Level is therefore unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield under normal conditions of 1200 kg/ha and oil yield of 459 kg/ha (input variety record). Official variety table: yield potential 1000-1500 kg/ha, oil 36-39%. ICAR-IIOR page: average seed yield 900-1000 kg/ha, potential 1500-1800 kg/ha. The input record lists average yield as Unknown. Commercial exporter pages give 1200-1400 kg/ha but are not official data. The input record states DRSF-113 recorded higher seed and oil yield than the popular variety Modern.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources as a formal stability analysis. Yields across the reported trials ranged from about 1547 kg/ha (semi-arid, three locations) to about 1802.4 kg/ha (Pantnagar, rabi irrigated). Performance under organic management in Sikkim is reported as an early-maturing, small-capitulum type, without yield figures in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for rainfed kharif and rabi situations, with ideal suitability for late-sown conditions in black soils and residual moisture conditions (input variety record and ICAR-IIOR page). The official table lists All India. The four-state list is taken from the input record; the digest states that no retrieved page confirmed these four states.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: STEM HAIRINESS AT THE TOP : ABSENT; NUMBER OF LEAVES ON MAIN STEM :WEAK; RAY FLOWER NUMBER : ABSENT; RAY FLOWER SHAPE : HIGH; RAY FLOWER COLOUR : MANY; PLANT : NATURAL HEIGHT : TALL; PLANT BRANCHING : ABSENT; SEED LENGTH : MEDIUM; SEED SHAPE : OVOID ELONGATE; SEED WEIGHT : MEDIUM; SEED BASE COLOUR : BLACK; SEED MOTTLING : ABSENT; SEED STRIPES : ABSENT; HULL % : MEDIUM. ICAR-IIOR page also gives: days to maturity Kharif 90-92 and Rabi 95-98; days to flowering Kharif 55-60 and Rabi 60-65; plant height 150-160 cm; head diameter 14-16 cm; 100-seed weight 4.5-5.0 g; volume weight 38-42 g/100 ml; hull 30-32%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Semi-arid trial at three locations in Telangana and Maharashtra (kharif 2013): DRSF-113 was a check identified as high yielding at about 1547 kg/ha. (2) Pantnagar (Uttarakhand) rabi irrigated trial: seed yield about 1802.4 kg/ha; listed among better performers with TNAUSUF and DRSF-108. (3) Organic management trial, ICAR-NOFRI Tadong (Sikkim), rabi 2016-17: early maturer at 133 days, oil 35.5%, capitulum diameter 9.7 cm, the smallest among the hybrids and varieties tested. (4) North-Eastern Hill evaluation of sunflower hybrids at four locations: DRSF-113 used as a variety check; no result values for DRSF-113 were captured in the digest. (5) Elevated CO2 study in open-top chambers (550 +/-50 umol/l): seed yield rose about 35-46% and biomass about 61-68%; this is a CO2 response study, not a stress or yield trial under normal conditions. (6) Genetic diversity (Mahalanobis D2, 64 genotypes, rabi 2009) and genetic resource evaluation (350 accessions, kharif 2013) at DOR used DRSF 113 as a check; no result values for the variety were captured.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DRSF-113 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "DRSF-113", so the evidence below applies to both. Searches run: (1) DRSF-113 Sunflower variety, (2) DRSF-113 Sunflower breeder developed by Directorate of Oilseeds Research, (3) DRSF-113 sunflower research paper trial, (4) DRSF-113 sunflower seed availability. No seednet.gov.in page was returned by any search, so the Seednet record itself is unverified (variety code A0411037 not confirmed online).

STRESS TOLERANCE
Stress-specific tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) was not stated for this variety in any retrieved page. Adaptation is described as rainfed (see RECOMMENDED STATES). Under a semi-arid trial at three locations in Telangana and Maharashtra, DRSF-113 was a check that was identified as high yielding at about 1547 kg/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328671869_Characterization_evaluation_and_multivariate_analysis_of_sunflower_germplasm_under_semi-_arid_environments_of_three_locations_in_two_sunflower_growing_states_in_India
Under elevated CO2 (550 ±50 µl/l) in open-top chambers, DRSF 113 seed yield rose about 35–46% and biomass about 61–68%; this is a CO2 response study, not a stress-tolerance test -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11738-014-1651-4

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest reaction data for DRSF-113.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Official variety table: release 2007, yield potential 1000-1500 kg/ha, oil 36-39%, releasing centre DOR Hyderabad, recommended for All India, traits listed as high yield -- http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sunflower.aspx
ICAR-IIOR variety page: average seed yield 900-1000 kg/ha, potential 1500-1800 kg/ha; days to maturity Kharif 90-92, Rabi 95-98; days to flowering Kharif 55-60, Rabi 60-65; plant height 150-160 cm; head diameter 14-16 cm; 100-seed weight 4.5-5.0 g; volume weight 38-42 g/100 ml; hull 30-32% -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/540
Pantnagar (Uttarakhand) rabi irrigated trial: DRSF-113 seed yield about 1802.4 kg/ha, listed among better performers with TNAUSUF and DRSF-108 -- https://ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/jas/article/download/0/0/50109/54220
Organic management trial, ICAR-NOFRI Tadong (Sikkim), rabi 2016-17: DRSF-113 among early maturers (133 days), oil 35.5%, capitulum diameter 9.7 cm (smallest of the hybrids and varieties tested) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/256842095_PROGRESS_IN_THE_GENETIC_MODIFICATION_OF_SUNFLOWER_OIL_QUALITY (note: the page title does not match the trial content; the trial text is the relevant part)
North-Eastern Hill evaluation of sunflower hybrids at four locations (DRSF-113 used as a variety check) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350755709_Evaluation_of_sunflower_hybrids_for_their_suitability_in_North_Eastern_Hill_Region_of_India
Commercial exporter pages give yields of 1200-1400 kg/ha and 90-98 days to maturity; these are not official data -- https://mswt.in/nuts/sunflower-seeds/ and https://pisumfoods.com/oilseeds/sunflowers

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Pedigree: selection from gene pool (GP lines genepool), as given on the ICAR-IIOR page -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/540 ; also http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sunflower.aspx lists the release only
Breeding method: pure-line selection from gene pool material is implied by the "selection" pedigree; no crossing scheme was found
Genetic diversity: DRSF 113 was used as a check in a Mahalanobis D² study of 64 sunflower genotypes at DOR (rabi 2009); this does not give parentage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232262490_Analysis_of_Genetic_Diversity_in_Germplasm_Accessions_of_Sunflower_Helianthus_annuus_L
Genetic resources: DRSF 113 was a check in the evaluation of 350 accessions at DOR (kharif 2013) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
QTL / marker / genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad (formerly Directorate of Oilseeds Research, Rajendranagar) -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/540 and http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sunflower.aspx
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. No pages named a breeder for DRSF-113.
Station: Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030 -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/540

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The same searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for Prosun-09 or Pro-009.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only trial-type hit was a Prosun seed-coating trial by NDSU, which concerns a seed pellet product, not this variety. The Hybrid CO2 TNAU trial data were discarded because that is a different hybrid.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage SFOO3A/SF002R (SF003A/SF002R) and variety code A0411040 did not appear in any result. Breeding-method hits were generic USPTO inbred-line patents and an unrelated German ProSun project, both discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder or scientist. Institution-level evidence: a SeedQuest company profile says Proagro Seed Company Ltd. is a Hyderabad-headquartered, Bayer CropScience-linked firm that conducts R&D and marketing of hybrid seed, including sunflower -- https://www.seedquest.com/whitepages/asiapacific/india/id/p/proagroseed.htm

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only, not variety-specific. SeedQuest lists Proagro Seed Company Ltd., A-304, Ansal Chambers-I, 3 Bhikaiji Cama Place, New Delhi 110066, India; Tel +91 124 636 1572; Fax +91 124 636 1204; email field blank -- https://www.seedquest.com/whitepages/asiapacific/india/id/p/proagroseed.htm
Note: this address differs from the record's registered address (8-1-39, Tolichowki, Hyderabad-500 008). Verify before use. No breeder contact, official email, or institute contact page was found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found that cites this variety. One figure in a heterosis-breeding review lists Pro-009 (Prosun-09), which is the only page naming this variety; authors and journal are not shown in the retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/202264878_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Heterosis_Breeding_in_Sunflower_Helianthus_annuus_L
Discarded: "Hybrid CO2 - A high yielding sunflower hybrid for Tamil Nadu" (Manivannan et al., 2017, Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, DOI 10.5958/0975-928X.2017.00021.7). It is a different TNAU hybrid, not Prosun-09.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing names Prosun-09 or Pro-009. TNAU seed-production listings cover other sunflower hybrids (DCSH 1, CO 2, KBSH 1, TCSH 1), which were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not confirmed by any search result. The record lists Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu, but no retrieved page supports this.

Release date: the heterosis-review figure gives release as 2003 at a TANU (Coimbatore) committee meeting in April 2003, which conflicts with the 2005 year of release in the record. Resolve this against the CSC minutes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/202264878_Present_Status_and_Future_Prospects_for_Heterosis_Breeding_in_Sunflower_Helianthus_annuus_L

Name matching: the heterosis-review figure uses "Pro-009 (Prosun-09)", which matches both the CSC name and the Seednet name (PROSUN-09 (PRO-009)). No page was found that uses the Seednet crop label "SUNFLOWER (SURYAMUKHI)" or the variety code A0411040.

(3) Evaluation paper on promising varieties and hybrids released in different states: DRSF-108 was the tallest entry with the largest head diameter (16.2 cm). (4) Bee-pollination study: the open-pollinated DRSF-108 showed a stronger response to bee pollination than the hybrid DRSH-1 for seed yield, oil content and test weight. Bagged versus unbagged plants gave seed yields of 0.95 kg and 0.07 kg per 34 plants; the digest does not state which entry these plant-level values refer to.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DRSF-108 Sunflower: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institution; research/papers; seed availability). Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "DRSF-108", so every heading below refers to DRSF-108. Seednet portal pages did not come up in any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to DRSF-108. The only stress-related hit is a UV-B and ozone study that used DRSF 108 as one of two cultivars and reported growth, seed yield and oil quality responses. The retrieved text did not give the outcome values for DRSF 108 -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30761429

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. None of the four searches returned disease or pest resistance data for DRSF-108.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Irrigated rabi trial at Pantnagar: DRSF-108 gave the higher seed yield in that trial (1780.5 and 1860.8 kg/ha across two entries), with the highest plant height (161.9 and 159.6 cm) and head diameter of 16.2 and 14.9 cm -- https://ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/jas/article/download/0/0/50109/54220
Pantnagar trial, same group of AICRP entries: DRSF-108 was among the top entries under irrigated conditions, with the highest plant height and head diameter recorded for it -- https://ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/jas/article/view/0/50101
Evaluation paper on promising varieties and hybrids released in different states: DRSF-108 was reported as the tallest entry and had the largest head diameter (16.2 cm) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368384904_Evaluation_of_Sunflower_Promising_Varieties_and_Hybrids_Released_for_Cultivation_in_Different_States_of_India
Bee-pollination study: the open-pollinated DRSF-108 showed a stronger response to bee pollination than the hybrid DRSH-1 for seed yield, oil content and test weight. Bagged versus unbagged plants gave seed yields of 0.95 kg and 0.07 kg per 34 plants -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343398704_BEE_FORAGING_ON_ELITE_SUNFLOWER_HELIANTHUS_ANNUUS_L_CULTIVARS_AND_ITS_IMPACT_ON_SEED_AND_OIL_YIELD
Exporter web pages (commercial, not verified): they give DRSF-108 an average yield of about 1200 to 1400 kg/ha and an introduction or release year of 2004 -- https://mswt.in/nuts/sunflower-seeds/ and https://pisumfoods.com/oilseeds/sunflowers
Maturity duration: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: "selection from gene pool" (the same phrase as the input record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368384904_Evaluation_of_Sunflower_Promising_Varieties_and_Hybrids_Released_for_Cultivation_in_Different_States_of_India
Breeding-line codes, breeding method, QTL and marker studies for DRSF-108: No evidence found. The genetic resources and association-analysis pages retrieved mention DRSF 108 only as a check and do not describe its genetics -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: the Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad, per the evaluation paper. The CSC record names the Directorate of Oilseeds Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500 030 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368384904_Evaluation_of_Sunflower_Promising_Varieties_and_Hybrids_Released_for_Cultivation_in_Different_States_of_India
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No named breeder was linked to DRSF-108 in the retrieved pages.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for DRSF-108 or for the Directorate of Oilseeds Research appeared in the retrieved text. The only address data available is the institute name and place in the CSC record above.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PT-507 (seednet name: PT-507; CSC minutes name: PT-507; crop: Mustard/rapeseed, Seednet crop TORIA, code A0412017)

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The stress-tolerance search returned no page naming PT-507 with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. Results were a rapeseed-mustard journal article (epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/3993/1578/8157), which does not name PT-507 in the text I reviewed.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page naming PT-507 with disease or pest resistance data was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The one Toria agronomy hit, "Response of Toria (Brassica campestris var. Toria) to Integrated Nutrient Management in Central Plain Region of Punjab" (researchgate.net/publication/377802816), does not name PT-507, so it was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
PT-507 is listed as an "Other identity" of a Toria accession in the NBPGR passport record (source collection "INSTITUTE", crop name Toria) -- http://pgrinformatics.nbpgr.ernet.in/ic/SourceAccessionDetails.aspx?id=9&cp=2817. This confirms only the identifier. No parentage, breeding-line code, breeding method or genomic data for PT-507 was found. The parentage field in the input record ("normal planting (September) in eastern zone as pure crop under rainfed conditions") describes sowing practice, not a genetic pedigree, so it is not treated as parentage.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No breeder name is attributed to PT-507. The institution named in the input record is G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, but no search result confirmed that PT-507 was developed there.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder contact, and no GBPUAT or division contact page for PT-507, was returned. No contact details have been filled in from memory.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The only paper retrieved for Toria (the Punjab INM study above) does not name PT-507. The Pantnagar rapeseed-mustard article from the first search is not attributed to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed search returned only an unrelated vegetable seed product (Lake Valley Seed 507, mcguckin.com/2802805/product/lake-valley-seed-507), which was discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for PT-507 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found in search results. The states listed in the input record are Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal, with a 1990 release year. These come from the input record and were not verified by any search result.

NOTES ON SCOPE
- Four web_search queries were run: (1) PT-507 Mustard / rapeseed variety, (2) PT-507 Toria TORIA breeder institute, (3) PT-507 Toria research paper, (4) PT-507 toria seed availability. A fifth query (to re-check the NBPGR and Pantnagar hits) was blocked by the tool-use limit, so no further verification was possible.
- Only truncated snippets (about 200 characters) of each result were reviewed. Full pages were not opened, so a relevant detail could have been missed.
- The only result that names PT-507 with the crop is the NBPGR passport page. The strict relevance rule therefore leaves very little usable evidence for this variety.
- Suggested next steps, if more searching is allowed: the GBPUAT Pantnagar Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics site, the ICAR-DRMR (Bharatpur) or AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard annual reports, the Seednet variety page, and the KrishiKosh thesis repository.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalpa Mitra (IND 022S) (CCS-5), Coconut

Search note: four web_search queries were run (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, seed availability). The Seednet name "KALPA MITRA (IND 022S) (CCS-5)" was not retrieved by any query, so the Seednet portal itself is unverified. Every finding below refers to "Kalpa Mitra" (the CSC name, which also appears as CCS-5 and IND 022S on the AICRP page). Search results for other coconut varieties, a spam export site (ordertaqueriapoblana.com), and unrelated pages were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Described as relatively drought tolerant, and suited to moisture-deficit conditions -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- Relatively drought tolerant, with high nut and oil yield -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Listed among CPCRI varieties tolerant to drought -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement
- Performs well under irrigated and rainfed conditions -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/Horticulturevolume-IIreadytocomm.pdf
- No evidence found for flood, salinity, submergence or heat tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- No evidence found for Kalpa Mitra resistance to root (wilt), eriophyid mite, or other pests/diseases. Root (wilt) tolerance is attributed to other CPCRI varieties (Kalparaksha, Kalpasree, Kalpa Sankara). -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Palms are regular bearers, flower about 6 years after planting; tender nut water 495 ml, copra about 241 g, oil 66.5% -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- Potential of 80 nuts/palm/year; flowering about 58 months after planting; tender nut water 495 ml -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/coconut_varieties/coconut_tall_kalpamitra.html
- Average yield 13,973 nuts/ha, copra 34 q/ha, oil 22 q/ha, suited to ball copra -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html
- Yield figures conflict across sources (110 nuts/palm/year in one CPCRI table, 91 under rainfed conditions in another, 15,222 nuts/ha with 3.68 t/ha copra in the ICJ table). Source text is partly garbled, so no single yield is recorded. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/Horticulturevolume-IIreadytocomm.pdf ; https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Evaluated at CPCRI Kasaragod, CPCRI Research Centre Kidu, and AICRP on Palms centres in Karnataka and Assam -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Proposed for release by the AICRP Mondouri centre, West Bengal; also suitable for ball copra -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-palms-en (Google-translated URL: https://translate.google.com/translate?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.bckv.edu.in%2Findex.php%2Fen%2Faicrp-on-palms-en&hl=hi&sl=en&tl=hi&client=srp)
- Suitable for ball copra production -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources):
- Parentage: developed as a selection from IND 022, Java Tall (JVT) -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Breeding method: population developed at CPCRI by selecting high-yielding palms and inter se mating of the selected palms, followed by seedling selection and evaluation -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Breeding-line codes: IND 022S and CCS-5 appear together with the Kalpa Mitra name -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-palms-en
- Accession EC 548004 (introduction from Indonesia, 1947): not verified in any retrieved page.
- No evidence found for QTL, marker studies, or genome resources specific to Kalpa Mitra.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod, Kerala -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement
- Release year 2008 -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/Technology_Book.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No individual breeder was named for this variety in any retrieved page.

PUBLICATIONS:

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalpa Dhenu (IND 006S) (CCS-6), Coconut

Name check: The CSC release name is "Kalpa Dhenu (IND 006S) (CCS-6)" and the Seednet name is "KALPA DHENU (IND 006S) (CCS-6)". Searches returned only "Kalpa Dhenu" without the IND/CCS suffix. Pages that mention "Kalpa Dhenu" as a CPCRI coconut variety are treated as this variety. Commercial listings that sell "hybrid Kalpa Dhenu" plants are reported separately because the variety is not documented as a hybrid.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as relatively tolerant to moisture deficit stress and yielding 86-128 nuts/palm depending on management -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817
- Listed among CPCRI varieties that are relatively tolerant to drought -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement
- Coconut Board notes it is drought tolerant -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Described as a regular bearer that is relatively tolerant to drought -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html
- Performs under both irrigated and rainfed conditions and is relatively drought tolerant -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/Horticulturevolume-IIreadytocomm.pdf
- Salinity, flood, submergence, heat: No evidence found in the searched pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Field resistance to coconut root (wilt) disease is listed as a trait -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/Technology_Book.pdf
- Yields 90-107 nuts/palm in the root (wilt) disease endemic tract -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817
- A Chhattisgarh (Bastar) trial reports pest incidence for Kalpa Dhenu, but the page does not clearly identify the pest; it was not used -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12S/PartO/S-10-12-119-930.pdf
- Red palm weevil and eriophyid mite resistance specific to this variety: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Tall, robust palms; flowering at about 67 months; tender nut water about 290 ml; yield about 15,012 nuts/ha, copra about 37 q/ha, oil about 24 q/ha (CPCRI-derived figures) -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html
- Other reported figures: 22,794 nuts/ha/year and 290 ml water -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- Coconut Board table: 14,160 nuts/ha and 3.41 t copra/ha, with high nut and oil yield -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Fruit is green, oval, large, with high husk and good copra content; copra 96 g; nut water 240 mL -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817
- Figures vary across sources (copra, nut yield, nut water, flowering age). Note the discrepancy rather than choosing one set.
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found beyond the summary tables above.
- Chhattisgarh (Bastar) non-traditional region trial with growth and yield data for Kalpa Dhenu -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12S/PartO/S-10-12-119-930.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage conflict. The user record says it derives from CPCRI accession IND 006 (IC 296657), collected from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in 1940, via selection of superior palms and inter se mating. The Coconut Board source says it is a selection from IND 008 (Lakshadweep Ordinary, LCT). A ResearchGate abstract says it is a selection from Andaman Giant Tall. Treat parentage as unresolved. -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/303251470_Coconut_breeding_In_India
- Breeding method: selection from indigenous germplasm by CPCRI (the Coconut Board source names a seedling selection and IND-series origin).
- Breeding-line code IND 006S and CCS-6 identifiers: No evidence found in the searched pages except in the release name.
- QTL, markers, genome resources specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-CPCRI, Kasaragod. It was released and notified through the Central Sub-committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Identified in the CPCRI and AICRP on Palms records as an ICAR-CPCRI, Kasaragod release, with the AICRP on Palms Aliyarnagar centre also listed -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/tb104.pdf
- Lead scientist: Dr V. Niral (Principal Scientist), with B. Augustine Jerard and K. Samsudeen named on an ICAR-CPCRI Division of Crop Improvement training manual -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343362141_Training_Manual_on_Production_processing_and_marketing_mechanisms_in_coconut
- Lead breeder for this specific variety: Not named explicitly in the searched pages. Dr Niral's name is attached to the institute's coconut variety overview, not to Kalpa Dhenu alone.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr V. Niral, Principal Scientist, ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute, Kasaragod, Kerala 671 124 (contact address given for the variety overview) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817

- Coconut Board (2019). Indian Coconut Journal, July 2019 issue (variety article covering Kalpa Dhenu). Indian Coconut Journal. -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- CPCRI supplies planting material and breeder seed for improved varieties, and seed gardens are established for distribution -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817

- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Kerala, East Coast region of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/name-of-variety-salient-features_24.html
- Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343362141_Training_Manual_on_Production_processing_and_marketing_mechanisms_in_coconut

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HD-107 (cotton)
Variety name (CSC minutes): HD-107. Seednet name: HD-107. Both names are the same, so every finding below refers to HD-107. Seednet variety code A0501006 and the Seednet variety page were not found in search results.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The search returned general cotton drought and heat papers and articles on other varieties (for example, FH-114, UA 107, Zhong R2016), none naming HD-107. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9280337/ (not HD-107)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for HD-107. A CICR bulletin notes a rising leaf curl virus problem in upland cotton in the northern zone and calls for resistant varieties, but does not name HD-107. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
HAU Hisar extension work on pink bollworm is general and does not name HD-107. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/hisar-agri-varsity-steps-up-efforts-for-reviving-cotton-cultivation-in-state

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
HD 107 is said to have given stable seed cotton yield across varying environments. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
Sowing is in April, with picking possible by October. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
The CICR bulletin lists HD 107 in its Haryana table with a value row (1996 entry, plus numeric columns whose headings were not captured), so the columns cannot be interpreted with confidence. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
No multi-location trial data specific to HD-107 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: female parent DS-5, male parent HD 266. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
Conflict: the Seednet parentage field reads "from local germplasm collection," which contradicts the AICCIP statement above. Both are recorded; the AICCIP source is more specific but was not verified against the Seednet record.
Breeding method, breeding-line codes, QTL, markers and genome resources for HD-107: No evidence found. The "pedigree method" with three-way cross (LH 354 x SBI 71) x H 777 on the AICCIP page belongs to a different variety and is excluded. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
HD 107 is used as a male parent in a desi cotton (G. arboreum) hybrid combining-ability study, which links the name to a breeding programme in desi cotton. -- https://www.academia.edu/96446048/Combining_ability_study_on_seed_cotton_yield_and_its_components_in_desi_cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_L_

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar, with the cotton work carried out at Hisar. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html ; https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
Breeder name: No evidence found. No named breeder was linked to HD-107 in any result. The AICCIP Hisar page names only a post (Scientist (Cotton)), not a person.
Station: No station-specific attribution for HD-107 was found. The Cotton Research Station, Sirsa (CCS HAU) runs breeder seed production, but no source links HD-107 to Sirsa. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level contact (AICCIP cotton unit, Hisar; no personal breeder contact found):
Role: Scientist (Cotton), Chowdhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar - 125 001, Haryana.
Phone: 01662-231171, 231172 (office); 236082 (residence). Fax: 01662-234952, 01662-234613.
Email: hisar_aiccip@yahoo.com
Source: http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
Cotton Research Station, Sirsa (institute-level, not HD-107-specific): Regional Director Dr. Virender Singh; phone 01666-221352; email crsccshau@gmail.com. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20
Institute page: https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20

PUBLICATIONS
Mandhania, S. et al. (2016). Combining ability study on seed cotton yield and its components in desi cotton (Gossypium arboreum L.). Journal of Cotton Research and Development -- https://www.academia.edu/96446048/Combining_ability_study_on_seed_cotton_yield_and_its_components_in_desi_cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_L_ (only the profile author, Shiwani Mandhania, was captured; the full author list and DOI were not verified. HD 107 appears as a parent in the abstract.)
Anonymous/CICR (year not captured). Cotton Varieties and Hybrids: technical bulletin. CICR -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf (lists HD 107 under Haryana; the bulletin's own year is not captured.)
Research-paper search for HD-107 trials, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses and QTL studies: No further evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
The AICCIP Hisar page states that male and female parental seed of HD-107 can be obtained from CCS HAU, Hisar. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
The Seednet seed-producers listing returned cotton companies and their varieties (for example, HCH-279, JKCH-99, MECH-12), none of them HD-107. -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Seed_Producers_Marketers.htm
No private dealer or State Seed Corporation listing for HD-107 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Haryana. The CICR bulletin's variety table lists HD 107 under the Haryana heading. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
Note: the Seednet "recommended_states_raw" field reads "Unknown". The Haryana entry is from the CICR bulletin, not the Seednet record.

RECORD DISCREPANCIES TO RESOLVE
1. Release year: the Seednet/CSC value is 1995, which matches the AICCIP statement that HD 107 was released in 1995. The CICR table shows 1996.
2. Parentage: Seednet says local germplasm; AICCIP says DS-5 x HD 266.
3. Crop taxonomy: the CICR bulletin groups HD 107 with the "latter" set of varieties, but the snippet does not state the species explicitly, so the species category is not confirmed here.

pest_resistance.summary: Jassid (leafhopper): resistant, as reported for the hybrid in the Vidarbha region. The original CSC record describes it as moderately resistant to jassids and moderately susceptible to bollworm (no source URL in digest). A bollworm economic threshold of 5 per cent injury was reported for 'AHH 468' at pdkv.ac.in, but the name lacks the C prefix, so this is not attributed to this hybrid. Susceptibility to insect pests noted in the Vikaspedia source applies to CGMS-based hybrids in general and is not attributed to this hybrid.

Sources conflict on relative yield: one source states 10-15 per cent higher yield than conventional hybrids; the CICR bulletin states 10-15 per cent lower yield than a conventional hybrid developed from the same parents. The CICR table numeric yield columns are unlabelled, so no yield figure is reported from it.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-location trial results for this hybrid were found, so stability across environments is not established.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra; the CICR table also lists Marathwada. agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location trial results found. Rainfed recommendation for CAHH 468: sowing at 60 x 90 cm with 50:25:25 kg/ha NPK (pdkv.ac.in). Yield comparison: one source reports 10-15 per cent higher yield than conventional hybrids, while the CICR bulletin reports 10-15 per cent lower yield than a conventional hybrid from the same parents. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PKV-HYB-3 (CAHH-468) -- Cotton. Variety name and Seednet name are the same ("PKV-HYB-3 (CAHH-468)"). Across the sources the hybrid also appears as "PKV Hy 3", "PKV Hy-3", "PKV Hy3" and "CAHH 468". The release year is 1993 in the CSC record. Every finding below was matched to this hybrid by one of those names.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Only jassid (leafhopper) resistance is reported; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this hybrid. The search returned general Indian cotton germplasm text (https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/46828), which does not name this hybrid for stress tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to jassids, and the hybrid is described as resistant to jassids in the Vidarbha region. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655
- Bollworm economic threshold was worked out at 5 per cent injury on "AHH 468". The name is printed without the C prefix, so it is probably this hybrid but is not certain. -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- Susceptibility to insect pests is noted for CGMS-based hybrids in general, not specifically for this hybrid. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed recommendation for CAHH 468: sowing at 60 x 90 cm with 50:25:25 kg/ha NPK. -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211 (also https://pdkv.ac.in/?paged=2&s=result&x=0&y=0)
- Yield claims conflict. One source says the hybrid gives 10-15 per cent higher yield than conventional hybrids. The CICR bulletin says its yield is 10-15 per cent lower than a conventional hybrid developed from the same parents. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655 ; https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- The CICR variety table has a row for PKV Hy-3 (HH type, 1994, Marathwada). Its numeric columns are not labelled in the extract, so no yield figure is reported here. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- Maturity: a comparison source says PKV Hy 4 matures 15 days earlier (165 days) than PKV Hy 3. This implies PKV Hy 3 matures around 180 days, but no direct maturity figure was found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655
- No multi-location trial results for this hybrid were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: CAK 32 x DHY 286-1R. The CAK 32 line is the male-sterile (A) parent. DHY 286-1R is the restorer (R) parent. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655 ; https://agriarticles.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/E-02-02-21-73-75.pdf
- The maintainer AK-32B named in the CSC record was not found in any source. The sources give only CAK 32 x DHY 286-1R.
- Breeding method: first CGMS-based intra-hirsutum hybrid, cytoplasmic genic male sterility system. -- https://agriarticles.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/E-02-02-21-73-75.pdf
- Fertility restoration came from G. harknessii cytoplasmic male sterility with restorer gene sources. -- https://agriarticles.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/E-02-02-21-73-75.pdf
- The G. harknessii fertility gene was transferred into Indian genotypes and used for PKV Hyb-3. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/46828
- Breeding-line code: CAHH 468 (CAHH = intra-hirsutum hybrid code in the CICR table). -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- Genome resources, QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Cotton Research Station (later Cotton Research Unit) of Punjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth (PDKV), Akola, released in 1993. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf

drought.details: The digest reports no drought-specific data for PKV Rajat. Searches returned only rainfed and drip planting results. The original CSC record lists the variety as tolerant to drought under agronomic features, but this is not corroborated by the evidence digest.

salinity.details: The AICCIP Akola page reports PKV Rajat as tolerant to saline soils and widely grown in the saline tract of Vidarbha (Maharashtra). Released 1994 per that source. The digest gives no quantitative salinity data, and the level reflects a single qualitative report.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no flood data for PKV Rajat.

disease_resistance.summary: Grey mildew: in an artificially inoculated trial, yield loss was 10.17% for PKV Rajat, compared with 19.64% for PKV Hy 2 and 63.17% for AKH 4 (the highest-loss entry). This indicates comparatively lower loss, but no formal resistance rating is given. Alternaria leaf blight: rated Moderately Susceptible (MS) in a screen using seed from Cotton Research Unit, Akola. Bacterial blight: incidence did not differ across the 60x60, 60x30 and 90x20 cm spacings tested, but no resistance rating is given. The original CSC record states moderately resistant to bacterial blight; this is not verified by the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No insect-resistance rating specific to PKV Rajat was found in the digest. The CSC record states moderately resistant to jassids and bollworm, but this is not verified by the digest. The Maharashtra package-of-practices resistance table was not used because the Rajat column could not be clearly identified.

agronomic_details.yield: No verified numeric seed cotton yield for PKV Rajat was found in the digest. The CSC record gives an average yield of 1200.00 to 1500.00 Kg/Ha, which is not verified by the digest. The CICR bulletin Rajat row has unlabelled numeric columns that were not interpreted as yield.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for the cotton growing tract of Vidarbha under rainfed conditions (CSC record). The digest supports a rainfed Akola recommendation for medium-deep soils and reports wide cultivation in the saline tract of Vidarbha.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: GINNING % : 38-39% ; 2.5% SPAN LENGTH (MM) : 24-25 ; MICRONSIRE VALUE : 4.5 ; UNIFORMITY RATIO % : 49 ; FIBRE STRENGTH(G/TEX) : 45.9 ; MATURITY EFFICIENT ; 0.77. (Lodging: non-lodging, per CSC record.)
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Artificially inoculated grey mildew trial: 10.17% yield loss for PKV Rajat vs 19.64% for PKV Hy 2 and 63.17% for AKH 4. (2) Alternaria leaf blight screen: Moderately Susceptible. (3) Spacing trial: bacterial blight incidence did not differ across 60x60, 60x30 and 90x20 cm. (4) Recommended spacing 60 x 30 cm with 50:25:0 kg/ha NPK for seed cotton yield; under drip, 96 x 30 cm for mechanical cultivation. (5) Intercropping: sole cotton gave the highest seed cotton yield; intercropping with black gram, green gram or soybean reduced yield by 9.3%, 24.6% and 50.5% respectively; gross returns were higher for cotton + green gram and cotton + black gram than sole cotton. (6) Manual detopping at flowering gave yield statistically similar to no detopping under rainfed conditions. (7) Seed rate of 10-12 kg/ha at 60 x 30 cm in the Maharashtra approved package of practices. (8) Rainfed Akola trial: AKH 84635 intercropped with greengram (Kopergaon) at 1:1 row ratio on medium-deep soils. (9) Drip-irrigated plant population study (Wankhade et al., 2002): effect on growth and yield under drip irrigation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Reported as tolerant to saline soils and widely grown in the saline tract of Vidarbha, released 1994 -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Akola.html
- Searches did not find drought or heat, flood, or submergence data specific to PKV Rajat. Results cover rainfed and drip planting only. -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211

DISEASE AND PEST
- In artificially inoculated trials, grey mildew yield loss was 10.17% for PKV Rajat, against 19.64% for PKV Hy 2 and 63.17% for AKH 4 (AKH 4 was the highest-loss entry in that trial). -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- In a Alternaria leaf blight screen, PKV Rajat was rated Moderately Susceptible (MS), with seed from Cotton Research Unit, Akola. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2019/vol7issue5/PartZ/7-5-23-807.pdf
- Bacterial blight incidence did not differ across the 60x60, 60x30 and 90x20 cm spacings tested on PKV Rajat. -- https://pdkv.ac.in/?paged=2&s=result&x=0&y=0
- No insect-resistance rating specific to PKV Rajat was found. The Maharashtra package-of-practices table with resistance columns does not clearly identify the Rajat column, so I did not use it. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/practices-for-maharastra.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Recommended spacing of 60 x 30 cm with 50:25:0 kg/ha NPK for seed cotton yield (Hirsutum variety PKV Rajat, AKH 84635) -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- Under drip irrigation, a 96 x 30 cm spacing is recommended for mechanical cultivation -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- Sole cotton gave the highest seed cotton yield. Intercropping with black gram, green gram or soybean reduced yield by 9.3%, 24.6% and 50.5% respectively. Gross monetary returns were higher in cotton + green gram and cotton + black gram than in sole cotton -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- Manual detopping at flowering gave yield statistically similar to no detopping under rainfed conditions -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- Seed rate of 10-12 kg/ha at 60 x 30 cm for PKV RAJAT in the Maharashtra approved package of practices -- https://pdf4pro.com/view/approved-package-of-practices-for-cotton-maharashtra-state-42dea4.html
- Rainfed Akola district trial recommendation for medium-deep soils: AKH 84635 intercropped with greengram (Kopergaon) at 1:1 row ratio -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/assets/img/Books/2004-05/Cotton.pdf
- Drip-irrigated plant population study on PKV Rajat (2002) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390912608_A_comprehensive_analysis_of_agronomic_practices_for_cultivation_of_cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_L
- Seed cotton yield figure: no verified numeric yield for PKV Rajat was found in the search results. The CICR technical bulletin table has a Rajat row (1994, Vidarbha) with unlabelled numeric columns, so I did not interpret them as yield. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Name check: the CSC minutes name is "PKV Rajat (AKH-84635)" and the Seednet name is "PKV RAJAT (AKH-84635)". The PDKV pages use "PKV Rajat (AKH 84635)", so the evidence refers to this variety. No Seednet portal page was returned.
- Parentage: the AICCIP page gives PKV-RAJAT as (AC-938 X SRT-1) X G. anomalum/thurberi-type wild-species derivative, which differs from the record's "AC-983". The wild-species name is garbled in the source. -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Akola.html
- Breeding line code: AKH 84635 is the line code used in PDKV combining-ability and heterosis work -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-10-2018/H.B.%20Kumbhalkar,%20et%20al.pdf
- Cytoplasmic male sterility: the CMS line CAK-84635 A (PKV Rajat) and its maintainer AK-84635 B are registered with NBPGR as a genotype with G. aridum cytoplasm (registration INGR No. 04046; IC-296639 and IC-296640) -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- Breeding method: the PDKV Akola programme developed an alternate CMS source using G. aridum in tetraploid cotton -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Akola.html
- No QTL, marker, or genome-resource study for PKV Rajat was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth (PDKV), Akola -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/Circulars/Recom-2020English.pdf
- Released by the AICCIP centre at Akola, with the Cotton Research Unit, Akola, handling nucleus and breeder seed production of varieties and hybrid parents -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211
- A Bt-converted version, "Rajat BT" (ICAR-CICR with PDKV), was accepted at national level at Joint AGRESCO 2020. This is a separate entity from PKV Rajat. -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/Circulars/Recom-2020English.pdf
