PA-183 (Cotton) evidence digest

Name check: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "PA-183", so the evidence below refers to the same name under both headings. The VNMKV page also lists it as "PA-183 (Sawata)" and "PA 183 [Sawta]". Four searches were run. No Seednet portal page was found, so nothing below is verified against Seednet.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for PA-183 (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence).

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for PA-183.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The CICR technical bulletin lists a "PA 183" row with release year 1996 and the value set 18 / 180 / 39 / 27 / 35 for Marathwada region. The extracted text has no column headers, so the meaning of each number cannot be confirmed; it should not be read as yield or maturity without the original table. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- The same bulletin says PA 183 is among the currently cultivated Maharashtra varieties, listed under G. arboreum. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- Plant Authority's annual report lists PA 183 among varieties under DUS testing for the South zone. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/eannual-report-15-16.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage and breeding history (three-way cross NA-39 x (C-C-1-1-3 x Lohit), dwarf selection, F2 to F6 pedigree selection 1983-89) come only from the brief supplied with the task. No external source was found to confirm it.
- The species assignment is unresolved. The parentage above suggests a hirsutum-type background, but the CICR bulletin lists PA 183 under G. arboreum and the VNMKV page calls it desi cotton. This should be checked against the release notification.
- No QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is listed on the VNMKV (Marathwada Agricultural University, Parbhani) "Variety Released" page. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_VarietyReleased.php
- The institution named in the brief is the Cotton Breeder, Cotton Research Station, Mahboob Baugh Farm, M.A.U., Parbhani. The Genesys entry for the Cotton Research Station at Mahboob Baugh Farm, Parbhani was returned but its text was not checked for PA-183. -- https://www.genesys-pgr.org/wiews/IND1049
- No lead breeder name was found for PA-183.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone, or postal address was found for PA-183.
- No institute-level contact page for the Cotton Research Station, Mahboob Baugh Farm was retrieved in these searches. The VNMKV variety-release page was found, but it contains no contact details in the text returned.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches for PA-183 papers, theses, and AICRP reports returned no items naming this variety. The Journal of Cotton Science result matched only the page-number string "167-183" and is unrelated.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The search for seed sources (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, dealers) returned only unrelated Marathwada dealer and Bt-cotton pages. No Seednet listing or current seed source was confirmed.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The CICR bulletin gives the region for PA 183 as "Marathwada region", which is within Maharashtra. This conflicts with the "Unknown" value in the supplied record, which should be updated. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf

Open items for follow-up: check the Seednet record (code A0501018) directly; obtain the CSC release notification for species, yield, and maturity; and contact the Cotton Research Station, Mahboob Baugh Farm, M.A.U., Parbhani for breeder details, since no contact was found online.

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest for drought tolerance specific to the non-Bt RCH-2 hybrid. The variety record states the hybrid is eminently adapted to extremes of climatic conditions such as drought, high rainfall and floods; this is a record-supplied claim that the digest did not verify, so no level is assigned. The Adilabad rainfed trial (Bt hybrid RCH-2) is a yield result under rainfed conditions and is not evidence of drought tolerance for the non-Bt hybrid.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance specific to the non-Bt RCH-2 hybrid. The variety record states adaptation to floods and high rainfall; this is a record-supplied claim not verified by any search result.

disease_resistance.summary: Non-Bt RCH-2 disease resistance: Not found in searched sources. The digest's only disease-related finding concerns the Bt derivative RCH 2 Bt (cry1Ac transgene), which is a different product and is not attributed to this variety. Variety record (not verified by the digest) lists: susceptible to grey mildew; moderately resistant to bacterial blight; alternaria and leaf spot moderately susceptible.

pest_resistance.summary: Non-Bt RCH-2 pest resistance: Not found in searched sources. Variety record (not verified by the digest) lists: moderately susceptible to jassid. Pest reaction field in the record is 'Unknown'.

(2) Rainfed trial at ARS Adilabad (Northern Telangana), 2006-07 and 2007-08, on the Bt hybrid RCH-2: maximum seed cotton yield 2278 kg/ha at 27,777 plants/ha; 2386 kg/ha with five-split nitrogen starting at 15 DAS. (3) Review of Bt cotton agronomy in India mentions RCH 2 Bt in nitrogen-use-efficiency and winter-irrigated southern-zone trials; the extracted text is fragmentary and gives no figures. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RCH-2 (Cotton, Gossypium hirsutum hybrid)

Name note: The CSC release name (variety_name) and the Seednet name (seednet_variety_name) are both "RCH-2", so one search covered both. The evidence found refers to the RCH 2 non-Bt hybrid only indirectly, through its Bt derivative RCH 2 Bt, and through Rasi's own product pages. I ran four searches. I did not query the Seednet portal, the CSC release minutes, KrishiKosh, or ICAR/AICCIP reports directly, so "No evidence found" under a heading means only that these four searches did not turn it up.

STRESS TOLERANCE (RCH-2 name)
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to the non-Bt RCH-2 hybrid. The only hits were for other RCH products, which I discarded. Searched: RCH-2 variety release/notification query.

DISEASE AND PEST (RCH-2 name; applies to the Bt derivative only)
- The Bt derivative RCH 2 Bt carries the cry1Ac transgene (MON 531 event), per the GEAC approved-products list. -- https://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf (also http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf)
- Non-Bt RCH-2 pest or disease resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (RCH-2 name)
- GEAC records that earlier trials of the RCH 2 hybrid gave appreciably higher seed cotton yield than a set of controlled cotton cultivars, consistently. -- https://archive.pib.gov.in/release02/lyr2003/rjun2003/13062003/r1306200317.html
- A rainfed trial at ARS Adilabad (Northern Telangana, 2006–07 and 2007–08) on Bt hybrid RCH-2 reported a maximum seed cotton yield of 2278 kg/ha at 27,777 plants/ha, and 2386 kg/ha with five-split nitrogen starting at 15 DAS. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/cr1-44-1and2-038
- A review of Bt cotton agronomy in India mentions RCH 2 Bt in N-use-efficiency and winter-irrigated southern-zone trials, but the extracted text is fragmentary and gives no figures. -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/4809/4484
- Rasi's product page says the company launched RCH 1 and RCH 2 in 1992 and describes RCH 2 as remarkable in farmers' fields. This date conflicts with the 1999 AICCIP release date above. -- http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage RC91A x RC 86R: supplied in the variety record only; not confirmed by any search result.
- RCH 2 Bt is described as a direct derivative of the released non-Bt RCH 2 hybrid, i.e., a transgenic (Bt) form of the same hybrid. -- https://archive.pib.gov.in/release02/lyr2003/rjun2003/13062003/r1306200317.html
- Breeding method, breeding-line codes, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (RCH-2 name)
- Developing institution per the record and the GEAC/Rasi sources: Rasi Seeds Company Ltd. (Rasi Seeds Pvt. Ltd. in later listings). -- http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html
- Named breeder for RCH-2: No evidence found. The Wikipedia page on Rajagopalan Krishnamurthy lists him as Research Director – Cotton of Rasi Seeds, but no source links him to RCH-2, so I have not attributed it to him. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajagopalan_Krishnamurthy
- Other breeder names in results (e.g., Kaderbad Ravindranath) relate to other varieties and are excluded.

CONTACT DETAILS (RCH-2 name; institute-level only)
- Institution address as supplied in the variety record (not verified by a search result): RASI SEEDS COMPANY LTD., P.BOX NO. 30273 KAMARAJANAR ROAD, ATTUR-636102, SALEM (DT), TAMILNADU.
- Company website: http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html
- Named breeder contact, email, phone: No evidence found.
- Official institute contact page URL: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS (RCH-2 name)
- Sree Rekha, M.; Pradeep, T. (2012). Performance of Bt cotton hybrid (RCH-2) at different plant densities and scheduling of nitrogen under rainfed conditions. Crop Research (journal name inferred from the source's volume/issue code "cr1-44-1and2"; verify) 44(1&2): 182–185. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/cr1-44-1and2-038 (also listed as ResearchGate: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324528853_Performance_of_Bt_Cotton_hybrid_RCH-2_at_different_plant_densities_and_scheduling_of_nitrogen_under_rainfed_conditions)
- Government Press Information Bureau (2003). GEAC gives its approval for large-scale trial of RCH 2 Bt cotton. PIB release -- https://archive.pib.gov.in/release02/lyr2003/rjun2003/13062003/r1306200317.html
- Journal/report on the non-Bt RCH-2 release (AICCIP): No evidence found. KrishiKosh and AICRP report searches were not run.

SEED AVAILABILITY (RCH-2 name; Bt derivative)
- GEAC approved Rasi's RCH 2 Bt for commercial seed production, and the 2004 Business Standard report says Rasi could sell RCH2 Bt seed in six states. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/rasi-can-sell-bt-cotton-seeds-104040501092_1.html
- GEAC yearwise list places RCH 2 Bt (Rasi Seeds, cry1Ac, MON 531) in the 2005 list. -- https://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf
- Current dealer or NSC/SSC/KVK/SAU listing for the non-Bt RCH-2: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES (RCH-2 name; Bt derivative)
- The GEAC list assigns RCH 2 Bt to the Central and South zones. -- https://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf
- The Rasi product table lists RCH 2 Bt for central rainfed and irrigated tracts. -- http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html
- Official recommended states for the non-Bt RCH-2 (CSC notification): No evidence found. The variety record lists "Unknown."

EXCLUDED RESULTS (not this variety)
- RCH 2 BG II (a separate BG II product, with its own states and cry1Ac/cry2Ab genes), RCH 659, RCH 386, RCH 668, RCH 317, RCH 20, RCH 138, RCH 134, RCH 2 BG II on indiamart and agribegri, and the Telangana-linked RCH-2 pages are excluded or noted only where they name the RCH 2 Bt hybrid directly.
- Non-cotton and other-variety pages (SVPR, RH-668, RH-647, FiBL organic varieties, Academia, Journal of Cotton Research, arXiv) were discarded.

The search tool stopped working partway through, so this digest is thin. My four searches ran in one batch: "L-604 Cotton variety", "L-604 Cotton breeder institute", "L-604 Cotton research paper", and "L-604 cotton seed availability". A follow-up pass to check the page contents was blocked by the tool limit. Findings below come only from the titles and short snippets I saw, so treat them as unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page that names L-604 with a stress-tolerance trait.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The CICR technical bulletin on cotton varieties and hybrids (https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf) came up, but the snippet I read did not mention L-604, so I have excluded it.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Title-level evidence only: a ResearchGate paper, "Identification of donor parents containing favourable alleles for improving target American cotton hybrid (NA 1325 × L 604)", indicates that L 604 is used as a parent line in cotton hybrid breeding -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325111656_Identification_of_donor_parents_containing_favourable_alleles_for_improving_target_American_cotton_hybrid_NA_1325_x_L_604. I did not read the abstract, so I have no parentage, breeding-line code or method details. The parentage given in the record (MCU5 × (L389 × SRT 1)) is not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No page named a breeder or scientist for L-604. The ResearchGate paper's author list was not visible in the snippet.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No institute page or breeder contact was returned. The institution in the record, Principal Scientist (Cotton), R.A.R.S., Lam, Guntur-34, is taken from the input only and not verified.

PUBLICATIONS -- Partial: Authors not visible (see title). (Year not visible). "Identification of donor parents containing favourable alleles for improving target American cotton hybrid (NA 1325 × L 604)". ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325111656_Identification_of_donor_parents_containing_favourable_alleles_for_improving_target_American_cotton_hybrid_NA_1325_x_L_604

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for L-604 was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record lists "Unknown", and no search result gave a state recommendation.

Notes:
- Name check: the variety name (L-604) and the Seednet name are the same, so no separate search was needed. The ResearchGate title writes it as "L 604", which is probably the same line but should be confirmed.
- The release year (1997) and parentage come from the input record only.
- Next steps: check the ResearchGate page for its authors and abstract, and look up the CICR bulletin and the Seednet entry for variety code A0501044 directly. KrishiKosh and the Lam (Guntur) RARS pages are also worth checking.

Most headings have no supporting evidence, so this digest is thin and should be re-run with a clean search budget before it goes into a reference record.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The "LAHH-4 (A 13) Cotton variety" search returned a USPTO patent document for an unrelated cotton variety (PX4444-13WRF), and nothing on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for LAHH-4. -- https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9743601

The column headings are not visible in the snippet, so the numbers cannot be reliably assigned to LAHH-4. Treat this as unverified. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/hybrid-cotton-present-status-and-future-prospects/253136852

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight: moderate resistance reported for CNH-120 MB in the high-density planting evaluation. Grey mildew: moderate resistance reported in the same paragraph. Attribution caveat: the source page does not name the line in that sentence, so the attribution is inferred from the same paragraph and should be checked against the full paper. The input record (not verified by the digest) states that the line is at par with local checks (LRA 5166) for disease reaction.

pest_resistance.summary: Bollworm (mean square damage): CNH-120 MB had the lowest mean square damage (2.76%) among the genotypes compared in a high-density planting trial. It was second only to PKV-081 (3.82%) in that comparison, and the two were statistically on par. The input record (not verified by the digest) states a higher level of bollworm resistance and tolerance to sucking pests. The digest does not report sucking-pest data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. None of the four searches returned a page that names Pratima (CNH 120 MB) with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. The only relevant hit was a 2020-era high-density planting paper, and it does not report stress tolerance for this line.

DISEASE AND PEST
CNH-120 MB had the lowest mean square damage (2.76%) among the genotypes compared in a high-density planting trial, second only in the same comparison to PKV-081 (3.82%), and the two were statistically on par. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347285247_High_Density_Planting_System_of_Cotton_in_India_Status_and_Breeding_Strategies (also https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172)
CNH-120 MB showed moderate resistance to bacterial blight and grey mildew in the high-density planting evaluation. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172 (The source text is the "It" passage. The page does not name the line in that sentence, so this attribution is inferred from the same paragraph and should be checked against the full paper.)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The high-density planting paper describes a G. hirsutum culture that matures in 125–135 days, has zero monopodia and short sympodial length, and averaged 2361 kg/ha seed cotton, 18.9% above the check Suraj. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172. The page does not clearly name this culture as CNH-120 MB, so these figures are NOT attributed to Pratima here.
Under the same high-density planting evaluation, the paper reports that the culture was fertilizer responsive at all locations. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172 (same caveat on identity)
CNH 120 MB was one of seven genotypes tested in a CICR Nagpur field evaluation of a cotton picker. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/47_20-02-2024.pdf (The extracted text does not give a clear per-variety result, so none is reported.)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "mutant of SRT-1 (EMS 1.5%)" -- No evidence found. This comes from the input record only. The EMS results from searches were about other cotton lines (for example, the Lian 2020 Plant Journal library, the TM-1 library, and the Gossypium barbadense library), so they were discarded.
No QTL, marker, or genome-resource study naming Pratima (CNH 120 MB) was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur. The CICR list of G. hirsutum varieties includes 'CNH 120 MB'. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140 and https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172 (the high-density paper credits CICR Nagpur for that programme).
Lead breeder or scientist: No evidence found. The breeder name was not on any retrieved page for this variety. The Rajagopalan Krishnamurthy page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajagopalan_Krishnamurthy) is about a different breeder and is not attributed to this variety.
Station: CICR Nagpur (headquarters). No station-level attribution was found.

Institute page cited by CICR's Wikipedia entry: https://cicr.org.in/about-us/about-cicr-mandate-duplicate-1/ (no contact details seen in the retrieved text).
Note: an indiaagronet notice for Kiran (CNH 36), another CICR variety, gives the CICR Nagpur postal code as 440 001, which differs from the 440010 in the input. -- https://indiaagronet.com/indiaagronet/technology_upd/contents/latest_notifications_of_crop_var.htm
No email or phone number was found for this variety or for CICR in the retrieved results.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). High Density Planting System of Cotton in India: Status and Breeding Strategies. Book chapter (IntechOpen) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/74172 (the same content also appears at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347285247_High_Density_Planting_System_of_Cotton_in_India_Status_and_Breeding_Strategies). This is the only retrieved publication that names CNH-120 MB in a trial context.

pest_resistance.summary: American bollworm: resistance reported in Nuziveedu's variety listing, which also reports a medium reaction to other major pests. The Bunny Bt version carries Cry1Ac (MON 531 event), which is a transgenic insect-resistance trait. A Farmonaut statement that NCS 145 resists bollworms and pink bollworm was excluded because it is a general statement, not a variety-specific finding. The BG II version (NCS 145 BG II) was excluded because it is a different product.

agronomic_details.yield: Bt NCS 145 gave 1930 kg/ha in a split-plot trial with 3 replications, compared with 1925 kg/ha for Ankur 09. In a comparative Bt trial, NCS-145 Bt gave 2685.1 kg/ha seed cotton versus 2335.3 kg/ha for DHH-11.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated and rainfed conditions and for soils with high moisture retention. The digest lists Central and South zones. The Scribd report gives a 2005 release date, which conflicts with the task record.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium maturity group, tall plant height, erect growth, and response to added fertilizers (Nuziveedu profile). The digest describes superior kapas quality and high ginning percentage for Bunny Bt.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) CRDA report: Bt NCS 145 split-plot trial, 3 replications, 1930 kg/ha versus Ankur 09 at 1925 kg/ha; location and season not given. (2) Comparative Bt trial (ResearchGate): NCS-145 Bt 2685.1 kg/ha seed cotton versus DHH-11 at 2335.3 kg/ha, with higher oil percentage; site and year not shown. (3) Rainfed heterosis trial at Cotton Research Station, Nanded (2018-19) used NCS 145 as a standard hybrid check; no yield result for this hybrid is given in the digest. (4) CRDA elevated CO2 study on Bunny Bt and non-Bt versions (seed development to 20 days after anthesis); no yield result is given. The phenology study on NCS-145 BG-II (greater leaf area index at 80, 110 and 140 days after sowing) was excluded because it concerns a different product.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NCS-145-Bunny (NCHH-145), Cotton
Name note: The CSC/PPV&FR order and compendium use "NCS-145 Bunny (NCHH-145)" (also "NCS-145 (NCHH-145) BUNNY" and "Bunny-NCS-145"). The Seednet-style name "NCS-145-BUNNY (NCHH-145)" appears in the WDRA seed-standard lists. Evidence below refers to this same hybrid under both spellings. Seednet itself was not searched directly. Searches run: 4.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bunny Bt and non-Bt versions were grown under elevated CO2 (650 ± 50 ppm) and studied for seed development up to 20 days after anthesis -- https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e5ece672.pdf
- Waterlogging effects were studied on Bt versions of Bunny, RCH-2, RCH-20 and Mallika; no tolerance rating was found in the snippet -- https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e5ece672.pdf
- Suitability: described as suitable for both irrigated and rainfed conditions and for soils with high moisture retention -- https://www.scribd.com/document/415992292/49461417-Nuziveedu-seeds-ltd-docx
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance rating was found for this variety specifically.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bt hybrid carrying Cry1Ac (MON 531 event) for Central and South zones -- http://wwwkisangangacom.weebly.com/cotton-varieties.html
- Nuziveedu's listing reports resistance to American bollworm and a medium reaction to other major pests -- http://nuziveedu-seeds.blogspot.com/2017/01/ncs-145-bunny.html
- Commercially approved list shows the BG II version (NCS 145 BG II) with Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab events for the North zone -- http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf
- Farmonaut describes NCS 145 as resistant to bollworms and pink bollworm, but this is a general statement, not a variety-specific trial -- https://farmonaut.com/asia/best-cotton-seed-in-maharashtra-telangana-2024-guide

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Field trial on Bt NCS 145 (split-plot, 3 replications) gave 1930 kg/ha, comparable to Ankur 09 (1925 kg/ha); location and season not given in snippet -- https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e5ece672.pdf
- Bunny Bt was described as high yielding, medium maturity, with superior kapas quality and high ginning percentage -- https://www.scribd.com/document/415992292/49461417-Nuziveedu-seeds-ltd-docx
- Nuziveedu's profile lists medium maturity group, tall plant height, erect growth, and response to added fertilizers -- http://nuziveedu-seeds.blogspot.com/2017/01/ncs-145-bunny.html
- Comparative Bt trial: NCS-145 Bt gave 2685.1 kg/ha seed cotton versus DHH-11 at 2335.3, with higher oil percentage; site and year not shown in snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264420149_Evaluation_of_commercially_available_Bt_cotton_genotypes_for_their_agronomic_performance_and_economic_returns
- Crop phenology study: NCS-145 BG-II had greater leaf area index at 80, 110 and 140 days after sowing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277352568_Crop_phenology_thermal_requirement_yield_and_fiber_properties_of_cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_genotypes_as_influenced_by_different_environments
- Rainfed heterosis trial at Cotton Research Station, Nanded (2018-19) used NCS 145 as a standard hybrid check; this is a different experiment on the same hybrid -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/8%20Heterosis%20Studies%20of%20Newly%20developed%20intra-hirsutum%20Cotton%20Hybrids%20for%20Seed%20Cotton%20and%20Lint%20Yield%20and%20their%20Performance%20for%20Economic,%20Morphological%20and%20Fibre%20Quality%20Traits%20under%20Rainfed%20K.S.%20Baig.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage NC 71 x NC 99 was not confirmed by any search result.
- Breeding-line codes, breeding method, and QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.
- Transgenic events: Cry1Ac (MON 531) in the Bunny Bt version; Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab (MON 15985) in the BG II version (NCS 145 BG II) -- sources listed under DISEASE AND PEST.
- Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Registered breeder recorded as Nuziveedu Seeds Limited in the PPV&FR revocation order, which concerns a dispute between Bioseeds Research India Limited and Nuziveedu over the BUNNY-NCS-145 registration -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/orderdated08.01.2020passedbyld.chairpersoninbunnyncs-145.pdf
- Scribd Nuziveedu report says the hybrid was developed by Nuziveedu Seeds Limited -- https://www.scribd.com/document/415992292/49461417-Nuziveedu-seeds-ltd-docx
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Public-sector institute involvement: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level contact from the task record (not verified by search): Nuziveedu Seeds Limited, Subeej House, 6/12, Brodipet, Guntur-522002.
- Email, phone, breeder contact, and institute contact page: No evidence found.
- A Nuziveedu Seeds Ltd listing in Dudyala (Survey No. 161, Baba Nagar, Kurnool district area) appears on JustDial -- https://www.justdial.com/jdmart/Kurnool/Nuziveedu-Seeds-Ltd-Survey-No-161-Baba-Nagar-Dudyala/9999P8518-8518-210316160141-L5Q3_BZDET/catalogue

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in search result (n.d.). Evaluation of commercially available Bt cotton genotypes for their agronomic performance and economic returns. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264420149_Evaluation_of_commercially_available_Bt_cotton_genotypes_for_their_agronomic_performance_and_economic_returns
- Authors not shown in search result (n.d.). Crop phenology, thermal requirement, yield and fiber properties of cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) genotypes as influenced by different environments. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277352568_Crop_phenology_thermal_requirement_yield_and_fiber_properties_of_cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_genotypes_as_influenced_by_different_environments
- Authors and year not shown (CRDA report on Bt cotton hybrid trials, including NCS 145) -- https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e5ece672.pdf
- Authors not shown in search result (n.d.). Heterosis studies of newly developed intra-hirsutum cotton hybrids under rainfed conditions (K.S. Baig; Cotton Research Station, Nanded). Bioscience Biotechnology Research/BFIJ -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/8%20Heterosis%20Studies%20of%20Newly%20developed%20intra-hirsutum%20Cotton%20Hybrids%20for%20Seed%20Cotton%20and%20Lint%20Yield%20and%20their%20Performance%20for%20Economic,%20Morphological%20and%20Fibre%20Quality%20Traits%20under%20Rainfed%20K.S.%20Baig.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR reports, and DOIs: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Listed as a notified cotton variety on the WDRA seed-standard lists, under NCS-145-BUNNY (NCHH-145) -- https://wdra.gov.in/web/wdra/cotton-seeds
- Retail listing: Nuziveedu Bunny NCS 145 BT-2 hybrid cotton seed, 475 g packet, Rs 740, from Elfaagri Services, Bhilwara, Rajasthan -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nuziveedu-bunny-ncs-145-bt-2-hybrid-cotton-seeds-23368398862.html
- Online listing of Nuziveedu BUNNY NCS 145 Bt-2 (475 g) -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nuziveedu-cotton-seeds-online--buy-cotton-seeds-online-india.php
- Listed among popular hybrids in a cotton seed production article -- https://allaboutagriculture.in/blogs/cash-crop/cotton-seed-production-technology/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Central and South zones, per the Scribd Nuziveedu report (released 2005) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/415992292/49461417-Nuziveedu-seeds-ltd-docx
- Central and South zones for the Cry1Ac version -- http://wwwkisangangacom.weebly.com/cotton-varieties.html
- Central zone listed for NCS-145 Bt 2 in the GEAC approved list -- http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf
- North zone listed for the NCS 145 BG II version in the same GEAC list -- http://www.geacindia.gov.in/resource-documents/approved-products/Final_commercially_approved.pdf
- Official SAU or CSC state recommendation notifications: No evidence found.

RECORD CONFLICTS
- Release year: The task record says 2001. The Nuziveedu report says 2005. The PPV&FR registration certificates were first issued in 2009. The 2001 date is not confirmed.
- Recommended states in the record are "Unknown". The sources above give Central and South zones.
- Ownership: The PPV&FR order records a dispute over this registration between Bioseeds and Nuziveedu. Treat the registration status as contested until checked against PPV&FR records.

drought.details: Described as resistant to lodging and drought, with escape from bollworms through early maturing habit. The sources give no graded rating, so 'medium' is a qualitative assignment. Mechanisms beyond early maturity and resistance to lodging are not described.

heat.details: No evidence found. Searches returned only generic cotton heat papers that do not name DS-1.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in DS-1.

disease_resistance.summary: Highly resistant to bacterial blight (black arm). Evidence: HAU source states highly resistant to black arm (bacterial blight); AICCIP source states highly resistant to bacterial blights. No DS-1 evidence found for resistance to wilt or other diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: Highly resistant to jassids (leafhoppers). Moderately resistant to spotted bollworm and pink bollworm, as recorded in the CSC pest reaction field (no digest URL supports this rating). Bollworm damage is avoided mainly through early maturity. No DS-1 evidence found for whitefly or Helicoverpa-specific resistance.

Kapas sheds on boll opening if not picked in time, though less than the control G 27 (CSC record).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DS-1 (variety_name) and DS-1 (seednet_variety_name) are identical, so every finding below refers to the same name. Each finding is tied to a page that names DS-1 with cotton/Gossypium context.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Crop is resistant to lodging and drought, escapes from bollworms due to early maturing habits. -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- The same drought and lodging tolerance is listed for DS-1 in Crop is resistant to lodging and drought, escapes from bollworms due to early maturing habits. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned only generic cotton drought, salinity and heat papers that do not name DS-1.

DISEASE AND PEST
- It is highly resistant to leaf hopper and bacterial blight. -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- It is highly resistant to jassids and bacterial blights. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
- Bollworm response is recorded as early maturity that avoids bollworm damage, as stated at the drought line above (hau.ac.in PDF, 2-12; AICCIP 1-15). No DS-1 evidence on resistance to whitefly, wilt, or Helicoverpa-specific resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DS-1 plant height and growth habit: It is tall growing (150-190 cm) and has tendency to go taller in humid and fertile soil conditions. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
- Yield: Mean seed cotton yield is 22 quintals per hectares. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
- Fibre: Its fibre is coarse and short, not suitable for mill consumption, however it is quite suitable for domestic use, medical dressing and for the non-spinning purpose. -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Sowing and picking window: the AICCIP page lists a April sowing for a variety whose female and male parent are given; this is ambiguous and not attributed to DS-1. No confirmed DS-1 sowing date or maturity-days figure was found (CSC maturity field is not verified).
- Multi-location or field-trial results for DS-1: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Desi cotton variety DS-1, developed through mutation breeding (gamma Radiation) from variety G 27 and was released in 1983. -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
- The CSC record gives the parentage as gamma radiation of G-27. This matches the AICCIP and Sirsa sources above.
- Species: DS-1 is a G. arboreum (desi) cotton, per Cotton varieties ( G. arboreum L.) DS-1 -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
- Breeding line codes, QTL, markers, and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing station: DS-1 and DS-5 (Female parent of Hybrid AAH-1) and two American cotton varieties HS 45 and HS6 has been developed at this station and released for general cultivation in Haryana State. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20
- Station location conflict: the CSC record says Cotton Research Station, Hisar, while the HAU sources place the developing station at Sirsa. The Cotton Research Station, Sirsa is located in the Western Haryana, This station was established in April 1956 as a fodder research station and was transferred to CCS HAU in 1976 under Integrated Cotton Development Project (Funded by World Bank). -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20
- Release year conflict: the CSC record says 1985. The AICCIP page gives 1983 (http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html, 1-10). The HAU Sirsa PDF gives 1985 (https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf, 2-9). The CICR bulletin gives 1984 (https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf, 14-12).
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. No pages name the breeder or scientist who developed DS-1.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level contact (AICCIP cotton, CCS HAU Hisar; not a DS-1 breeder contact): Scientist (Cotton) Chowdhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar - 125 001 HARYANA Phone no: 01662-231171, 231172(O) 236082(R) Fax no:01662-234952 01662-234613 Email : hisar\_aiccip@yahoo.com -- http://aiccip.cicr.org.in/Hisar.html
- Sirsa station postal address or phone: No evidence found.
- Official HAU homepage: https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The search returned papers that do not name DS-1, including gamma-ray cotton mutagenesis work by Mehetre, Patil and Dahat (1998) on a branching mutant of G. hirsutum, and Khatod et al. (2002) on naturally coloured cotton. These are not about DS-1 and are excluded.
- Mandatory searches for KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports, and conference papers naming DS-1: none returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for DS-1 seed from NSC, the Haryana State Seed Corporation, KVKs, or the SAU seed sales. The search returned generic dealer listings for "desi cotton seed" that do not name DS-1, such as https://www.tradeindia.com/products/desi-cotton-seed-c2849824.html. These are excluded.
- Possible lead (unverified): the AICCIP page says Its male and female can be obtained from CCS HAU, Hisar. The sentence is adjacent to a different variety's parentage line, so it may refer to the hybrid rather than DS-1. Verify with CCS HAU before use.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Haryana: released for general cultivation in Haryana State -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20
- The CICR bulletin table lists DS 1 with Haryana in the state column -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- The CSC field "Unknown" should be updated to Haryana, subject to the verification noted above.

seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: PLANT ARE ERECT-GROWING SEMI-SYMPODIAL BUT LESS VEGETATIVE (0-3 MONOPODIA) AND CARRIES MORE FRUITING BRANCHES (8-18) ON THE MAIN STEM. ITS LEAVES ARE MEDIUM BROAD WITH 3-5 LOBES AND POLLEN AND FLOWER COLOURS ARE CREAMY ITS BOLLS HAVE FOUR TO FIVE LOCULI WITH AVERAGE BOLL WEIGHT OF ABOUT 3.2 GM. THE BOLL OPENING IS SYNCHRONOUS AND MATURITY IS ABOUT 145-155 DAYS. ITS SEED INDEX IS 7-8 GM.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: THIS NEW VARIETY OF AMERICAN COTTON IS SEMI-SYMPODIAL IN ITS HABIT OF GROWTH IT MATURES EARLIER THAN PRAMUKH BY ABOUT 15 DAYS. THE OPTIMUM PLANTING OF AMERICAN COTTON IS LAST WEEK OF APRIL IN UTTAR PRADESH. HOWEVER, COTTON SOWINGS GET DELAYED DUE TO SCARCE AVAILABILITY OF WATER AND LATE HARVEST OF WHEAT. BY VIRTUE OF ITS EARLIER MATURITY, IT CAN BE PLANTED UP TO MID OF JUNE AND THE ENTIRE CROP FINISHES OFF BY THE MID OF NOVEMBER AND PERMITS TIMELY WHET CULTIVATION. IT IS DISTINCTLY SUPERIOR TO PRAMUKH. IN KAPAS YIELD AND GINNING OUTTURN. IT GIVE 28% HIGHER KAPAS YIELD THAN PRAMUKH. ON AN AVERAGE AND ITS MATURITY IS MORE UNIFORM. IT IS ALSO MORE TOLERANT TO INSECT PESTS AND DISEASES. IN EARLINESS, YIELD, FIBRE QUALITIES AND RESISTANCE, IT IS PAR WITH H777 AND SH131. THE MEAN FIBRE LENGTH OF VIKAS IS 23.4 MM AND GINNING PERCENTAGE IS 34.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
MECH-4 (Cotton) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "MECH-4", so every finding below refers to that one name. Four searches were run: variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, and seed availability. The searches returned no official Seednet, CSC, ICAR, SAU, or institute page for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The variety/release search returned only cotton fibre price pages and no stress-tolerance data for MECH-4.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. None of the returned pages reported disease or pest resistance for MECH-4.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for MECH-4 were returned.

GENETICS AND QTL: Partial evidence only. The parentage (female 601 cytoplasmic male sterile x male C-219 fertility restorer) comes from the supplied record, not from search results. A Vikaspedia hybrid cotton seed production document describes MECH 4 as a private-sector hybrid, and notes that hybrids built on cytoplasmic male sterility were a major route to commercial cotton hybrids in India. It does not confirm the 601 x C-219 parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, or genome resources. -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-cotton-seed-production.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Partial evidence only. The Vikaspedia document (above) places MECH 4 in the private sector, which is consistent with the supplied institution but does not name a breeder or scientist. The supplied record gives the institution as Research Division, Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds Company Ltd., Jalna - 431 203 (Mah.). No search result named a lead breeder for MECH-4. Wikipedia's Mahyco page and news items about Mahyco's Bt cotton were found, but they do not name MECH-4, so they were excluded.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No official email, phone, or contact page for the Research Division or the company was returned that names MECH-4. The only address on record is the supplied one: Research Division, Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds Company Ltd., Jalna - 431 203 (Mah.). It was not verified by search.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming MECH-4 was returned. The "MECH-4 cotton research paper" search returned a cotton harvesting review (PMC12058488) with no mention of MECH-4, so it was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: Partial evidence only. A commodity market page lists MECH-4 as a cotton variety with market prices (about 5,365 INR per quintal in its latest summary). This shows trade listing, not seed sales by NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or a dealer. -- https://www.commodityinsightsx.com/commodities/mandi-prices/cotton/mech-4/latest-market-price

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in search results. The supplied CSC record lists Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan. The raw field repeats these three states twice, so the duplicated entry should be cleaned up. These states come from the input record and are not verified.

EXCLUDED RESULTS (name resemblance only): "ICF Mech-I/H-4 (Madhya Pradesh)" is a cotton fibre price index, not this variety. -- https://www.fibre2fashion.com/market-intelligence/texpro-textile-and-apparel/raw-material-prices/cotton-fibre/icf-mech-i-h-4-madhya-pradesh

Gaps for follow-up: query Seednet (seednet.gov.in) directly for variety code A0501197 and the CSC notification minutes for the 2004 release, and check the AICRP on Cotton annual reports and KrishiKosh for MECH-4 entries.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ajeet-33 (AHH-90-2), Cotton (Kapas)

Name check: variety_name "Ajeet-33 (AHH-90-2)" and seednet_variety_name "AJEET-33 (AHH-90-2)" are the same name apart from case, so one set of searches covered both.

Search status: three searches ran successfully. A fourth search was not run, and a follow-up check of the first two result sets was blocked by the tool-use limit. Findings below rest on the first-pass result snippets only.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned nothing that names Ajeet-33 (AHH-90-2) with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page returned names this variety with disease or pest resistance data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage (CAG/306/85 x CAG/330/85) and the breeding-line code AHH-90-2 did not appear on any returned page. The only genetics-related page was the PPV&FR compendium (see PUBLICATIONS), and it did not show these codes in the visible snippet.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the breeder. The only company-level result was an Ajeet Seeds company profile (https://www.indiamart.com/ajeet-seed-ltd/aboutus.html). It describes Ajeet Seeds as a seed producer, mentions Ajeet-11, a cotton hybrid from 1992, and does not mention Ajeet-33 or AHH-90-2. It is a different product and is excluded, so no breeder is attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute or division contact was returned for this variety. The Ajeet Seeds profile is a commercial page for a different product, so I have not recorded its details as contacts for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for this variety. Two results were returned and both were excluded:
- Compendium of Extant Notified Varieties Registered under PPV&FR Act, 2001 (plantauthority.gov.in). Its visible snippet covers other cotton entries and a "Tetraploid Cotton" list, with no visible mention of Ajeet-33. It should be checked directly for an Ajeet-33 entry: https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/envcompendium.pdf
- DSIR Annual Report 2005-2006 (dsir.gov.in). It mentions a Bt cotton hybrid, ACH-33-1, which is a different product and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not searched. The fourth search was not run, so no seed-source evidence was gathered for NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or dealers.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The supplied record lists Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, but the searches did not confirm this from any source.

Recommended next steps:
1. Check the PPV&FR compendium PDF for an Ajeet-33 or AHH-90-2 entry.
2. Search the CSC/ICAR cotton variety release notifications, and the AICRP on Cotton annual reports, for the 2006 release.
3. Search seednet.gov.in directly for variety code A0501220.
4. Ask Ajeet Seeds Ltd (Research Division, Hanumantagaon, Gangapur, Aurangabad) for breeder and parentage records, since no public breeder contact was found.

PUBLICATIONS

Two of the four returned mostly off-topic results (textile and fashion pages), which were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Plant habit (less spreading, freer growth, 1-3 monopodial branches) and boll size (2.00-2.50 g) are listed in the Ankur catalogue, but the page layout does not clearly tie these lines to Swadeshi-1 rather than neighbouring entries, so they are not attributed here. Days to square initiation (30-34) and 50% flowering (58-62) appear on the same page with the same ambiguity -- https://indiaagronet.com/cotton/Exhibition/AnkurSeeds/Data/products.htm. No multi-location or field-trial results were found -- No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SUMANGALA (CWROK 165) COTTON: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search note: four web searches were run (variety/registration, breeder/institute, research papers, seed availability). Two of the four returned relevant material. The name on the Seednet portal was not checked directly, since no Seednet page appeared in the results. Both names are used below, and each finding states which name it refers to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Sumangala. The search returned only variety lists and general cotton package-of-practice pages. The "Verticillium wilt resistant" note in the TNAU table appears in a row next to Surabhi, not Sumangala, so I have not attributed it to this variety. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Fibre%20crops/fibrecrops_cotton.html

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Sumangala (CWROK 165) or Sumangala. -- searched across all four result sets; no page named this variety with a resistance trait.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The TNAU cotton page lists Sumangala among irrigated winter (Aug-Sep) cotton varieties for Coimbatore, Erode, Madurai, Dindigul and Theni, and for Salem and Namakkal and for Cuddalore and Villupuram. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Fibre%20crops/fibrecrops_cotton.html
- The same TNAU page's release table appears to give a sowing window of Sept-Oct and Jan-Feb for Sumangala. The column alignment in the extracted text is ambiguous, so treat this as unconfirmed. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Fibre%20crops/fibrecrops_cotton.html
- An Odisha Technology Mission on Cotton lecture-note document includes Sumangala (CWROK-165) in a G. hirsutum descriptor table, with fibre and boll traits, but the extracted fragments do not give reliable yield or trait values. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353572829_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies_State_Department_of_Agriculture_Odisha_under_Technology_Mission_on_Cotton_For_official_use_only_Lecture_Notes_of_Exposure_Visit_cum_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies
- Yield: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: CW 134 x Reba B 50 x Khandwa 2, as given in the TNAU release table. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Fibre%20crops/fibrecrops_cotton.html
- Species: Gossypium hirsutum, per the Odisha lecture-note descriptor table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353572829_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies_State_Department_of_Agriculture_Odisha_under_Technology_Mission_on_Cotton_For_official_use_only_Lecture_Notes_of_Exposure_Visit_cum_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies
- Breeding method, breeding-line code beyond CWROK 165, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. No page named a breeder for Sumangala.
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Regional Station, Coimbatore, per the CSC institution field supplied in the input. The Odisha lecture notes name the same regional station. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353572829_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies_State_Department_of_Agriculture_Odisha_under_Technology_Mission_on_Cotton_For_official_use_only_Lecture_Notes_of_Exposure_Visit_cum_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies
- Institutional listing: CICR's varieties are listed in a book chapter on cotton research in India, and Sumangala is among them. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140

CONTACT DETAILS

- Institute contact: Address as supplied in the input record: ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Coimbatore-641003 (TN). The Odisha lecture notes give the same address line: "ICAR – Central Institute for Cotton Research, Regional Station, Coimbatore – 641 003." -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353572829_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies_State_Department_of_Agriculture_Odisha_under_Technology_Mission_on_Cotton_For_official_use_only_Lecture_Notes_of_Exposure_Visit_cum_Capacity_Building_Program_on_Cotton_Production_Technologies

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Hybrid Kalyan (CSHH-238), Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum)

Name note: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Hybrid Kalyan (CSHH-238)"), so one set of searches covered both. The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any result. Evidence below refers to the name "CSHH 238 (Kalyan)" or "CSHH 238" as written in the source. Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for this hybrid.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for this hybrid was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The 2013-14 Line x Tester heterosis study at CICR Regional Station, Sirsa included CSHH 238 as a check hybrid. Its main result was a single cross (RS 2013 x CSH 2811) with significant heterosis for seed cotton yield over CSHH 238 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/CoRJ/article/view/114111
AICRP/ICAR circular table lists CSHH 238 (Kalyan), G. hirsutum x G. hirsutum, year 2006, institution CICR (RS) Sirsa, area adopted "North Zone" (yield range given only generically as about 18-25 q/ha for the group of varieties) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf
A CICR technical-bulletin table on hybrid seed production lists CSHH 198 (2004, CICR RS Sirsa) but I found no row giving CSHH 238 yield or maturity values in the retrieved text -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/hybrid-seed-production-cotton/61889931 (secondary copy of CICR Technical Bulletin No. 35)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) --
Parentage: No evidence found in search results. The female parent SH 2379 (Y) and male parent PIL 8 (Selection) appear only in the user-supplied record, not in any retrieved source.
Breeding method, breeding-line codes, QTL, markers for this hybrid: No evidence found beyond the seed-protein fingerprinting study below.
Seed-protein fingerprinting: Albumin and globulin fractions separated CSHH 198 and CSHH 238 from their male and female parents, and albumin gave the stronger discrimination, for purity testing -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/15440478.2015.1005330
Mirror of the same study indexed on ResearchGate under the title "Characterization of DCH-32 cotton hybrid and parental lines by SDS-PAGE and RAPD marker". The page text matches the CSHH 198/238 study; the title names a different hybrid, so treat the title as a mislabel and not as evidence for DCH-32 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279462410_Characterization_of_DCH-32_cotton_hybrid_and_parental_lines_by_SDS-PAGE_and_RAPD_marker

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No named breeder or lead scientist for CSHH 238 was found. Developing institution (from AICRP table and heterosis study): ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Regional Station, Sirsa, Haryana -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf ; https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/CoRJ/article/view/114111
The PPV&FR compendium lists the variety under its name, but the retrieved text shows only the index entry, not the applicant or breeder details -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for CICR Regional Station Sirsa was returned in any search result. Institute name only: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Regional Station, Sirsa, Haryana -- 125 055 (as given in the supplied record, not verified by search).

PUBLICATIONS --
Tuteja, O. P.; Verma, S. K. (year not stated in retrieved text). Estimation of Economic Heterosis for Seed Cotton Yield Components and Fibre Traits of American Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum). Journal of Cotton Research and Development -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/CoRJ/article/view/114111

Journal of Natural Fibers (per DOI prefix) -- DOI 10.1080/15440478.2015.1005330 -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/15440478.2015.1005330
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report entry with yield data, or QTL paper for this hybrid was found.

A trader listing titled "Hybrid Kalyan Cotton Seeds" (Gujarat) was found at https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kalyan-cotton-seeds-20465526673.html but it does not name CSHH-238 or its parentage, so it was discarded under the strict relevance rule.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Only zone-level evidence found: the AICRP table places CSHH 238 (Kalyan) under "North Zone" -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf
No retrieved page named Haryana, Punjab or Rajasthan as recommended states for CSHH 238. The Haryana/Punjab/Rajasthan list in the supplied record is not confirmed by search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PKV DH-1 (AKDH-7), Cotton (Kapas)

Scope note: I ran four searches, one per topic. My reading was incomplete. I printed only the first 400 characters of each result, and a follow-up call hit the search limit, so I could not reread the full pages. Most headings below therefore have no confirmed evidence. Treat the single lead as unverified until the full page text is checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No resistance data for this variety appeared in the returned text.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only Akola cotton-unit text I saw gave agronomy for a different variety, PKV Rajat (a hirsutum cotton), so I discarded it. -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211

GENETICS AND QTL -- The variety name and parentage (female GAK-423, male HD-110-151) come from the input record, not from a search result. The Akola cotton-unit page says a new source of genetic male sterility was used to develop and release two hybrids, one of them named PKV DH-1. The snippet was cut off, so I could not confirm the breeding method or breeding-line codes from it. -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial evidence. The Cotton Research Unit at Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth (PDKV), Akola, is the likely developing institution. The page snippet links it to the PKV DH-1 hybrid release. No breeder name was visible in what I read. -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4211

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The institute-level contact page is not confirmed. The PDKV Cotton Research Unit page is the closest candidate, but I did not read any email, phone or address on it. The input record names a Senior Research Scientist, AICCIP, Punjabrao Krishi Vidyapeeth, Akola-444 104 (M.S.), but this is not verified by a search result.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. None of the returned results was a paper, report, thesis or KrishiKosh entry for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety appeared in the returned text.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The input record says "Unknown", and no search result gave a recommended state.

RELEASE/NOTIFICATION -- The input gives the year of release as 2002. The PPV&FR compendium PDF (https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/envcompendium.pdf) came up in the first search, but the visible text was about other varieties (for example DMH-1 and BGD-72), so I did not record it as evidence for this variety. It should be checked for a PKV DH-1 entry.

Name check: the variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("PKV DH-1 (AKDH-7)"). The evidence above refers to that name.

Suggested next steps: read the full text of the PDKV page; check the PPV&FR compendium for an entry; search KrishiKosh and the AICRP cotton reports under "PKV DH-1" with "hybrid" and "male sterility" terms; and check seednet.gov.in directly for the variety code A0501253.

disease_resistance.summary: CSC variety record: PA-255 showed reaction similar to PA-183 for bacterial blight, grey mildew (powdery mildew) and Alternaria leaf spot, and was moderately resistant to anthracnose. The CSC record has no URL in the digest. The VNMKV listing states PA-255 is among varieties released with tolerance to pests and diseases, but names no specific pathogen. No pathogen-specific resistance data beyond the CSC record was found. The level for each disease is not assigned because the digest gives no quantitative scoring.

pest_resistance.summary: Conflicting evidence. (1) The VNMKV listing and the DAC document cite general pest tolerance for desi cotton and PA-255. (2) A krishikosh genetic-transformation thesis states this desi cultivar is susceptible to all lepidopteran insects. This conflicts with the pest-tolerance claims and is not reconciled in the digest. (3) An Earias vitella biology study found larvae developed more suitably on PA-255 than on NHH-44 or Paras Brahma, which indicates host suitability rather than resistance. (4) The DAC document reports Bt genes (Cry1Ac, Cry1Aa3) transferred into PA 255. No verified lepidopteran resistance level is established.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC variety record: 1500.00 to 1600.00 Kg/Ha (15-16 q/ha). The AICRP circular states most varieties released 2002-07 yield 18-25 q/ha. This implies the CSC figure is below that group range, but no PA-255-specific yield figure from a trial was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for medium to deep black cotton soils of Marathwada in particular and Maharashtra in general under rainfed ecosystem (CSC record). Recommended for assured-rainfall areas of Marathwada (Marathwada adoption study). Tamil Nadu (Kovilpatti area) is named as a recommendation area in the DAC document. Recommended states are Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; the Seednet state field is 'Unknown' and these states need verification against the CSC minutes.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 140 To 150Days (CSC record). A desi cotton comparison table gives 145-150 days; this table's column alignment is unclear and the values are provisional.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DWARF PLANT TYPE THAN PA-183 ; ROUND AND BIG BOLLS TAPERING TOWARDS APEX HAVING FINE BOLL BURSTING THAN PA-183. Semi dwarf and resistant to lodging (CSC record). Staple length: 28 mm in a comparison table (provisional, same row lists release year 1999); 26.3 mm in a Tamil Nadu recommendation context. Boll shattering: PA 255 was one of eight lines among 69 genotypes reported as completely resistant to shattering, with over 80% boll retention. Fibre quality described as good (DAC document).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Marathwada adoption study: PA 255 and PA 183 recommended for assured-rainfall areas at 45 x 30 cm spacing with 50:25:25 NPK per ha. (3) Earias vitella study: larval development was assessed on PA-255 alongside NHH-44 and Paras Brahma. No yield trial result specific to PA-255 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PA-255 (Parbhani Turab), Cotton (Kapas)

Name coverage: The CSC name (PA-255 (Parbhani Turab)) and the Seednet name are identical, so one set of searches covered both. The Seednet portal itself returned nothing, so the Seednet variety code A0501255 and the "Unknown" recommended-states field could not be checked against it. All evidence below refers to PA-255 (Parbhani Turab), the Gossypium arboreum (desi) cotton. Four searches were run: variety/release, breeder/institute, research papers, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The variety was described as evolved at Parbhani and released in 2000, with tolerance to drought and pests and diseases cited as beneficial features of desi cotton -- https://nriipm.res.in/NCIPMPDFs/FOLDERS/RevolutioninIndianCotton_.pdf
- The same source describes the variety as having high productivity, early maturity, good fibre quality, and tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses for rainfed cotton -- https://nriipm.res.in/NCIPMPDFs/FOLDERS/RevolutioninIndianCotton_.pdf
- A VNMKV/AICRP-style listing says PA-255 is among varieties released with superior fibre quality and tolerance to pests and diseases -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php
- Drought: a Parbhani drought-screening study of 12 cotton genotypes is mentioned, but the snippet does not name PA-255 in the results, so this is not recorded as a finding -- https://crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e3650e47.pdf
- Boll shattering: PA 255 was one of eight lines reported as completely resistant to shattering among 69 genotypes with over 80% boll retention -- http://crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e3650e47.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- A krishikosh genetic-transformation thesis notes that this desi cultivar is susceptible to all lepidopteran insects -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/9277367c-3d1b-4d29-8b95-12495b7ad4e5/content (this conflicts with the pest-tolerance claims above and must be reconciled before use)
- Pest-tolerance claims for desi cotton generally come from the DAC document cited under STRESS TOLERANCE; no pathogen-specific resistance data for PA-255 was found.
- Earias vitella biology: larvae were studied on PA-255 (Parbhani Turab) alongside NHH-44 and Paras Brahma, and PA-255 was judged more suitable for larval development -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298733932_Biometrics_of_Earias_Vitella_Fabricius_on_Cotton
- Bt-gene transfer: the DAC document says long-staple arboreum varieties PA 255 and PA 402 were transferred with Cry1Ac and Cry1Aa3 genes -- https://nriipm.res.in/NCIPMPDFs/FOLDERS/RevolutioninIndianCotton_.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A Marathwada adoption study reports that PA 255 and PA 183 are recommended for assured-rainfall areas of Marathwada, at 45 x 30 cm spacing with 50:25:25 NPK per ha -- https://api.seea.org.in/uploads/pdf/v07112.pdf
- The same study recommends cotton + tur intercropping (8:2 or 6:2) over sole cotton -- https://api.seea.org.in/uploads/pdf/v07112.pdf
- An AICRP circular lists Parbhani Turab (G. arboreum, MAU, 2004) among varieties released 2002–07 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf (note: this entry names "Parbhani Turab" and the year 2004, not PA-255 directly)
- Yield: the AICRP circular states that most varieties released 2002–07 yield 18–25 q/ha; no PA-255-specific yield figure was found -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf
- A desi cotton comparison table lists PA 255 (Parbhani Turab) with a maturity of 145–150 days and a staple of 28 mm (the same row lists the release year as 1999); the column alignment is unclear, so treat these values as provisional -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/ad26f1d1-28cf-4a9c-84fb-4e805eee6839/content
- Staple length of 26.3 mm was reported for PA 255 in a Tamil Nadu recommendation context -- https://nriipm.res.in/NCIPMPDFs/FOLDERS/RevolutioninIndianCotton_.pdf
- Release year discrepancy: the CSC minutes say 2002; the DAC document says 2000; the genetic diversity thesis table gives 1999; the AICRP circular says 2004. Record all and flag for verification.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (BC progenies of (CJ-73 x A-4) x CJ-73, crossed with NA-39): NOT FOUND in any search result. The pedigree from the CSC minutes remains unverified.
- Breeding method: NOT FOUND in any search result.
- Genome resources: NOT FOUND (no QTL, marker-trait, or genome-sequence study for PA-255 was returned).
- Biotechnology: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of PA-255 (diploid, G. arboreum) with npt-II and cry1Ac genes, with GUS integration in T0 and later generations; the transgenic plants carried more than one T-DNA copy -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/9277367c-3d1b-4d29-8b95-12495b7ad4e5/content and http://crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e3650e47.pdf
- Micropropagation: PA-255 (diploid) and PH-348 (tetraploid) shoot-tip culture was compared -- http://crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n531e9e3650e47.pdf
- DNA diversity: a thesis fingerprinted 20 desi genotypes, including PA 255, with RAPD primer OPA-6 -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/ad26f1d1-28cf-4a9c-84fb-4e805eee6839/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name(s): NOT FOUND. No page named the lead breeder for PA-255 in any search.
- Developing institution: Marathwada Agricultural University, Parbhani (now Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth, VNMKV), listed as the source of PA 255 (Parbhani Turab) under desi cotton releases -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_VarietyReleased.php
- Station: Cotton Research Station, Mahboob Baugh Farm, Parbhani (the CSC station named in the variety record); a genebank record for it exists -- https://www.genesys-pgr.org/wiews/IND1049
- Cotton Research Scheme, VNMKV Parbhani, established 1969, with a stated focus on cotton agronomy and crop improvement -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php
- Seed-chain context (general, not variety-specific): breeders produce nucleus seed; ICAR/SAU institutes produce breeder seed; NSC/SSCs produce foundation seed -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I ran four searches, but the tool limit was reached during a fifth, so I could not pull full page text. Several headings below have thin or no evidence. The snippets I saw were truncated, so I have not quoted or paraphrased them beyond what they show.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shresth (CSHH-198), Cotton (Kapas)
Name check: the CSC release-minute name and the Seednet name are both "Shresth (CSHH-198)". The evidence below refers to that name. The CICR at-a-glance page also gives the alias "CICR-HH Cotton 19" for the same entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The retrieved snippets did not discuss drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Possible but unverified: an AICRP/ICAR circular lists CSHH-198 (Shresth) in a table row that also mentions Cotton leaf curl virus. The snippet does not state that the variety is resistant or tolerant, so I am not recording it as a finding. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Shresth was used as a non-Bt check entry in the North Zone first-year Bt cotton hybrid trial (2006-07), where the non-Bt check hybrids were listed as CSHH 198 (Shresth) and LHH 144. This shows it was a trial comparator, not yield data. -- https://core.ac.uk/outputs/250041265/
Yield, maturity and fibre data: No evidence found in the retrieved text.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage (from the supplied record, not verified on the web): female CSH 19 x male CSH 8.
The AICRP circular table row gives the breeding entry as "CSHH-198 (Shresth)" with the cross listed as "G.hir x G.hir" and the institute as "CICR, Sirsa", North zone. The snippet is truncated, so I cannot confirm the cross, the parent codes or the breeding method from it. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf
QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution per the CICR at-a-glance brochure: the variety is listed among CICR releases as "Shresth (CSHH 198) (CICR-HH Cotton 19)". The breeder name on that line is cut off in the snippet, so no breeder is named. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
Institution from the supplied record: Central Research Institute for Cotton Research, Regional Station, Sirsa (Haryana) 125 055. This was not confirmed by a retrieved page.
Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No official institute email, phone or contact-page URL was retrieved. The supplied record gives only the postal line "Regional Station, Sirsa (Haryana) - 125 055" and no phone or email. The institute headquarters is ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur; its contact details were not retrieved and should be taken from https://cicr.org.in.

PUBLICATIONS
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis or conference paper naming this variety was found. The AICRP circular and the North Zone trial report above are the only items, and neither is a publication with authors and a DOI.
- Trial report: "North Zone Evaluation of Bt Cotton Hybrids First Year Trial (2006-07)" -- AICRP on Cotton trial report, year not confirmed from the snippet. URL: https://core.ac.uk/outputs/250041265/
- AICRP/ICAR circular (crop science) listing CSHH-198 (Shresth) -- URL: https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
Not searched. The fourth search was lost to the tool limit. Seednet listing: no evidence retrieved. Seed sources (NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, dealers): not checked.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Supplied record: Punjab, Rajasthan. Not independently confirmed by a retrieved page.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Hybrid CSHH-243 (Cotton, Gossypium)
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Hybrid CSHH-243"), so all searches used this one name. Seednet crop name "COTTON (KAPAS)" was searched as "Cotton".
Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). No search returned a page naming this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Search 1 returned a Google Patents page on hybrid cotton plants and seeds (WO2004060051A2), which does not name CSHH-243.
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page in the results discussed resistance for this variety.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No page in the results gave maturity, yield, or trial data for this variety. The seed-treatment AICRP circular in search 4 covers other experiments and does not name this hybrid.
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No parentage, breeding-line code, or genome resource was found for CSHH-243.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. Search 2 returned an intechopen chapter on the institutional structure of cotton research in India (https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140). It describes national cotton research structure in general and does not mention CSHH-243 or CICR Regional Station Sira. No breeder name is attributed to this variety.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. The only institution details are those supplied in the input record (Central Institute of Cotton Research, Regional Station, Sira, Haryana - 125 055). No contact page for that station was found in the results, so no email, phone, or URL is given.
PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. Search 3 returned a USDA ARS paper on developing hybrid cotton using honey bees (https://www.ars.usda.gov/ARSUserFiles/60500500/PDFFiles/501-600/530-Zumba--Developing-Hybrid-Cotton.pdf). It concerns a different hybrid programme and is not attributed to this variety.
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Search 4 returned an ICAR AICRP crop science circular (https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/AICRPsCropScience.pdf). It does not name CSHH-243 and is not used as a source for seed availability.
RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in the search results. The input record states "Haryana and Punjab, irrigated conditions" (from the parentage field, which contains release text). This is not confirmed by an independent source. The input record's recommended_states_raw field is "Unknown".

Gaps to close: check the Seednet portal entry (seednet.gov.in) for A0501291 directly, the CICR website (cicr.org.in) for the Sira station contact page, and the CSC/AICRP cotton release notifications for 2008 (the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards notification). None of these were reachable through the search tool.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigation conditions
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: On the basis of average of 4 locations LH 2076 gabe maximum yield of 2289 Kg.ha at 100 kh nitrogen per hectare which is slightly higher as compared to recommended dose of 75 KgN/ha (2215 Kg/ha). As regards spacing LH 2076 recorded maximum yield at recommended spacing of 67.5 x 60 cm.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: - Sympodial plants with green broad lobbed medium sized leaves. - Flower and another colour is cream.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: b. Distinguishing Morphological characteristics: Plants with green stem and branches, green broad lobed leaves of medium size with five lobes, cream flower with cream anthers, medium sized bolls with fluffy opening.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: LH 2076 found resistant to cotton leaf curl virus at Ludhiana, Faridkot and Abohar stations. This new variety was also found resistant to bacterial blight and fungal foliar leaaf spots at Ludhiana and Abohar but at Faridkot it was moderately resistant to both the disease.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: On an average of comparative trials jassids grade in LH 2076 was comparable to check varieties. Whitefly population in LH 2076 was comparable to check varieties and remained below economic threshold level in all trials. Bollworm incidence on boll and loculi basis was comparable in LH 2076 to check varieties.

drought.details: The AICRP-Jute record does not list Bidhan Pat-3 among the drought-tolerant varieties. This is an absence of listing, not a measured tolerance result, so no drought level is assigned. No drought trial data found in the digest. The digest does not report a moderate water-stress reaction; that statement is not present in the evidence provided.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: AICRP-Jute lists Bidhan Pat-3 among varieties suited to waterlogging. BCKV and the Directorate of Jute Development describe it as suitable for low-lying, flood-prone jute areas. These are qualitative suitability statements; no quantified flood-tolerance measurements were found in the digest, so the level is medium.

disease_resistance.summary: AICRP-Jute records the variety as tolerant to stem rot and yellow vein mosaic virus (YVM). No resistance evidence for Macrophomina phaseolina was found in the digest. The digest does not state a percentage reaction for any disease.

pest_resistance.summary: AICRP-Jute records tolerance to mealybug and spiral borer. A jute agronomy deck lists tolerance to yellow mite, but this is a secondary source that conflicts with the AICRP list, so it was not relied on. No quantified pest infestation values were found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Mahapatra and Mitra review (same table row as parentage): 2.5-2.7 t/ha. AICRP fibre yield as notified: 25-27 q/ha. These are fibre-yield figures from different sources and are not directly comparable to the seed-yield trial.
agronomic_details.stability: Non-lodging and sowing-date flexibility are reported (AICRP). No multi-environment stability analysis was found. Registration: PPV&FRA No. 105/2012 dated 02.08.2012, as listed by BCKV. This differs from the 2001 release and notification year given by AICRP and the Directorate of Jute Development.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Photoperiod-insensitive; suitable for early, medium and late sowing, with sowing from 1 March to 1 July (AICRP). Recommended for late sowing in an agronomy deck (secondary source). Suited to low-lying, flood-prone areas (BCKV, Directorate of Jute Development). Rainfed red and laterite zone seed-crop trial results are in field_trials.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT: 3.0-3.5 METER;RED PIGMENTED IS PETIOLE ,MID RIB OF LEAVES AND NODES
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Seed-crop trial at Raghunathpur (BCKV, Purulia, 2014-15), rainfed red and laterite conditions: sowing late June to mid-July with topping gave the highest seed yield. (2) Fibre quality as notified: fibre strength 22.78 g/tex, fineness 3.39 tex, lower root content and defects (AICRP; BCKV). (3) Mahapatra and Mitra review: maturity 110-115 days and fibre yield 2.5-2.7 t/ha. (4) A Bangladesh study (Yield and quality of jute seed as influenced by variety) quotes a Bidhan Pat-3 seed-yield result; the value is not stated in the digest.
