search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bidhan Pat-3 (D-110), Jute (Corchorus capsularis)

Name note: "variety_name" is "Bidhan Pat-3 (D-110)" and "seednet_variety_name" is "BIDHAN PAT-3 (D-110)". No search result came from the Seednet portal, so every finding below refers to "Bidhan Pat-3" as printed by AICRP-Jute, BCKV, or the other sources cited. None of the sources printed the "D-110" designation, so I could not confirm it as a synonym from the evidence. Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- AICRP-Jute lists Bidhan Pat-3 among the varieties suited to waterlogging, and it is not listed among the drought-tolerant ones -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- A jute technology deck groups Bidhan Pat-3 with varieties tolerant to waterlogging and submergence -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- Bidhan Pat-3 is described as suitable for low-lying, flood-prone jute areas -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf (the same claim also appears at https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx)

DISEASE AND PEST
- AICRP-Jute records the variety as tolerant to mealybug, spiral borer, yellow vein mosaic virus (YVM) and stem rot -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- A deck on jute agronomy lists Bidhan Pat-3 among the varieties tolerant to yellow mite, but this is a secondary source and conflicts with the AICRP list, so I have not relied on it -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Photoperiod-insensitive, non-shattering pods, maturing about 110 days after sowing, with sowing anytime from 1 March to 1 July -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Recommended for late sowing in the agronomy deck -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621
- Seed-crop trial at Raghunathpur (BCKV, Purulia, 2014-15): sowing late June to mid-July with topping gave the highest seed yield under rainfed red and laterite conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319469619_Jute_seed_production_as_influenced_by_dates_of_sowing_and_topping_in_red_and_laterite_zone_of_West_Bengal
- Fibre yield 25-27 q/ha as notified, with fibre strength 22.78 g/tex, fineness 3.39 tex, and lower root content and defects -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/ ; https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage given as D-154 x D-18 (D-18 described as a mutant), with a 2000 BCKV release entry; the source is a table with merged cells, so the row assignment is not fully certain -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262246414_Research_on_jute_Corchorus_olitorius_and_C_capsularis_and_kenaf_Hibiscus_cannabinus_and_H_sabdariffa_Present_status_and_future_perspective
- The Mahapatra and Mitra review also states the variety's maturity and fibre yield in the same table row (110-115 days; 2.5-2.7 t/ha) -- same URL
- No QTL, marker, breeding-line code, breeding-method or genome-resource evidence found -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is listed as released by BCKV (Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya), Mohanpur, Nadia, with ICAR-CRIJAF as applicant and AINP on Jute and Allied Fibres as associated project -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- CRIJAF lists Bidhan Pat-3 among the varieties it selected for registration -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- Named breeder or lead scientist: No evidence found (the searches returned no individual breeder name for this variety)
- The Department of Seed Technology is not named as the developing unit in any source; the institute-level attribution comes from the BCKV page above

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KOM-62 (Revati), Jute (Corchorus olitorius, tossa)

Name handling: "variety_name" is KOM-62 (Revati). "seednet_variety_name" is KOM-62 (REVATI). I did not find a Seednet portal page in the four searches. Every finding below refers to KOM-62 (Revati) under one of these names. The AICRP page spells it "KOM 62 (Rebati)", which I treated as the same variety because the release year, state and notification match. The institution appears as OUAT in the sources, which corresponds to the V.C.O.U.A.T., Bhubaneswar entry in the input.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Premature flowering resistance is recorded as absent, and pod dehiscence as present; seed colour is steel grey -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was found for this variety. The tolerance statements on the same AICRP page refer to other varieties, so I have not attributed them to KOM-62.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to KOM-62 (Revati). The AICRP page lists resistance traits only for other varieties.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pods are described as non-shattering, with optimum sowing from mid-March to late April; the variety is listed as suitable for Odisha -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/TossaJute.aspx
- The AICRP table gives a yield value of 30.40 for KOM 62, with no unit stated on the page. The DAC page gives a range of 30-35 for the same variety, also with no unit -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/ ; https://jute.dac.gov.in/TossaJute.aspx
- Source conflict: the DAC page calls the pods non-shattering, while the AICRP page records pod dehiscence as present. I have not resolved this.
- KOM-62 (Revati) is listed among jute varieties recommended for early sowing -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546 (a secondary slide deck, not an official report)
- Maturity days: no evidence found.
- Multi-location trial results: no evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- The parentage given in the input (B2SE variety - Revati; Muagen used - 40 KR Gamaray) was not confirmed by any search result. No evidence found.
- No QTL, marker, genome or breeding-line code evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution listed as OUAT on the DAC page -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/TossaJute.aspx
- Release notification: 1993, Odisha, S.O. 615(E), dated 17.08.1993 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): no evidence found.
- Developing station: no evidence found beyond the OUAT attribution.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No OUAT or institute email, phone or address was found in these results.
- Institute-level page for the national network coordinating the variety list: https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/ (this page is hosted by ICAR and lists ICAR-CRIJAF as a participating institute; no email or phone was shown in the retrieved text).

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The retrieved pages are variety lists and extension notes, not papers, theses or AICRP reports specific to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was returned for KOM-62 (Revati).
- Non-seed mention: the WDRA trade standard for raw jute lists KOM-62 (REVATI) among accepted jute types -- https://wdra.gov.in/web/wdra/jute-bales (this is a commodity grading reference, not a seed source).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha. The AICRP table records the state as Odisha at notification, and the DAC page says suitable for Odisha -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/ ; https://jute.dac.gov.in/TossaJute.aspx
- The input value "Unknown" should be updated to Odisha on the basis of these sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JRC-532 (C-532), Jute (Corchorus capsularis)

Name note: The evidence refers to this variety as "JRC 532 (Sashi)" or "Sashi (JRC-532)", in the AICRP and ICAR release tables and the CRIJAF variety page. The variety_name ("JRC-532 (C-532)") and seednet_variety_name ("JRC-532 (C-532)") are identical, so I matched on "JRC 532 / JRC-532 / Sashi." I found no separate page for "C-532" itself. Results for "JRC 517", "JRO 204", "JRC 80" and other varieties were excluded. The Corchorus olitorius lineage papers and the RuneScape "jute" items were excluded as other crops or unrelated topics.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Release-table entry: the variety is described as drought-resistant at early growth and as tolerating waterlogging, maturing in about 110 days after sowing, with pods that do not shatter -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- ICAR's 2008-09 release summary lists Sashi (JRC-532) as tolerant to drought and waterlogging in capsularis-growing areas -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Crop-Improvement_0.pdf
- A state-wise list in the CRIJAF agronomy lecture places JRC 532 (Sashi) among varieties grouped under submergence tolerance -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621
- Salinity, heat, flood and pest tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The stem-rot screening papers found concern germplasm and an F2 population, not JRC-532.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A 2023 pre-kharif trial in the coastal region of South Bengal tested JRC 532 against five other capsularis varieties. The paper reports JRC 9057 as highest in fibre yield (25.25 q/ha), followed by JRC 80, JRC 517, JRC 532 and JRCJ 11 -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/IJBSv11n2c.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390811461_Varietal_Performance_of_Jute_Corchorus_capsularis_L_Based_on_Crop_Growth_and_Yield_in_the_Coastal_Region_of_South_Bengal
- The trial tables also list JRC 532 gross and net return values (Rs 1,41,849 gross, Rs 85,746 net per ha in the table, the same figures attributed to JRC 532 in the Renu PDF), but the table extraction is unclear, so treat these as unverified.
- Yield and maturity figures for JRC 532 specifically from other sources: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (exotic Chinese DTYPE CHN/FJ/O44Cc x JRC 321, then F2 intermating): No evidence found on any retrieved page.
- Breeding-line codes, QTL, markers and genome resources specific to JRC-532: No evidence found. The microsatellite map papers found concern other lines.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (CRIJAF), Barrackpore, West Bengal -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-central-research-institute-jute-and-allied-fibres
- CRIJAF applied to the PPV&FR Authority for registration of JRC 532 and other varieties. DUS testing for JRC 532 was reported as complete and judged distinct from reference varieties -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- Lead breeder or scientist name for JRC-532: No evidence found. Names of CRIJAF scientists on other jute papers were not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level, as found)
- Director, ICAR-CRIJAF: Dr Gouranga Kar (listed in a 2021 profile) -- Email: director.crijaf@icar.gov.in -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-central-research-institute-jute-and-allied-fibres
- Postal address: ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore, Kolkata-700121 (W.B) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
- Alternate address on institute site: Nilganj, Barrackpore, Kolkata 700121, INDIA. Website: https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/
- Seednet's listed address reads "Kollatta - 700 120". The institute uses 700121, so verify before use.
- Dr C S Kar, Principal Scientist and Nodal Officer, appears in a seed-industry news item about jute seed. This is a seed-liaison role, not a breeder contact -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-11/ICAR-News-Jan-Dec%202021.pdf
- Phone numbers: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2023). Varietal performance of jute (Corchorus capsularis L.) based on crop growth and yield in the coastal region of South Bengal. Journal not confirmed (Renu Publishers PDF) -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/IJBSv11n2c.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (c. 2012). Promising technologies of CRIJAF. Walsh Medical Media proceedings -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- ICAR-CRIJAF / AICRP-Jute (2009). Details of varieties, entry 14, JRC 532 (Sashi). AICRP on Jute and Allied Fibres -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Theses (KrishiKosh) and peer-reviewed papers specific to JRC-532: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- ICAR-CRIJAF lists JRC-532 among varieties it licenses for commercial seed production, and it reports supplying breeder seed to the seed industry -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-11/ICAR-News-Jan-Dec%202021.pdf
- CRIJAF sells jute seed under its own trademark. Breeder-seed supply is noted as a revenue source -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/promising-technologies-of-crijaf-14411.html
- The institute's EOI notice mentions seed production for "high yielding jute and flax varieties" but the retrieved text does not list them, so it cannot be tied to JRC-532 -- https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for JRC-532: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal is confirmed as the release state in the AICRP table (notified 11.02.2009) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- The recommended states in the input (Assam, Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh) are not confirmed by any retrieved page. The state-wise ICAR table was truncated in the search output, so verify against the notification (S.O. 449(E)).

disease_resistance.summary: Root rot and stem rot: reported as tolerant (AICRP jute page, agronomy slideshare) and recommended as resistant (AICRP achievements page). Anthracnose: reported as tolerant (AICRP jute page, agronomy slideshare) and better biotic resistance described (improved technologies slideshare, agrovista). Stem rot is also listed under better biotic resistance in the improved technologies slideshare.

pest_resistance.summary: Yellow mite: described as having better biotic resistance (improved technologies slideshare, agrovista farming). Semilooper: resistance not found for this variety; the AICRP page mentions semilooper tolerance only for AAUCJ 2 (Kkhyati), which is a different variety and is excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: 36 q/ha (AICRP jute page; academic review of Assam jute production notes high yield potential of 36 q/ha). No other yield values were found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location trial data or yield tables specific to this variety were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed among varieties suitable for late sowing alongside JBO 2003 H, JRO 204 and JRO 524 (improved technologies slideshare). Recommended states per digest: Assam, Nagaland, Tripura. Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal appear in the variety record but were not confirmed by the search and are excluded from the verified list.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources. The variety record lists 160 To 175 Days, but the digest states maturity is not explicitly given in the snippets.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-shattering pod, broader leaf, longer green stipule, tall cylindrical stem, non-lodging type (AICRP details of varieties page). Resistance to lodging and moderate shattering resistance are not separately confirmed in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: AAUOJ-1 (Tarun), Jute (Corchorus olitorius)

Name note: The CSC release name is "AAUOJ-1 (Tarun)" and the Seednet name is "AAUOJ-1 (TARUN)". Searches returned both forms, and the AICRP pages use "AAUOJ 1 (Tarun)" and "AAU-OJ-1 (Tarun)". All findings below refer to this variety. Only the AAUOJ-1 name is matched; the Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- AICRP jute page lists AAUOJ 1 (Tarun) as tolerant of root and stem rot and anthracnose, with a yield of 36 q/ha and a release year of 2007 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- A slideshare summary of improved jute technologies credits the variety with better biotic resistance and resistance to premature flowering -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- Agronomy slideshare lists it among varieties tolerant of root and stem rot and anthracnose -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621
- No evidence found for specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. The search returned only general lists of varieties for waterlogging-tolerant or late-sowing conditions without naming AAUOJ-1 under those traits.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Recommended as resistant to root and stem rot and anthracnose -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
- Described as having better biotic resistance to stem rot, root rot, anthracnose and yellow mite -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546 ; https://agrovistafarming.com/cultivation-of-jute-corchorus-spp-in-india/
- Semilooper resistance was not found for this variety. The AICRP page mentions semilooper tolerance only for a different jute variety (AAUCJ 2, Kkhyati) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Non-shattering pod, broader leaf, longer green stipule, tall cylindrical stem, non-lodging type -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Maturity/duration is not explicitly given in the snippets; the AICRP entry shows a 36-38 range for a related trait, which I did not attribute to the variety.
- Suitability: listed among varieties for late sowing alongside JBO 2003 H, JRO 204 and JRO 524 -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- Academic review of Assam jute production notes the high yield potential (36 q/ha) of Tarun and the pest and disease risks of intensive cultivation -- https://www.academia.edu/106135512/Growth_and_Instability_of_Jute_Production_in_Assam
- No multi-location trial data or yield tables specific to this variety were found beyond the 36 q/ha figure.

GENETICS AND QTL:
- No evidence found for QTL, marker, genome, or breeding-line code studies for AAUOJ-1 (Tarun). The searches did not return any genomic or marker publications for this variety.
- Parentage and breeding method were supplied in the variety record (NOJ PL-1 pure line; Sel. 2 from a Tanganyka-1 × JRO 640 cross). No independent source in the searches confirmed these details, so I am not reporting them as search-verified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist for this variety.
- AICRP and AINP pages place the variety within the All India Network Project on Jute and Allied Fibres, with CRIJAF (Barrackpore) as the coordinating centre -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
- The AICRP and AAU records associate the release with Assam Agricultural University, under the AINP on Jute and Allied Fibres, AAU-ZRS Shillongani -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
- Institution as given in the variety record: ICAR-CRIJAF (Central Research Institute for Jute & Allied Fibres), Barrackpore, West Bengal.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- Institute website: CRIJAF -- http://www.crijaf.org.in/SideLinks/Research/Varieties.html
- Postal address (from the variety record, not verified by search): ICAR, Central Research Institute for Jute & Allied Fibres, Barrackpore, West Bengal, PIN 700 120.
- AAU research station: AINP on Jute and Allied Fibres, AAU-ZRS, Shillongani (Nagaon, Assam) -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
- Breeder-level contact: No evidence found. No official email or phone number for the institute or the division was present in the search snippets.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Guha, B. (2015). Tarun (AAUOJ-1), Deomorar eti unnata jat [Research Bulletin No. 1/2015, RARS, AAU Shillongani, Nagaon, Assam]. Research Bulletin -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/publication-2/other-publication/ (author and year are from the AICRP listing; the full title is truncated in the search snippet)
- Author not stated (2009). Tarun-Deo(Tossa) Morapatar Ati Natun Rastriya Jat. Ghare Pathare, April 2009 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/publication-2/other-publication/ (popular-press article)
- Academic paper naming Tarun in an Assam production study (Growth and Instability of Jute Production in Assam, International Journal of Research, 2020) -- https://www.academia.edu/106135512/Growth_and_Instability_of_Jute_Production_in_Assam (this is a production-economics paper, not a variety study; author not confirmed from the snippet)
- No KrishiKosh thesis, peer-reviewed variety paper, or DOI specific to AAUOJ-1 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No evidence found from Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales pages for this variety. The search returned only general crop-statistics pages that list AAUOJ-1 as recommended in Assam and Tripura -- https://www.farmer.gov.in/cropstaticsjute.aspx
- Seednet portal check (AAUOJ-1 (TARUN), variety code A0502029) was not returned by any search and remains unverified.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Assam -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/ ; https://www.farmer.gov.in/cropstaticsjute.aspx
- Tripura -- https://www.farmer.gov.in/cropstaticsjute.aspx
- Nagaland -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621
- The variety record lists Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal. Those three states were not confirmed for AAUOJ-1 in the search results, so they are reported as unverified.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: JRO-524, JBO-2003H, JRO-632, JRo08432, all of these varieties resemble the proposed variety for stem colour.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Due to presence of premature flowering resistance genes achieved from its parentage of JBO2003H, this proposed variety can be sown within a wide range of sowing period, from early to mid March to as late as mid May of the year.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
1.	Green coloured stem, petiole and leaf margin.
2.	Pods non-dehiscent on maturity.
3.	Green coloured prominent dentawns on leaf lamina base, of 25-35mm length.
4.	Stem cylindrical, green pigmentation; stem basal diameter 2.06cm (1.71-2.36cm).
5.	Leaf colour green, ovate-lanceolate in shape erect in nature with 0-42 degree angle from leaf axis.
6.	Flower petal colour is yellow, pods green and cylindrical in shape with non dehiscent type.
7.	Seed colour is steel grey with 1000 grains weight being 2.01g.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: The proposed variety is adapted to rainfed situation and tolerant to biotic stresses specially yellow mite & stem rot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Considering average performance of AVT I and AVT II, (Ref Table - 7), KRO-4 showed high level of tolerance to stem rot, performing almost at par with the national check JRO-524 and nearly 40% less incidence of this disease compared to the other check JRO-8432.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Under field condition, as per occurrence of different major pests in Olitorius, the proposed variety KRO-4 performed exceptionally well against all the major pests.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Five tonnes of well decomposed farm yard manure is to be applied during last ploughing in one ha of land. Fertlizer reqirement of low fertility soil is N PK 60:40:50 kg/ha.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NCJ-28-10 AAUCJ-2 (Kkhyati) -- evidence digest

Name note: Every page that matched refers to "AAUCJ 2 (Kkhyati)", the Assam white jute variety released in 2017. None of the results used the "NCJ-28-10" code, so I cannot confirm that it is the same entry. The Seednet name and the CSC minutes name are both unverified against these sources. The findings below apply to AAUCJ 2 (Kkhyati) and should be read under that name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to semi looper, yellow mite and stem rot, with better tolerance than earlier releases; the notified traits also list tolerance to mealybug, spiral borer and yellow vein mosaic virus (YVM) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
Stem rot resistance and tolerance to semi looper and yellow mite were restated in the AAU department profile, which also notes resistance to lodging -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Breeding objective was high fibre yield together with resistance to several pests and diseases -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The search returned general white jute notes only (for example, tolerance of abiotic stresses listed for JROG 1 Bithika, a different variety) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to stem rot and root rot, tolerant to semi looper and yellow mite, and moderately tolerant to stem weevil -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Tolerant to mealybug, spiral borer, YVM and stem rot -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
Semi looper, yellow mite and stem rot tolerance also appear in the DAC white jute variety table -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Sowing window: mid-February to the last week of April -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Maturity: about 120-125 days to fibre maturity and 155-165 days to seed maturity -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Stem is cylindrical, non-branching, green and lodging-resistant -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Yield: 27.95 q/ha in the AINP-JAF notification table -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
Yield range of 27-30 q/ha in the DAC white jute table -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx
Yield of 27-28 q/ha in a jute technology compendium (listed under AAUCJ 2) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
Fibre quality discrepancy: one AICRP listing gives fibre strength 22.78 g/tex and fineness 3.39 tex, while the AAU profile gives 16.98 g/tex and 1.93 tex. Neither was checked against a trial report -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/ and https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Lower root content and fewer defects are also reported for the variety -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
Multi-location trial data: no evidence found beyond the AICRP and AAU summaries above

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: CEX-045 x CEX-050 -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Breeding method: selection using the modified bulk method -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Breeding-line code: NCJ-28-10 not found in any result. The parentage was recorded by the institution of origin, ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore (per the brief).
QTL, marker or genome studies: No evidence found. The Bt jute and polycotyledony hits concern JRC 321, a different cultivar, and were discarded -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5758602/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Assam Agricultural University (AAU), AINP on Jute and Allied Fibres, Regional/Zonal Research Station at Shillongani (the brief says Shillonganj) -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271
Network: Released through the All India Network Project on Jute and Allied Fibres, run with ICAR-CRIJAF -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No named breeder appears on any page searched.

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder email, phone or direct address: No evidence found.
Institute page for the AAU jute programme: https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/271 (no phone, email or postal address on the page as indexed)
ICAR-CRIJAF (institute-level): Nilganj, Barrackpore, about 6 km from Barrackpore railway station; website https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/ . No phone or email was in the indexed text.
Director of ICAR-CRIJAF: Dr. Gouranga Kar, per Wikipedia (not an official source; not verified) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP annual report entries, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers specific to AAUCJ 2 (Kkhyati). The search returned unrelated jute papers (fibre, retting and tossa stem anatomy), which were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No variety-specific seed source found: no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for AAUCJ 2 (Kkhyati).
General guidance only (not variety-specific): certified jute seed should come from NSC centres, government supply agencies or authorized dealers -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in): not reached in these searches; no listing confirmed.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Assam, as the release state (notification S.O. 1007(E), dated 30.03.2017) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
Also suited to other white jute states: West Bengal, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/
Release/notification year 2017, listed as AAU under white jute -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/WhiteJute.aspx

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Sanai-1 (sunnhemp, Crotalaria juncea)
Names searched: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Narendra Sanai-1", so one set of searches covered both. Four web_search queries were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The search returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. A 2007 news item about the Punjab Agricultural University releases mentions disease resistance, but it does not tie that trait to Narendra Sanai-1 and I did not treat it as evidence. -- https://www.oneindia.com/2007/02/17/six-new-improved-varieties-of-crops-released-1171712372.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
- Described as a sunnhemp variety with quick, erect growth, and given an average seed yield of about 3.9 quintals per acre (the same article gives 4.8 quintals per acre for PAU 1691). -- https://www.oneindia.com/2007/02/17/six-new-improved-varieties-of-crops-released-1171712372.html
- Maturity is given as about 152 days, with notes on sowing, green-manure use and seed production. These come from non-official grower guides and are not verified against an ICAR or SAU trial report. -- https://permacultureplants.com/plants/sunn-hemp/narendra-sanai-1/ ; https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/green-manure/sunhemp
- A grower page gives green-manure biomass of about 3.8 to 6.2 tonnes per acre at 45 to 60 days after sowing, without a trial source. It is not verified. -- https://www.cannabistimesindia.com/sunhemp-quick-growing-leguminous-crop-for-fibre/
- Used as the check variety (labelled ND-I) for green-manure biomass at 45 days in a Punjab trial of PAU 1691. -- https://indianjournals.com/api/article-view/jre-45-1and2-023

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage "PLANT INTRODUCTION" is from the supplied CSC/Seednet record only and was not confirmed by any search result. No breeding-line code, QTL, marker or genome study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder or scientist. The institution is linked in a result to Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology, which lists Narendra Sanai-1 among its developed varieties (the crop label beside it was not confirmed in the retrieved text). -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for a breeder, email, phone or postal address. The only institute web address retrieved is the university site, which I did not open for contact data. -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf (institution listing only)

PUBLICATIONS --
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2008). PAU 1691: a new variety of sunnhemp for green manuring (new crop variety note; Narendra Sanai-1 appears only as the check). Journal of Research, Punjab Agricultural University 45(1&2): 104 -- https://indianjournals.com/api/article-view/jre-45-1and2-023
No peer-reviewed paper, ICAR/AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record specifically on Narendra Sanai-1 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet seller listings naming Narendra Sanai-1. Generic sunnhemp seed sellers and seed-production articles were discarded because they do not name this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not confirmed by search. The supplied record lists Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, and I found no notification or state-recommendation document that verifies this. Source for the states: supplied CSC/Seednet record only.

Summary of gaps: no breeder name, contact, genetics, stress-tolerance, disease-resistance or seed-source evidence was found. The CSC release minutes and the official Seednet entry were not retrieved, so the 2003 release year and the state list remain unverified.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: NDFB-3 (Narendra Chara Bajra-3)

Name check: The release-minute name (NDFB-3 / Narendra Chara Bajra-3) and the Seednet name are the same, so every finding below refers to that one name. Four searches were run, and no Seednet portal page surfaced.

CROP MISMATCH (READ FIRST): The sources I retrieved describe NDFB-3 as a pearl millet (bajra) fodder variety, not a Napier grass variety. The Database of Forage Crop Varieties lists the crop as "Bajra/Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum L.)" and says it was selected from NDFB-202. The NDUAT bajra document calls it "a fodder bajra variety." The Seednet crop label "BAJRA NAPIER HYBRID" is a separate grouping, and no retrieved page calls NDFB-3 a Napier grass or Bajra Napier hybrid. Under the strict-relevance rule, the Napier-grass crop field is not confirmed by any page. The findings below are kept because the pages name this variety, but they describe it as bajra. Please verify the crop field before this record is filed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The NDUAT bajra document says the variety is moderately resistant to ergot, smut and green ear diseases, and that it performs better than check varieties against stem borer. It also reports good green biomass on salt-affected soils (about 300-320 q/ha versus 380-440 q/ha on normal soils). Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/bajra.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Moderate resistance to ergot, smut and green ear, and resistance to stem borer relative to checks (as above). -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/bajra.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Single-cut system, recommended for kharif and zaid seasons; medium-duration maturity; tall, erect plants with broad dark-green leaves; grain yield 18-20 q/ha; green biomass 380-440 q/ha on normal soils and 300-320 q/ha on salt-affected soils; dry matter 110-120 q/ha (normal) and 70-100 q/ha (salt-affected); crude protein yield 8.9-9.2 q/ha; crude protein content 8.32%. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/bajra.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020 (single-cut entry). Field-trial or multi-location results beyond these figures: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Developed by mass selection breeding (NDUAT). The Database of Forage Crop Varieties says it is a selection from NDFB-202. This conflicts with the record parentage "local selection from Saidpur, Ghazipur (U.P.)"; the sources do not mention Saidpur or Ghazipur. Breeding-line codes beyond NDFB-202, QTL/marker studies, and genome resources: No evidence found. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/bajra.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: Acharya Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology (NDUAT), which lists the variety under its research developments. Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. Station: No evidence found beyond the university. -- https://www.nduat.org/ ; https://www.nduat.org/Doc/bajra.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute website only: https://www.nduat.org/ . Official email, phone, postal address and breeder contact: No evidence found in the retrieved pages. The record's institution address (Kumarganj, Faizabad-224229) was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

PUBLICATIONS --
Authors not shown in retrieved record (2020). Database of Forage Crop Varieties: 2020. ResearchGate (entry for NDFB-3 and other forage varieties) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
NDUAT (year not shown). Narendra Chara Bajra-3 / NDFB-3 variety note. NDUAT bajra document -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/bajra.pdf
Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses (KrishiKosh) specific to this variety: No evidence found. The other bajra-napier hybrid papers returned by the search are about different varieties and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for NDFB-3 from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, or private dealers. The only seed listings returned were generic Amazon and retailer pages for Bajra Napier hybrid grass seed, which are not this variety and were discarded.

drought.details: The CSC record classes the variety as drought tolerant (stress reaction) and drought hardy (agronomic features). The digest supports this only indirectly. A transcriptomic and metabolomic study of Bundel Dinanath 2 seed from the IGFRI Jhansi collection reports drought-response pathways in this cultivar, but the digest gives no quantitative tolerance score. A germplasm study used Bundel Dinanath-2 as a check and describes Dinanath grass as drought tolerant, but that is a crop-level statement, not a cultivar test. The level is taken from the CSC designation and should be treated as provisional until a cultivar-level trial is found.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence found in the digest. The CSC record states an optimum growth temperature of 15 to 35 C. This describes adaptation and is not a heat stress test.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: CSC record: the variety possesses considerably high tolerance to leaf spot, Helminthosporium and other major diseases. Digest: leaf blight reaction was scored in a germplasm study with Bundel Dinanath-2 as a check, but no resistance rating for this cultivar was found in the text. A generic IGFRI listing describes Dinanath grass as highly resistant to leaf spot and Helminthosporium, but it does not clearly tie this to Bundel Dinanath-2, so it was not attributed. The CSC disease claim is therefore not confirmed by independent evidence in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC record: fairly high resistance to major insect pests. Digest: no evidence found in searched sources. The CSC claim is unverified.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 35000.00 to 36000.00 kg/ha. The digest contains no cultivar-specific yield evidence. The only yield figure captured (30-40 t/ha green forage yield) belongs to Bundel Dinanath 1 and was excluded.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for cultivation in the entire country except the southern zone; optimum growth temperature 15 to 35 C. Digest: general Dinanath grass agronomy (rainfall 300-800 mm, sandy loam soils, seed rate 3-4 kg/ha) is crop-level and not cultivar-specific.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif 2021 trial at a Zonal Agricultural Research Station, reported in Mysore Journal of Agricultural Sciences (2023): Bundel Dinanath-2 was among Dinanath genotypes evaluated for green forage yield, nutritional value and economics under nitrogen levels. No cultivar-specific values appear in the digest. (2) Germplasm study (Journal of Environmental Biology, 2021): Bundel Dinanath-2 was a check; leaf blight was scored, but no cultivar rating was reported. (3) Seed-quality study of caryopsis set in Bundel Dinanath-1 and Bundel Dinanath-2: the digest reports the study but no result values. No other trial results were found.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A transcriptomic and metabolomic study of Bundel Dinanath 2 reports drought-response pathways. The digest does not list specific genes or pathway names.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bundel Dinanath-2 (Dinanath grass, Pennisetum pedicellatum)
Name note: The CSC name "Bundel Dinanath-2" and the Seednet name "BUNDEL DINANATH-2" are the same variety, so all evidence below refers to that name. No result gave the variety code A0604004 or the 1987 release.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought-stress transcriptomic and metabolomic study of Bundel Dinanath 2 seed from the IGFRI Jhansi collection; the paper reports drought-response pathways in this cultivar -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11452992 and https://bmcplantbiol.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12870-024-05579-3
- Germplasm study that used Bundel Dinanath-2 as a check; it describes Dinanath grass as a drought-tolerant multipurpose species, but this is a crop-level statement, not a cultivar test -- http://www.jeb.co.in/journal_issues/202109_sep21/paper_19.pdf
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Leaf blight reaction was scored in the Journal of Environmental Biology germplasm study, with Bundel Dinanath-2 as check; no resistance rating for this cultivar was found in the text -- http://www.jeb.co.in/journal_issues/202109_sep21/paper_19.pdf
- A generic IGFRI forage-variety listing names Dinanath grass as highly resistant to leaf spot and Helminthosporium, but it does not clearly tie this to Bundel Dinanath-2, so I did not attribute it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Forage yield, nutritional value and economics of Dinanath genotypes under nitrogen levels, with Bundel Dinanath-2 among the genotypes, kharif 2021, Zonal Agricultural Research Station (Mysore Journal of Agricultural Sciences 2023) -- https://www.old.uasbangalore.edu.in/images/2023-2nd-Issue/38.pdf
- Dinanath grass agronomy in general (rainfall 300–800 mm, sandy loam, seed rate 3–4 kg/ha); not cultivar-specific -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/168495
- Seed-quality study of caryopsis set in Bundel Dinanath-1 and Bundel Dinanath-2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322466248_Innovative_Technologies_for_Quality_Seed_Production_and_Vegetative_Multiplication_in_Forage_Grasses
- Yield figures for this cultivar: No evidence found (the only yield figure captured, 30–40 t/ha GFY, is for Bundel Dinanath 1, so it was excluded -- https://igfri.org.in/CropImprovement.aspx)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (mutant progeny of exotic material, pedigree 3808-4-2-1): No evidence found in search results; the parentage given in the input was not verified.
- Breeding-line codes, breeding method, markers, QTL: No evidence found for this cultivar. The IGFRI genome-wide association project on Dinanath grass (PI Shashikumara, 2025–2028) is crop-level and does not name this cultivar, so it was excluded -- https://igfri.org.in/CropImprovement.aspx
- Transcriptome and metabolome profiles of Bundel Dinanath 2 (drought) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11452992
- Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi. The BMC study states that the Bundel Dinanath 2 seed was obtained from IGFRI's Dinanath accession collection -- https://bmcplantbiol.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12870-024-05579-3
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found in the search results.
- Breeding programme page: The IGFRI crop improvement page lists Dinanath work but no breeder for this cultivar -- https://igfri.org.in/CropImprovement.aspx

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- Institute address, as printed in an affiliation of a Bundelkhand fodder paper: ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute, Jhansi-284003 (UP) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350447817_Major_Fodder_crops_and_their_high_yielding_varieties_for_the_Bundelkhand_region
- Institute phone, email, and division contact: No evidence found. The institute's own page (igfri.org.in) was returned but no contact block was captured.
- Email found on that Bundelkhand paper: subhashchand5415@gmail.com (listed as the paper's corresponding author; it is not confirmed as an official IGFRI address, and I have not attributed the cultivar to that person) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/350447817_Major_Fodder_crops_and_their_high_yielding_varieties_for_the_Bundelkhand_region

PUBLICATIONS

Unravelling the molecular mechanism underlying drought stress tolerance in Dinanath (Pennisetum pedicellatum Trin.) grass via integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. BMC Plant Biology 24, article 928 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12870-024-05579-3 (DOI: 10.1186/s12870-024-05579-3)
- Authors not captured (2021). Collection and evaluation of genetic diversity in Dinanath grass (Pennisetum pedicellatum Trin.) for forage yield and leaf blight resistance. Journal of Environmental Biology 42(5):1355-1362 -- DOI: 10.22438/jeb/42/5/MRN-1487 (http://doi.org/10.22438/jeb/42/5/MRN-1487)
- Authors not captured (2023). Green Forage Yield, Nutritional Value and Economics of Dinanath Grass Genotypes as Influenced by Nitrogen Levels. Mysore Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 2023 issue 2 -- https://www.old.uasbangalore.edu.in/images/2023-2nd-Issue/38.pdf
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Innovative Technologies for Quality Seed Production and Vegetative Multiplication in Forage Grasses -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322466248_Innovative_Technologies_for_Quality_Seed_Production_and_Vegetative_Multiplication_in_Forage_Grasses
- Authors not captured (2022). IGFRI Annual Report 2022 (mentions transcriptome and metabolic profiling of Bundel Deenanath 2) -- https://igfri.org.in/uploads/AR-2022.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses and AICRP reports for this cultivar: No evidence found (not returned by the searches).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Official seed sources (NSC, State Seed Corporation, SAU, KVK, IGFRI seed unit) for Bundel Dinanath-2: No evidence found.
- Private dealer listings for "Dinanath grass seed" (Green Fields, Jabalpur; Green Octane, Jabalpur; Pragati Nursery, Dehradun) do not name Bundel Dinanath-2, so they were discarded as unrelated products -- https://www.indiamart.com/greenfieldagroforestryproducts/grass-seed.html ; https://www.exportersindia.com/jabalpur/grass-seeds.htm ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/dinanath-grass-seeds-pennisteum-pedicellatum-7995858591.html

agronomic_details.yield: 2500.00 to 2600.00 Kg/Ha (CSC record). The digest contains no yield measurements for Bundel Guar 2.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for arid and semi-arid zones with relatively dry conditions and medium to low rainfall (CSC record). Dual purpose for gum and fodder (CSC record). Digest lists semi-arid zones of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh as recommended areas. A private listing describes all-India cultivation, especially semi-arid zones; this is an unverified commercial claim.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: In a Koshi region (Bihar) evaluation of clusterbean varieties, Bundel Guar-2 had the taller plants and the higher dry matter accumulation (32.27 g/plant reported). Described as a fodder-type variety with green fodder, dry fodder and crude protein yield as special features. CSC record also notes tolerance to lodging and freedom from pod shattering, but these were not confirmed by the digest for this variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Koshi region of Bihar evaluation of clusterbean varieties: Bundel Guar-2 showed the tallest plants and highest dry matter accumulation among the varieties compared (32.27 g/plant). Trial year, design, replication and yield figures were not retrieved. (2) Fodder-type trait description: green fodder, dry fodder and crude protein yield noted as special features; no trial values given in digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bundel Guar-2 (CSC name "Bundel Guar-2"; Seednet name "BUNDEL GUAR-2"; crop Cluster bean/guar)

Name note: All evidence below refers to "Bundel Guar 2", also written as IGFRI 2395-2. No search result was a Seednet page, so I could not confirm that the Seednet name or variety code A0606001 matches these sources.

Release date note: The input gives 1993. The sources say Bundel Guar 1 was released in 1993 and Bundel Guar 2 in 1995, with a notification dated S.O. 408(E), 4 May 1995. The 1993 date may belong to Bundel Guar 1 or be a data-entry error; this needs checking against the gazette.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No specific stress-tolerance finding for Bundel Guar 2 was found. A table that lists it as "dual purpose, suitable for drier areas with moderate rainfall" is the closest match -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf. Drought tolerance and lodging resistance are attributed to Bundel Guar 1 in other tables, so I have not attributed them to Bundel Guar 2 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/67533/28817/169501

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Bundel Guar 2. The only resistance finding (moderate resistance to leaf blight) refers to Bundel Guar 1, so I discarded it -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/67533/28817/169501

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- In a Koshi region (Bihar) evaluation of clusterbean varieties, Bundel Guar-2 had the taller plants and the higher dry matter accumulation (reported as 32.27 g/plant) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4908
-- Bundel Guar 2 is described as a fodder-type variety, with green fodder, dry fodder and crude protein yield as its special features -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384757778_Cluster_Bean_Cyamopsis_tetragonoloba

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
-- Parentage: selection from indigenous material collected at Jodhpur, accession No. 5496-2 -- https://www.leafconagro.com/guar-variety-bundel-guar-2-igfri-2395-2/ ; https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/67533/28817/169501
-- Conflicting parentage: a second IGFRI document gives the source as Durgapura (Rajasthan), accession RGC-19-1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
-- Breeding line code: IGFRI 2395-2 -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf
-- Breeding method: single plant selection from indigenous material of Rajasthan; self-pollinated; propagated through seed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
-- Genome resources and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
-- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf
-- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found in the retrieved text

CONTACT DETAILS
-- Institute-level address only: "Division of Crop Production, ICAR-IGFRI, Jhansi-284003" -- https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Agripreneurship%20Development%20On%20Value%20Added%20Fodder%20Products.pdf
-- Breeder name, role, email and phone: No evidence found
-- Institute contact page URL: not retrieved; a search for the IGFRI site was not run

PUBLICATIONS
-- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Evaluation of Clusterbean (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba L.) Varieties for Koshi Region of Bihar. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4908 (year and DOI not retrieved)
-- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Forage genetic resources at ICAR-IGFRI Jhansi: accomplishments and future strategies -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338139523_Forage_genetic_resources_at_ICAR-IGFRI_Jhansi_accomplishments_and_future_strategies (lists Bundel Guar 2 among IGFRI guar releases; year and journal not confirmed)
-- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Improved Forage Crop Varieties of IGFRI -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
-- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP reports and DOI-level papers specific to this variety: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
-- IGFRI Jhansi supplied 24 quintal of breeder seed, and farmers in Jhansi and Datia districts grew Bundel Guar 2 and Bundel Guar 3 for seed under IGFRI technical guidance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264561349_Spread_of_quality_forage_seed_and_farmers'_livelihood_improvement_An_IGFRI_initiative
-- Bundel Guar 2 is among the guar varieties in the forage seed chain, with seed-chain status for guar reported as 5 of 14 notified varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321267628_Forage_seed_production_scenario_in_India_Issues_and_way_forward
-- Private dealer listing: https://www.leafconagro.com/guar-variety-bundel-guar-2-igfri-2395-2/ (commercial source; not verified)
-- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales: No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
-- Semi-arid zone of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf ; https://dairyknowledge.in/sites/default/files/vkyadavnddb_feb_2018.pdf
-- A private seed listing describes it as suitable for all-India cultivation, especially semi-arid zones -- https://www.leafconagro.com/guar-variety-bundel-guar-2-igfri-2395-2/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRUCTURE NOTE: variety_name "RGC-197" and seednet_variety_name "RGC-197" are the same in both fields. Sources write it as "RGC 197", "RGC-197", or "RCG-197", and all of these are treated as the same variety below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No variety-specific stress evidence found. The searches returned only crop-level statements that guar is drought-tolerant and salinity-tolerant, not RGC-197 data. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391521739_PRODUCTION_TECHNOLOGY_OF_GUAR_FOR_ZONE-IIIA_RAJASTHAN (crop-level only)
RGC-197 appears among 15 or more guar genotypes in a sowing-date study, where it was sensitive to late sowing (seed yield fell at the second sowing date; timely sowing recommended until the second week of August in kharif). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/293821574_Genetic_components_of_variance_of_guar_and_its_response_to_sowing_dates_in_semi_arid_region_of_Maharashtra_India

DISEASE AND PEST
No RGC-197-specific disease or pest resistance evidence found. The pest study that names RGC-1066, HG 2-20 and RGC-1033 does not name RGC-197 in the retrieved text and was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368607560_Study_the_less_susceptible_genotype_against_major_insect_pests_on_cluster_bean
The Karan Guar-14 paper's disease resistance (bacterial blight, root rot, alternaria blight) refers to a different variety (RGr 18-1) and was discarded. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
RGC-197 was one of the superior ideotypes (with RGR 18-1 and RGR 20-15) in a Rabi 2023 evaluation of 22 gum-type guar genotypes against check MDU 1, using MGIDI selection; the trial location is not stated in the retrieved text. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/3193
A 15-genotype seed-yield trial reports RGC-197 as a single-stem line, but the retrieved table fragment gives no reliable yield values. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf
A guar production-technology guide reports 10-14 q/ha average yield for the crop generally, not for RGC-197 specifically. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391521739_PRODUCTION_TECHNOLOGY_OF_GUAR_FOR_ZONE-IIIA_RAJASTHAN
Non-official trade sites describe RGC 197 as a single-stem, flat-seeded type with about 27% gum; these are not verified sources. -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/how-to-identify-guar-seed-varieties-hgc-365-rgc-936-hg-563-rgm-112-rgc-1038.104383/
A 2024 cluster bean chapter describes RGC 197 as a selection from the Nagaur district collection, suitable for the rainy season in Rajasthan, with gum content of 32-33%. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384757778_Cluster_Bean_Cyamopsis_tetragonoloba

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: selection from local germplasm collection, Nagaur district (Rajasthan). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I used all four permitted searches, and the tool then refused a fifth, so this digest is incomplete. The search results contained little that names RGC-936 specifically. Each heading below shows what the four searches actually returned.

The CSC name and the Seednet name are both "RGC-936", so the evidence applies to both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for RGC-936.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on RGC-936 disease or pest resistance was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for RGC-936 was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) --
- A gene-regulation study on cluster bean that names the variety RGC-936 appears in a ResearchGate listing (cluster bean overview) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384757778_Cluster_Bean_Cyamopsis_tetragonoloba. I saw only a fragment, so I cannot confirm the study's design, genes or findings.
- Parentage: the input record gives E.C.248 x RGC-401. This comes from the input record, not from a search result I could verify.
- An ICAR/Krishi-type PDF (https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf) names RGC 936 only as a parent of a selection from a different cross. It is not evidence about RGC-936 itself, so I have not attributed its content to this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the breeder's name. The input record names the institution as the Plant Breeder (Guar), Rajasthan Agricultural University, A.R.S. Durgapura, Jaipur. That is from the input, not confirmed by search.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder email, phone, address or institute contact page was returned.

PUBLICATIONS -- No verified publication was found. The only related item is the ResearchGate listing above, and I could not extract its authors, year or journal from the fragment I saw. A snippet from an ICAR-related PDF (https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf) mentions RGC 936 as a parent, but its authors, year and title were not visible.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The only seed-related result was a private dealer listing for "Rookhraj Paudhshala Dried Guar Seeds" (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/dried-guar-seeds-4328565833.html). That is a different product and I have discarded it. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale page was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not verified by search. The input record lists Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. These come from the input record only.

Next steps: search Seednet (seednet.gov.in) directly for variety code A0606025, the CSC release minutes for 1989, and KrishiKosh for RGC-936 theses. Also check RAU and A.R.S. Durgapura pages for breeder contacts.

drought.details: The variety is described as drought tolerant in a Rajasthan value-chain report and in an unofficial seed-variety blog. The CSC record states it is tolerant to drought conditions and suitable under rainfed situations. A drought transcriptome study screened RGC-1038 alongside RGC-1025, RGC-1055 and RGC-1066 using germination, seedling growth, biomass, relative water content and membrane injury; the digest does not report the numerical results for RGC-1038 or name specific mechanisms for it. The Karan Guar 14 paper describes the parent RGC 1038 as suited to semi-arid, sandy loam soils under rainfed conditions in northern India. The sources give qualitative tolerance only, so 'medium' reflects an unquantified tolerance claim rather than a graded measurement.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for rainfed kharif and zaid seasons in the listed states. The CSC record states wider adaptability to rainfed conditions and suitability for late-sown, rainy and summer cultivation. The Karan Guar 14 paper describes the parent RGC 1038 as suited to semi-arid, sandy loam soils under rainfed conditions in northern India.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 76-93 cm; erect, medium-tall, highly branched habit (forum variety table). Recommended spacing 30 x 10-15 cm and fertiliser N 40, P 60, K 50 kg/ha (forum variety table). CSC features: higher grain and fodder yield, resistant to lodging and shattering, responsive to 20 kg N/ha and 40 kg P2O5/ha with 30 cm row spacing, and 20 kg seed/ha is sufficient for sowing. The Karan Guar 14 paper gives maturity of 95-105 days for the parent RGC 1038.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Organic-system trial at ICAR-NRCSS, Tabiji (Ajmer), 2016-2020: RGC-1038 led among eight cultivars for growth, seed yield, quality, harvest index and net return. (2) Sowing-date trial (1 June, 1 July, 1 August; five varieties including RGC 1038): RGC 1038 had the lowest plant population and plant height in that trial. Numerical results were not reported in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE [name: Rajasthan Guar-1038 (RGC-1038), same for variety_name and seednet_variety_name]
- A Rajasthan value-chain report describes this variety as drought tolerant and moderately resistant to bacterial blight and Alternaria blight -- https://www.tourism.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/agriculture/Rajasthan%20Agricultural%20Competitiveness%20Project/valuechainreport/RACP_VC_Guar.pdf
- A seed-variety blog gives the same drought-tolerance claim and lists moderate resistance to root rot and wilt, but it is an unofficial source -- http://aciguarclutivationinindia.blogspot.com/p/blog-page_8.html
- A drought transcriptome study screened RGC-1038 alongside RGC-1025, RGC-1055 and RGC-1066 for drought tolerance using germination, seedling growth, biomass, relative water content and membrane injury -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9274130/
- The Karan Guar 14 paper describes the parent RGC 1038 as suited to semi-arid, sandy loam soils under rainfed conditions in northern India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- No heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found.

DISEASE AND PEST [name: Rajasthan Guar-1038 (RGC-1038)]
- Moderate resistance to bacterial blight and Alternaria blight is listed -- https://www.tourism.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/agriculture/Rajasthan%20Agricultural%20Competitiveness%20Project/valuechainreport/RACP_VC_Guar.pdf
- Moderate resistance to root rot and wilt is listed in an unofficial blog -- http://aciguarclutivationinindia.blogspot.com/p/blog-page_8.html
- No pest-resistance evidence was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS [name: Rajasthan Guar-1038 (RGC-1038)]
- A variety table (forum reproduction) gives notification date 11-02-2009, average yield 1070 kg/ha, and medium maturity of 101-105 days -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/high-yielding-with-high-gum-guar-varieties-for-sale-hg-563-rgm-112-rgc-1038-rgc-936.103231/
- The same forum table records plant height of 76-93 cm, an erect, medium-tall, highly branched habit, spacing of 30 x 10-15 cm, and fertiliser of N 40, P 60, K 50 kg/ha; yield is also given as 1000-1100 kg/ha -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/officially-released-guar-varieties-details-from-agri-univerity.103226/
- The Karan Guar 14 paper gives maturity of 95-105 days for the parent RGC 1038 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Organic-system trial at ICAR-NRCSS, Tabiji (Ajmer), 2016-2020: RGC-1038 led among eight cultivars for growth, seed yield, quality, harvest index and net return -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5113
- Sowing-date trial (1 June, 1 July, 1 August; five varieties including RGC 1038): RGC 1038 had the lowest plant population and plant height in that trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390554980_Effect_of_Dates_of_Sowing_and_Varieties_on_Growth_and_Yield_of_Cluster_Bean_Cyamopsis_tetragonaloba_L_Taub_under_Rainfed_Conditions

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) [name: Rajasthan Guar-1038 (RGC-1038)]
- Parentage RGC 516 x HG 75 is given for RGC 1038 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety and https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Breeding method recorded as selection from a cross, in a cultivar-diversity table -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/5f4a/cd224de1c8e1c13fde58f92c4df5503a5f4e.pdf
- RGC-1038 was one of the parents of Karan Guar 14 (RGC 1038 x RGC 1017), a different variety; that is not evidence about this variety's own genetics -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- The Karan Guar 14 paper says RAPD-based profiling was run on that variety and both parents; the primer details were cut off in the retrieved snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety
- No QTL, marker-trait, or genome-resource evidence specific to RGC-1038 was found. The chromosome-scale cluster bean genome paper did not name this variety in the retrieved text -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10279686/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Jayee-1 (NDO-1), Oat

Name note: The CSC release name is "Narendra Jayee-1 (NDO-1)" and the Seednet name is the same. All four searches returned the same name family. The NDO 1101 (Narendra Jayee-1101) notification is a different name and is not attributed to this variety below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The NDUAT NAAC document lists Oat forage varieties Narendra Jayee-1 and Narendra Jayee-2 as suitable for salt-affected areas, developed by the university. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/NAAC/7.3%20photos.pdf
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for this variety. The searches returned no disease or pest reaction data for Narendra Jayee-1 or NDO-1.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A Central Gujarat forage trial of oat varieties reports that NDO-1 had superior growth parameters (crop growth rate, relative growth rate, leaf area index) and the highest benefit-cost ratio (2.84) among the tested varieties. The name shown is "NDO-1", which matches this variety's code, but the page does not spell out "Narendra Jayee-1". -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332106548_RELATIVE_PERFORMANCE_OF_OAT_FORAGE_VARIETIES_FOR_SEED_PRODUCTION_ECONOMICS_AND_FODDER_YIELD_UNDER_CENTRAL_GUJARAT_CONDITIONS
- A 2025 IJABR article (vol. 9, issue 2, pp. 14-17) mentions "NDO-1" in an oat yield/grain-weight context. The snippet is too fragmentary to confirm that it refers to this variety. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue2/PartA/9-1-140-704.pdf
- Yield (t/ha): No evidence found for this variety in the retrieved text.
- Maturity: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "local selection from Kothi, Barabanki (U.P.)": No evidence found in the search results. This is taken from the input record only.
- Breeding method and breeding-line codes: No evidence found for this variety. The NDO 1101 notification says that variety was developed by inter-varietal hybridization, but it is a different name and is not attributed here. -- https://justagriculture.in/files/newsletter/2024/may/40.%20NDO%201101%20(Narendra%20Jayee%20-%201101)%20dual%20purpose%20as%20well%20as%20suitable%20for%20normal%20and%20salt%20affected%20soils%20in%20U.P.%20sub-%20committee%20on%20crop%20standard,%20Notification%20of%20varieties.pdf
- QTL, markers and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The NDUAT NAAC document credits the university with developing the Narendra Jayee oat forage varieties. It does not name an individual breeder. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/NAAC/7.3%20photos.pdf
- The institution is now Acharya Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology (NDUAT), Kumarganj, Ayodhya-224229. The input record says Faizabad, and the name and location have changed. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/NAAC/7.3%20photos.pdf
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal location: Kumarganj, Ayodhya-224229 (U.P.), per the NDUAT NAAC document. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/NAAC/7.3%20photos.pdf
- Official email, phone and breeder contact: No evidence found in the search results. The institute's website is https://www.nduat.org.

PUBLICATIONS
- Relative performance of oat forage varieties for seed production, economics and fodder yield under Central Gujarat conditions. Authors not captured in the search snippet (year not captured). Journal/report not captured. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332106548_RELATIVE_PERFORMANCE_OF_OAT_FORAGE_VARIETIES_FOR_SEED_PRODUCTION_ECONOMICS_AND_FODDER_YIELD_UNDER_CENTRAL_GUJARAT_CONDITIONS (names NDO-1 only; not confirmed as Narendra Jayee-1)
- IJABR 2025; 9(2): 14-17. Authors not captured. Title not captured. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue2/PartA/9-1-140-704.pdf (ambiguous match)
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or DOI was found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The searches returned no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Narendra Jayee-1 or NDO-1. The only seed-related hits were unrelated commercial oat seed shops.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found for this variety. The input says "Unknown", and the searches did not confirm a state recommendation.

Source-level caveats: The strongest evidence is the NDUAT listing that names Narendra Jayee-1 as a salt-tolerant oat forage variety. The Gujarat paper is the only trial result, and it only names "NDO-1". The NDO 1101 notification is a different name and should not be merged into this record without the breeder's confirmation.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the States of Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra under timely sown irrigated condition suitable for single cut system. Early maturity - 90 days.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: In agronomic trials, the proposed variety OS 346 showed its superiority over the National Checks, OS 6 and Kent whereas, for DMY it was superior to the National Check Kent only. The variety responded significantly up to 80 kg N/ha for GFY at Raipur and for DMY at Jhansi whereas at Jabalpur and Raipur the similar response was observed up to 120 kg N/ha. At Jhansi and Raipur locations, the highest FGY and DMY were recorded by the proposed variety OS 346. The proposed variety OS 346 was found better in protein yield (q/ha), plant height and leaf: stem ratio as well.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 125-135 cm; b) Distinguishing morphological Characters: The proposed variety OS 346 is tall, bold seeded, suitable for single cut system and gives higher per day productivity of GFY and DMY as compared to the best check.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: The proposed variety performs better under normal sown, normal fertility and irrigated conditions under single cut regime.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The proposed variety is highly resistant to Helinthosporium leaf blight
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: There is no major problem of insect-pests.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The results are strings, so I'll parse them and check for relevant hits.STRESS TOLERANCE
Bidhan Rice Bean 1 is listed on BCKV's crop-variety page as tolerant to drought, cold and waterlogging, with a green forage yield of 35-40 t/ha. (Name evidence: "Bidhan Rice Bean 1", not the CSC name "BC-15/K-1".) -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
A review chapter reports that drought slowed germination and its speed in rice bean cultivar Bidhan 1, citing Atta and Pal et al. (2021). (Name evidence: "Bidhan 1".) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365650495_Rice_Bean_Vigna_umbellata_-_A_Potential_Legume_under_Adverse_Conditions
The same chapter notes that rice bean generally tolerates waterlogging and grows in low-fertility acidic soils; this is crop-level, not variety-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365650495_Rice_Bean_Vigna_umbellata_-_A_Potential_Legume_under_Adverse_Conditions
A BCKV Mohanpur lab study tested copper and lead stress on seedlings of rice bean cultivar Bidhan 1 (2017-18). Results are about metal-stress physiology, not field tolerance. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4820

DISEASE AND PEST
The AICRP on Forage Crops page (BCKV) says Bidhan Ricebean-1 was identified as resistant to insect pests and diseases in field and storage conditions in All-India coordinated trials. Specific diseases are not named for this variety on that sentence. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en
The same page lists yellow mosaic virus, anthracnose, stem/collar rot, wilt, aphid, foliage beetle and pod borer in a field-condition sentence, but it is not clearly tied to this variety, so it is not counted as evidence. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A variety-group page naming Bidhan-1 gives rainfed cultivation, sowing May-August, seed rate 20-25 kg/ha, spacing 40 x 30 cm, fertiliser 25:60:30 N:P:K kg/ha, green fodder harvest 100-120 days after sowing, green fodder 250-300 q/ha, and seed yield 7-10 q/ha. The page gives the botanical name as Vigna calcaratus, which conflicts with Vigna umbellata. -- https://rsfpdkalyani.com/varietymain.php?2%29=&category=Ricebean+%28Bidhan-1&id=74
The AICRP page says that Bidhan Ricebean-1 was tested in coordinated trials for three years and showed consistent superiority in green and dry matter yields. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en
The AICRP page also says it is a fodder-and-pulse type that BCKV distributed to farmers for under-canopy cropping in mango, banana and guava orchards in several West Bengal districts. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en
A 2018 Food Security chapter (ResearchGate listing) reports a gamma-ray mutagenesis study in Bidhan Ricebean-1 (BRB-1) for trait improvement. The page snippet does not show trial results. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325083152_Rice_bean_A_healthy_and_cost-effective_alternative_for_crop_and_food_diversity

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "LOCAL LAND RACE" comes from the user-supplied record. No search result confirmed it. -- user-supplied record, not web-verified
The BCKV pages give the breeding-line code only as "BCKV"; no search result gave a line code such as "BC-15" or "K-1" for this variety. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
The AICRP page says K-1 was recommended for release in West Bengal under irrigated and non-irrigated conditions, but it does not say K-1 is this variety's line code. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en
A ResearchGate review (2010s) says a rice bean variety "Bidhan (K-" was released nationally, citing Shukla et al. (2003). The snippet is truncated and does not give the name in full. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260991113_Food_Security_through_Ricebean_Research_in_India_and_Nepal_Distribution_of_RIcebean_in_Indian_and_Nepal
No QTL, marker or genome-resource study naming this variety was found. No evidence found for breeding method.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The variety is attributed to BCKV on the BCKV IPR and AICRP pages, which name the university as applicant. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
The AICRP on Forage Crops centre at BCKV holds the mandate for ricebean nucleus and breeder seed production. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en
No individual breeder or lead scientist name was found for this variety. No evidence found for named breeders.

Ohwi and Ohashi] Seedling in Response to Equimolar Concentration of Copper and Lead Stress. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4820 (year and volume not confirmed from the snippet)
