The seednet.gov.in portal was not returned in any result, so no Seednet listing was verified under either name.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified by the Government of India in 2000 for the North Eastern Zone per the AICRP page, which conflicts with the 2001 release year in the record. The page lists the adapted areas as North-Eastern, South and South-Central regions of India. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en
BCKV's crop-variety page cites a CVRC notification (S.O. No. 92(E), dated 02.02.2001) for Bidhan Rice Bean 1. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
The AICRP page says K-1 was recommended for West Bengal (Eastern Zone) under irrigated and non-irrigated conditions, and lists the adapted areas as West Bengal, Odisha, Assam, Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-forage-crops-en

NAME NOTES
CSC name "BIDHAN-1 (BC-15/K-1)": "BC-15/K-1" appears in no search result. The BCKV pages use "Bidhan Rice Bean 1" and "Bidhan Ricebean-1". The Seednet name "BIDHAN-1 (BC-15/K-1)" was not returned by any search.
Crop name: Seednet lists "RICE BEAN (RED BEAN)"; the sources use Vigna umbellata.
Excluded as other varieties or crops: Gontra Bidhan-1 (rice), Bidhan Coix-1, Bidhan Barbati-1, the 2023 rice bean transcriptomics preprint (no variety named), and Gotra Bidhan-1 rice frontline demonstrations.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Setaria-92 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Setaria-92"; all evidence below refers to that name, and the only match found was for "S-92")

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Setaria-92. The one trial found reports that S-92 gave the lowest green fodder yield among four Setaria anceps genotypes under mid-hill rainfed conditions at Palampur, so it is not a stress-tolerance claim. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308163408_Performance_of_improved_Setaria_grass_Setaria_anceps_Stapf_genotypes_at_varying_levels_of_nitrogen_under_mid_hill_of_North-Western_Himalayas

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for Setaria-92 appeared in any search. Generic Setaria disease and pest pages returned were about other species or cultivars and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Four varieties of Setaria anceps (S-20, S-21, S-92 and PSS-1) were evaluated at four levels of nitrogen (N0, N40, N80 and rates during Kharif 2010 and 2011 at CSK HPKV, Palampur, as reported by Naveen Kumar, V. K. Sood, S. R. Kantwa and Sunil Kumar. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308163408_Performance_of_improved_Setaria_grass_Setaria_anceps_Stapf_genotypes_at_varying_levels_of_nitrogen_under_mid_hill_of_North-Western_Himalayas
- S-92 produced green fodder of 14.30 t/ha, dry fodder of 3.77 t/ha and crude protein yield of 367 kg/ha, the lowest of the four genotypes; S-20 led with 25.24, 7.76 and 752 respectively. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308163408_Performance_of_improved_Setaria_grass_Setaria_anceps_Stapf_genotypes_at_varying_levels_of_nitrogen_under_mid_hill_of_North-Western_Himalayas
- The same paper's conclusion calls PSS-1, S-92 and S-20 good performers in the Himalayan region with high nutritive value and low oxalate content. This conflicts with the yield ranking in the same paper, so it should be checked against the full text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308163408_Performance_of_improved_Setaria_grass_Setaria_anceps_Stapf_genotypes_at_varying_levels_of_nitrogen_under_mid_hill_of_North-Western_Himalayas
- Excluded: the AICRP Forage Crops 2019–2023 report mentions Setaria grass silvi-pastoral and intercropping recommendations at Palampur, but does not name Setaria-92, so it was not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- No evidence found. Searches did not confirm the parentage "Setaria anceps x S. glauca" or the variety code A0612003. The S-92 entry in the trial paper is a genotype label, and no pedigree or breeding-method information is given for it. Genome and QTL papers returned concern S. viridis or S. italica and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The trial paper lists the authors as Naveen Kumar, V. K. Sood, S. R. Kantwa and Sunil Kumar, from the Department of Agronomy, Forages and Grassland Management, CSK Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya, Palampur. This is the only source naming people linked to the S-92 entry, and it does not state that they developed the variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308163408_Performance_of_improved_Setaria_grass_Setaria_anceps_Stapf_genotypes_at_varying_levels_of_nitrogen_under_mid_hill_of_North-Western_Himalayas
- The institution in the record (Forage Production & Grassland Management Centre, CSK HPKV, Palampur) is consistent with that paper's affiliation, but no source names the developing breeder for Setaria-92.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for Setaria-92 appeared. Institute-level contact should be taken from the CSK HPKV website or the Seednet listing. The research paper gives affiliation only, with no contact details.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kumar, N., Sood, V. K., Kantwa, S. R., & Kumar, S. (year not shown in snippet; trial Kharif 2010–2011). Performance of improved Setaria grass (Setaria anceps Stapf.) genotypes at varying levels of nitrogen under mid hill of North-Western Himalayas. Journal not identified in snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308163408_Performance_of_improved_Setaria_grass_Setaria_anceps_Stapf_genotypes_at_varying_levels_of_nitrogen_under_mid_hill_of_North-Western_Himalayas
- No other publications specific to Setaria-92 were found, including KrishiKosh theses and AICRP reports naming this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned only ornamental and horticultural Setaria seed sellers (for example eBay, Etsy, Amazon and Pase Seeds) and a Setaria italica listing. None of these is linked to Setaria-92 or to NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or Indian private dealers.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found. The record field reads "Unknown", and no search result gave recommended states for Setaria-92. The release year of 2003 in the record was also not confirmed by any search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bundel Anjan-1 (Cenchrus ciliaris, anjan / buffel grass). Variety code A0617002.

Name note: The CSC name "Bundel Anjan-1" and the Seednet name "BUNDEL ANJAN-1" are the same variety. All evidence below refers to that name. The four searches were run as planned. Searches 2 and 4 returned the same Grassland Congress page as search 1, and no Seednet page was retrieved.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought and frost hardiness, and moderate lodging resistance, are attributed to Bundel Anjan-1 on a variety-by-variety listing page -- https://www.leafconagro.com/anjan-grass-buffel-grass-varieties/
- Heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found for this variety. Drought tolerance for buffel grass in general appears on https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc, but that page does not single out this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Potential green fodder yield is given as 35–40 t/ha, with the variety described as palatable and nutritious at flowering -- https://www.leafconagro.com/anjan-grass-buffel-grass-varieties/
- An IGFRI variety sheet gives the variety's propagation as seed and rooted slips or tussocks, and its mode of pollination as cross-pollinated (over 80% outcrossing) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
- The same IGFRI sheet lists a fertilizer schedule under the Anjan grass section (20 kg N/ha at one month, 40 kg N in later years, 20 kg P2O5/ha at the start of rains). It is unclear whether this applies to Bundel Anjan-1 specifically or to the crop generally -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
- A multi-variety table in the Grassland Congress keynote lists "Bundel Anjan 1 (MC)" with three numeric values. The column headers were not retrieved, so the values cannot be interpreted -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc
- No multi-location trial results were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage conflict. The IGFRI variety sheet says the variety was selected from exotic material EC-397692, received from Tanzania through IGER (UK) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
- The LeafConAgro page says the variety was made by intra-population selection from IGFRIS-3108 at IGFRI Jhansi -- https://www.leafconagro.com/anjan-grass-buffel-grass-varieties/
- The input record gives parentage as indigenous material from Coimbatore, IG-69-3108. Neither IGFRI source mentions Coimbatore as the origin of this variety. The Coimbatore reference on the LeafConAgro page belongs to CO-1 (TNAU), which is a different variety.
- Breeding method: intra-population selection, per the IGFRI sheet and LeafConAgro page (both URLs above).
- One Grassland Congress passage says Bundel Anjan-1 was released through clonal selection. This conflicts with the intra-population selection evidence -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc
- Breeding-line code: IGFRIS-3108 appears as the source line (LeafConAgro page above).
- Genome resources: No evidence found. The Grassland Congress source notes that buffel grass is apomictic and that apomixis is genetically controlled, but this is about the species, not this variety -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi -- https://www.leafconagro.com/anjan-grass-buffel-grass-varieties/ and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI. The input record says "Unknown", so this should be updated.
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder contact, IGFRI email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was retrieved in these searches. Institute contact details should be taken from the IGFRI official site, which was not retrieved here.

PUBLICATIONS
- IGFRI (2015 or earlier, undated in snippet). Improved Forage Crop Varieties of IGFRI. Institute variety sheet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
- Authors not shown in snippet (undated). Recent trends in breeding of tropical grass and forage species. Review that lists Bundel Anjan-1 among Cenchrus ciliaris varieties. Only the listing was retrieved, not the body text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309253494_Recent_trends_in_breeding_of_tropical_grass_and_forage_species
- Authors not shown (2015). Proceedings of the 23rd International Grassland Congress, Keynote Lectures. Mentions Bundel Anjan-1 in a list of varieties and in a genetic-resources table -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc
- Not included: Kumar et al. (2006), on root distribution of buffel grass in western Rajasthan. It concerns buffel grass in general, not this variety, so it was excluded under the strict relevance rule.
- No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP reports or DOI-bearing journal papers on this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for this variety was retrieved. The Seednet portal entry was not reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The input record says "A AND N ISLANDS". No evidence found supporting Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
- The IGFRI variety sheet gives the recommended region as arid and semi-arid tracts of northwest India, but the snippet is cut off before the state list -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
- Release year: The IGFRI sheet cites a central notification (915(E), dated 6 November 1989), not 1987 as in the input record. A separate 1985 notification (832(E)) appears nearby on the LeafConAgro page, but it is unclear whether it refers to this variety. Verify the release year against the CSC minutes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jaisalmeri Sewan (RLSB-11-50), Cenchrus (anjan / buffel grass), code A0617004

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Jaisalmeri Sewan (RLSB-11-50)"), so all evidence below refers to that one name. Four searches were run.

CROP MISMATCH WARNING: Every page that names Jaisalmeri Sewan or RLSB 11-50 describes sewan grass (Lasiurus sindicus), not Cenchrus. Under the strict relevance rule these are discarded from the headings below and listed at the end. The crop field in the record needs checking.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for this variety in Cenchrus. Searches returned only Lasiurus sindicus (sewan) pages and buffel-grass seller pages, which were not kept.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for Cenchrus. The only trial-type hits (a sewan grass chapter and an accession fodder-yield study) concern Lasiurus sindicus and were discarded (see list below).

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage "Selection from exotic material EC-397692" was not found in any result. The RLSB 11-50 accession code appears only in a Lasiurus study (discarded below).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found that ties Jaisalmeri Sewan to a named breeder or to IGFRI Jhansi. A sewan chapter says research centres in Jaisalmer district led development of sewan varieties and names CAZRI varieties (CAZRI Sewan-1, CAZRI 317, CAZRI 319) alongside Jaisalmeri Sewan (RLSB 11-50) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77618 . This does not name a breeder or the developing institute for RLSB 11-50, so the IGFRI attribution in the record is unverified. The IGFRI-related pages found (e.g., https://igfri.org.in/uploads/AR-2022.pdf) concern other varieties or germplasm and were not kept. A private-seller page for Bundel Anjan-1 (https://www.leafconagro.com/anjan-grass-buffel-grass-varieties/) names IGFRI Jhansi but is a different variety, so it was discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact was found. No IGFRI contact page or address was captured in the results.

PUBLICATIONS -- Items naming Jaisalmeri Sewan (RLSB 11-50), all about Lasiurus sindicus and discarded from the headings:
- Sewan Grass: A Potential Forage Grass in Arid Environments. Authors and year not shown in the search results. Book chapter -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77618 (also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353365267_Sewan_Grass_A_Potential_Forage_Grass_in_Arid_Environments)
- Genetic diversity analysis of sewan grass using RAPD markers (Journal of Eco-Biotechnology, 2017 issue). Authors and title not fully captured -- https://www.jeb.co.in/journal_issues/201705_may17/paper_09.pdf (this one does not name RLSB 11-50 in the captured text)
- Accession trial with RLSB 11-50 and RLSB 4-41 fodder-yield data, Phytojournal 2019 vol 8 issue 3S (authors not captured) -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue3S/PartB/SP-8-3-13-119.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Jaisalmeri Sewan from NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet. A scribd list of IGFRI seed and slip stocks was returned, but its captured text does not name this variety, so it was not kept.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record lists RAJASTHAN, UTTAR PRADESH, ANDHRA PRADESH, HARYANA, MAHARASHTRA and PUNJAB, which no search result confirms. Sewan-grass pages place the crop in western Rajasthan and its arid desert zone, but that is for Lasiurus sindicus, so it was not kept.

DISCARDED (crop mismatch or other variety, listed for audit only):
- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353365267_Sewan_Grass_A_Potential_Forage_Grass_in_Arid_Environments (Lasiurus sindicus)
- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77618 (Lasiurus sindicus; also has the yield figures for sewan)
- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue3S/PartB/SP-8-3-13-119.pdf (Lasiurus accessions)
- https://www.jeb.co.in/journal_issues/201705_may17/paper_09.pdf (Lasiurus sindicus)
- https://garph.co.uk/IJAREAS/Mar2014/6.pdf (Lasiurus sindicus)
- https://eng.kisanofindia.com/latest-news/sewan-grass-excellent-for-animals-livestock-farmers (CAZRI sewan varieties; no Jaisalmeri Sewan)

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Uttara (Sugarcane)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Uttara", so the evidence below would refer to the same name under either heading. The crop names differ only in form ("Sugarcane" vs "SUGARCANE (NOBLE CANE)"). Searches ran for 4 queries: "Uttara Sugarcane variety", "Uttara Sugarcane breeder institute", "Uttara Sugarcane research paper", and "Uttara sugarcane seed availability". None of the returned pages mentions Uttara, so no finding was kept.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The variety search returned a UP sugarcane disease-status paper that discusses other cultivars (for example Co 0238) and does not name Uttara.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The same disease-status paper does not name Uttara, so it is not kept.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No returned page reports Uttara yield, maturity, or trial results.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. Nothing returned confirms the parentage CO 62198 x COC671 or the code A0701002. Those values come only from the task input and are not verified here.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The breeder query returned a general page on the Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research, Lucknow, which is a different institute from the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore named in the input, and it does not name Uttara. It is not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore contact page or breeder contact was returned, so no email, phone, or address is recorded.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The research query returned a general Academia.edu sugarcane cultivation listing with no Uttara-specific title, author, or DOI.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The seed query returned a ChiniMandi item on a Uttar Pradesh seed-availability app, which is about UP seed information in general and does not name Uttara.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in search results. The only state information is the input value "GUJARATMAHARASHTRATAMILNADU", which is unverified. Recommend checking the CSC release notification and the Seednet record directly.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal entry for A0701002, the CSC release minutes for 1998, and the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore website and KrishiKosh. These sources were not reachable with the search tool.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Snippet from the TNAU Expert System page says Co 87025 (Kalyani) is tolerant to drought and waterlogging (the page lists these traits as "tolerant to drought and water logging"). -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/season&varieties.html

DISEASE AND PEST -- Same TNAU page snippet says Co 87025 (Kalyani) is resistant to smut and field resistant to red rot. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/season&varieties.html

disease_resistance.summary: Smut: resistant (TNAU expert system; Indian Sugar 2001 note via eurekamag). Input record: moderately resistant to red rot and smut. Red rot: conflicting evidence. Moderately susceptible in the Navsari nodal-method test and in the TNAU list; input record states moderately resistant. Rust: recommended as a resistant variety for rust control (TNAU crop protection page and Map My Crop guide). General: built-in resistance to major pests and some diseases per the 2001 Indian Sugar note. Ratoon and red rot evidence should be checked against the primary release record.

pest_resistance.summary: Input record: field resistant to all pests. Digest: built-in resistance to major pests and some diseases per the 2001 Indian Sugar note. No variety-specific shoot borer, top borer, stalk borer or YLD data for Co 91010. The AICRP zone-wise pest text (least susceptible to shoot borer) was excluded because it appears to belong to a variety released in 2020.

agronomic_details.yield: Cane yield 116000 kg/ha (input record, equal to 116.0 t/ha). Navsari trial (2001 note): mean cane yield 134.2 t/ha, CCS 15.46 t/ha, sucrose 19.09%. Coimbatore centre table: 116.00 t/ha, sucrose 19.10%, 11,818 ha. Release table (PZ): cane yield 116.0 t/ha, sucrose 19.1%.
agronomic_details.stability: Wide adaptability is stated in the Coimbatore centre page, which also says it has been cultivated over 1 million ha in tropical India from 2007-08 onward. This is a general statement and should be checked before citing. Consistent 116 t/ha value across several tables; the Navsari value is from a single trial.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Peninsular zone (release table). Suitable for Kerala (TNAU list). Adapted to normal soils under irrigated conditions (input record). Performs well in North Karnataka under water-deficit conditions. Ratoon performance best under wide row spacing, after Co 94005.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: MEDIUM THICK ERECT YELLOWISH GREEN CANE WITH LONG INTERNODES, EASY TRASHING WITH SPINOUS LEAF SHEATH.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Navsari (Gujarat) trial, 2001 note: sucrose 19.09%, CCS 15.46 t/ha, mean cane yield 134.2 t/ha. (2) Release table, Peninsular Zone: cane yield 116.0 t/ha, sucrose 19.1%. (3) Coimbatore centre table: 11,818 ha, 116.00 t/ha, sucrose 19.10% (listed as Co 91010 in a table; no separate page confirms it). (4) North Karnataka water-deficit and Striga-infected field results: good yield and sucrose retention, and merit in Striga-infected fields. (5) Ratoon trial: best ratoon performance under wide row spacing, after Co 94005. Planting window Nov.-Jan. is shown in the release table (mid-season planting in Kerala/TN context). Planting material from 6-8-month-old disease-free nursery crop with two-budded setts preferred (organic package, TNAU; secondary blog source).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Dhanush (CO 91010), sugarcane

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical here ("Dhanush (CO 91010)"). The evidence below uses the forms "Dhanush (Co 91010)" and "Co 91010 (Dhanush)". The seednet portal was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-page evidence was found. Searches run: 4 (variety/traits, breeder/institute, research, seed).

Discrepancies to check against the release record:
- Release year: the input says 1998. The AICRP table gives 1999 (mid-late), the Map My Crop table gives 2000, and the Vikaspedia list gives 2000. A PPV&FRA entry also appears in the search results. The 1998 date was not confirmed.
- Recommended states: the input says Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. The evidence names peninsular zone, especially North Karnataka, plus Kerala (TNAU list) and a Navsari (Gujarat) trial. Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu were not confirmed for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to drought, per the TNAU expert system for sugarcane (Kerala list) -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/season&varieties.html
- Tall, erect, non-lodging canes with a deep root system, yielding well and keeping sucrose under water-deficit conditions in North Karnataka -- http://agrinnovateindia.com/subTechnologyDescription?id=532&Subtitle=Sugarcane+Variety+Co+19010+-+Dhanush&Techtitle=ICAR-Sugarcane+Breeding+Institute+(SBI)
- Showed merit in Striga-infected fields in North Karnataka -- http://agrinnovateindia.com/subTechnologyDescription?id=532&Subtitle=Sugarcane+Variety+Co+19010+-+Dhanush&Techtitle=ICAR-Sugarcane+Breeding+Institute+(SBI)
- Waterlogging, salinity, heat and flood tolerance: No evidence found for this variety. The TNAU Kerala list gives waterlogging tolerance for other varieties (Madhurima, Madhumathi), not Co 91010.
- Best ratoon performance under wide row spacing, after Co 94005 -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5516

DISEASE AND PEST
- Smut: resistant -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/season&varieties.html ; https://eurekamag.com/research/003/463/003463594.php
- Red rot: moderately susceptible (Navsari nodal-method test) -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/463/003463594.php
- Red rot: moderately susceptible (TNAU list) -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/season&varieties.html
- Rust: recommended as a resistant variety for rust control -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/cropprotection.html ; https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-crop-guide/
- Built-in resistance to major pests and some diseases, per the 2001 Indian Sugar note -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/463/003463594.php
- Shoot borer, top borer, stalk borer, red rot and YLD: the AICRP varietal-development page contains zone-wise resistance text (for example, "least susceptible to shoot borer" and "moderately resistant to red rot and YLD"). That text appears to belong to a variety released in 2020, not Co 91010, so it was excluded -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mid-late variety maturing in about 360 days -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/463/003463594.php
- Sucrose 19.09%, CCS 15.46 t/ha, mean cane yield 134.2 t/ha (Navsari trial, 2001 note) -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/463/003463594.php
- Cane yield 116.0 t/ha and sucrose 19.1% (PZ, release table) -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/ ; https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
- Coimbatore centre table: 11,818 ha, 116.00 t/ha, sucrose 19.10% -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/coimbatore.htm (listed as Co 91010 in a table; no separate page confirms it)
- Wide adaptability; cultivated over 1 million ha in tropical India from 2007-08 onward (Coimbatore centre page). This is a general statement and should be checked before citing.
- Planting in the Kerala/TN context: mid-season, Nov.–Jan. planting window is shown for the variety in the release table -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
- Planting setts from 6–8-month-old disease-free nursery crop, two-budded setts preferred (organic package, TNAU) -- https://nataliaphule.wordpress.com/2013/12/05/my-tryst-with-organic-farming-on-the-farm/ (secondary blog source)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: Co 312 × Co 775 -- https://eurekamag.com/research/003/463/003463594.php

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nayana (CO 86032), sugarcane

Name note: the release-minutes name "Nayana (CO 86032)" and the Seednet name are the same variety. Sources mostly use "Co 86032" and some use "Nayana"; each finding below says which name its page uses. Searches run: (1) variety and traits, (2) breeder and institute, (3) research papers, (4) institute contacts. No separate seed-dealer search was run; seed findings came from results of searches 1 to 3.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought: described as tolerant to drought, with Tamil Nadu districts listed as performing well under drought (Co 86032 / Nayana) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_seasonandvarieties_sugarcane.html ; https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm (named as drought tolerant in the Padegaon table via the AICRP Forty Five Years summary) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane ; https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/ (Co 86032 (Nayana) listed as tolerant to drought, good ratooner)
Salinity: a Scribd summary (AI-enhanced description, low reliability) says it is resilient to drought and salinity (Nayana / Co 86032) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/855558763/Nayana-1 . No independent source confirmed this.
Heat, flood, submergence: No evidence found. Searches returned no statements on these stresses for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Smut: resistant (mapmycrop; AICRP Forty Five Years table lists "R to smut") -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane . A Scribd overview says "moderately resistant to smut" (Co 86032), which conflicts with "resistant" -- https://www.scribd.com/document/854856215/Co-86032
Red rot: field tolerant (Co 86032 / Nayana) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane ; https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
Wilt: moderately resistant (Co 86032) per a review on sugarcane breeding and genomics -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336537202_Sugarcane_Saccharum_spp_Breeding_and_Genomics
Woolly aphid: a fragment of an AICRP-related ResearchGate page describes Co 86032 as a susceptible check for woolly aphid screening; this is not a clear resistance rating -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: midlate (Co 86032 / Nayana) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
Season suitability: suru, preseason and adsali seasons (Co 86032 (Nira)) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm
Yield: cane yield 102.0 t/ha and sugar yield 20.1 (table entry, Co 86032 (Nayana)) -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/ ; cane yield 159.0 t/ha and sugar yield 22.50 t/ha in adsali conditions (Co 86032, Scribd overview; low reliability) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/854856215/Co-86032 ; a Padegaon AICRP table lists

EVIDENCE DIGEST: CoOr 03151 (Sabita), Sugarcane

Name check: The release minutes and Seednet both use "CoOr 03151", and the evidence refers to the same variety under that name and the cultivar name "Sabita". No Seednet page was retrieved, so the Seednet entry (code A0701008, "SUGARCANE (NOBLE CANE)") is unverified.

- Year of release: the record says 1998. Sources say the variety was identified in 2009 and released and notified in 2011 (S.O. 2326(E)).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Moti (CO 87268), Sugarcane

Search note: four web_search queries ran, one per topic. A fifth call to re-read full page text hit the tool's usage limit, so the findings below come from search snippets, not full pages. Snippets were truncated, so several headings have gaps.

Name note: "variety_name" (CSC minutes) and "seednet_variety_name" (Seednet) are both "Moti (CO 87268)". Evidence found used "Co 87268" and "Co 87268" in tables, which matches the same variety code. No separate Seednet page was retrieved.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches did not return a stress-tolerance statement (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) for Co 87268.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Co 87268 is listed as moderately resistant to red rot in a table row of recommended varieties (snippet truncated; full row not retrieved) -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Co 87268 is named among five early-maturing varieties reported by the Motipur regional centre as achievements for the north central zone (snippet truncated before full zone and trial details) -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/9025
The AICRP varietal development page lists Co 87268 in its table of varieties, but the retrieved snippet showed only a neighbouring entry (Co 87263, early), so no yield data for Co 87268 was confirmed -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. Parentage (BO 91 x CO 62399) comes from the input record only and was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Motipur regional centre (Muzaffarpur, Bihar) of the Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research is credited with Co 87268 among its early-maturing releases; A.D. Pathak is named as Nodal Officer in that report -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/9025
The vikaspedia document attributes the recommended-variety list to the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
Lead breeder name for Co 87268: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No direct contact for this variety was found. Institute-level pointer only: the ICAR regional-centre report (Motipur) is the source for the centre's identity; no email, phone or postal address was in the retrieved snippets -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/9025

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for a paper, report or thesis specifically on Co 87268. The ResearchGate entry "Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane" was returned, but its snippet did not mention Co 87268, so it is not listed as evidence -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Co 87268 was returned. The seed search was run but yielded only the Motipur regional-centre page, which does not mention seed supply.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (from the input record; not independently confirmed). Partial support: the Motipur report links Co 87268 to the north central zone -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/9025

Release year (1998): from input record only; no search result confirmed it.

Gaps to close next: fetch the full vikaspedia PDF row and the icar.org.in node 9025 text; search the AICRP varietal pages for Co 87268's zone and yield data; check KrishiKosh and the SBI Coimbatore site for release notification and breeder names; check Seednet directly.

drought.details: Described as tolerant to drought in several digest sources, without a graded rating. The AICRP-based source describes it as moderately resistant to red rot and tolerant to drought and salinity. The vikaspedia and mapmycrop sources list drought tolerance among its traits, and the book chapter describes it as tolerant to early drought. The CSC record describes it as tolerant to drought and suitable for rainfed conditions. No physiological mechanism was reported in the digest.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest contains no heat-stress evidence for this variety.

salinity.details: One digest source (AICRP-based publication) describes the variety as tolerant to salinity. This is a single source and is not corroborated by the other sources, so the level is provisional.

flood.details: Waterlogging tolerance is reported consistently across digest sources, and the CSC record states tolerance to water logging and suitability for waterlogged situations. The digest does not report a flood-specific test, so the waterlogging evidence is applied here as the closest match. No degree of tolerance is quantified.

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: reported as moderately resistant (MR) in the AICRP-based publication, and as resistant in the mapmycrop source, the vikaspedia source, the book chapter entry (red-rot-resistant) and the CSC record. Smut: reported as MR in the AICRP-based publication, and as resistant in the mapmycrop source and the vikaspedia source (smut resistance listed). The sources disagree on the degree of resistance for both diseases; the CSC record (input data, no URL) states resistant to red rot and smut. No other disease evidence was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Early shoot borer: reported as resistant in the mapmycrop source and in the CSC record, and as tolerant to shoot borer in the AICRP-based publication. Other pests: the CSC record states tolerance to all other pests, but the digest contains no independent evidence for other pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Adsali crop about 200 t/ha, 16.9% above Co 86032 (AICRP-based publication). This conflicts with the CSC record, which gives an average yield of 80000-100000 Kg/Ha (80-100 t/ha). The 200 t/ha figure refers to the adsali crop only. The CSC figure is treated as the reference value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports results from pre-season, suru and adsali plantings but no multi-environment stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for spring, autumn and adsali (18-month) planting (AICRP-based publication). The CSC record recommends it for eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, for rainfed and waterlogged situations, for low-input conditions, and for late planting after wheat harvest. It lodges under heavy fertilizer application. The digest also lists West Bengal and Jharkhand under zone NCZ (AICRP-based publication). These states are not in the CSC record and are not verified against it, so they are not included in the standardized recommended states.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: MEDIUM THICK PURPLE CANE WITH GREEN TINGE, NO SPLITS, BUD GROOVES PRESENT, BIG BUDS, MANY SOFT SPINES ON GREEN LEAF SHEATH, LIGULAR PROCESS PRESENT.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Pre-season and suru planting: cane yield higher than existing varieties (AICRP-based publication). (2) Adsali planting: about 200 t/ha, +16.9% over Co 86032 (AICRP-based publication). (3) AICRP-based table: entry for zone NCZ with a year of 2000, listing values 66.3 and 17.4 for sugar/quality; the table labels are not clear, so these values are not interpreted. (4) Vikaspedia recommended-list entry: early maturity and tolerance to drought and waterlogging, listed in a garbled table (Feb.-March row), treated as unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Sarayu (CO 87263), Sugarcane

Name note: The CSC release minutes name is "Sarayu (Co 87263)" and the Seednet name is "Sarayu (CO 87263)". Findings below refer to the same variety under both spellings unless stated otherwise. Four web searches were run. The search tool returned no Seednet portal page for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as moderately resistant to red rot and tolerant to drought and salinity; the adsali crop yielded about 200 t/ha, 16.9% above Co 86032 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Tolerant to drought and waterlogging (listed among its traits) -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
- Tolerant to drought and water logging; early, resistant to smut and red rot, resistant to early shoot borer -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
- Described as early, waterlogging-tolerant and red-rot-resistant, and tolerant to early drought (in a book chapter, the entry is for Co-87263 (Sarayu)) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant (MR) to red rot; MR to smut; tolerant to shoot borer -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Resistant to smut and red rot, resistant to early shoot borer -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
- Smut and red rot resistance also listed -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Suitable for spring, autumn and adsali (18-month) planting; in pre-season and suru planting, cane yield was higher than existing varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Adsali yield about 200 t/ha, +16.9% over Co 86032 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Early-maturing; the table lists sugar/quality values (66.3 and 17.4) and zone NCZ, with a 2000 year -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/ and https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
- Early maturity, tolerant to drought and waterlogging, listed in the recommended list (Feb.–March row in a garbled table; treat as unverified) -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Co 312 x Co 6806 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Breeding method: biparental crossing followed by clonal selection -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
- Breeding-line code: Co 87263 (the "CO 87263" code itself) -- same source as above
- No QTL, marker, or genome study for this variety was found in the search results. No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore (ICAR), per the AICRP release table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Named lead breeder or scientist: No evidence found. The breeder search returned no named breeder for this variety.
- Station: Motipur research centre is named in the release minutes but no page describing it was returned -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
- Sugarcane Breeding Institute (ICAR), Coimbatore; Address: 641 007, Coimbatore; Tel +91 422 247 2621; Fax +91 422 247 2923; Email info@sugarcane.res.in; Website www.sugarcane.res.in -- https://www.asti.cgiar.org/india/directory/sugarcane-breeding-institute (note: this directory record is dated 2009)
- Institute website: http://www.sugarcane.res.in/ -- https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q24939773
- Motipur research centre address/phone/email: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS (Author(s) (Year). Title. Journal/Report -- URL/DOI)
- AICRP on Sugarcane, ICAR-IISR (year not stated in the extracted text). Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane. Publication (AICRP) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Dutta, D.; Ghosh, K. (2024). Sugarcane. Book chapter, Jaya Publishing House (Vol. I, pp. 160–177) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane (author list shown partly; the Sarayu entry sits in the chapter table)
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper specific to Sarayu (Co 87263) was found. No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet: No evidence found. No Seednet variety page was returned.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for Sarayu: No evidence found. A blog lists Sarayu among popular varieties but gives no seller or stock details -- https://www.bighaat.com/kisan-vedika/blogs/field-preparation-for-sugarcane (not used as availability evidence).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Jharkhand, under the zone NCZ -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Also listed under Uttar Pradesh in the state-wise recommended table -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
- Input field said "BIHARUTTAR PRADESH", which matches Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION
- Notification: S.O. 821(E) of 2000 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Year discrepancy: the input record says 1998; the sources list 2000 for the release/notification year. Flag for checking against the CSC minutes.

DISCARDED RESULTS
- "CoN 87263" in the Gujarat list on sugarcane.res.in is a different code and was not used -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=4852
- Hits for "Sarayu" in other crops or products were excluded.

drought.details: Tolerance to drought is recorded in the CSC release record ("TOLERANT TO DROUGHT"). A separate AICRP-based list describes the variety as tolerant to drought and mid-late maturing. Both sources describe tolerance without a graded scale, so the 'medium' level is an assignment based on the qualitative term 'tolerant' and not a reported rating. The digest lists this trait for CoM 88121 (Krishna) as part of the 2000 notified entry. No physiological mechanisms were reported.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance data were found for this variety.

flood.details: Waterlogging tolerance appears in a 1997 row that lists "CoM 88121 & Co 8371" together. It cannot be confidently attributed to CoM 88121 alone, so no level is assigned.

disease_resistance.summary: Smut: The CSC release record describes the variety as MODERATELY RESISTANT TO SMUT. Smut resistance is also recorded for CoM 88121 (Krishna) in the ResearchGate AICRP review, in a Vikaspedia package-of-practices table, and in a 2025 review that names CoM 88121 (CoM7714) (Krishna) as disease resistant. No other disease resistance data were found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No insect-pest resistance data were found specific to this variety. The CSC record lists pest reaction as Unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC release record (kg/ha): Suru 115000; Preseason 135000; Adsali 160000 (equivalent to 115, 135 and 160 t/ha cane). Padegaon station table (t/ha cane / sugar): Suru 115 / 14.05; Preseason 130 / 18.50; Adsali 166 / 23.00. The 2000 AICRP notification (peninsular zone): 88.7 t/ha cane and 18.6 t/ha sugar. An indiaagronet page reports 116 t/ha cane, 14.4 t/ha sugar and 12.4% recovery. The preseason and sugar values differ between sources and are reported as published.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Multi-location stability data were not found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for heavy to medium black soils under irrigated conditions (CSC release record). Responsive to fertilizers. Semi-lodging, non-breaking at nodes. Peninsular zone per the 2000 AICRP notification.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SPARSE FLOWERING, HIGH TILLERING, THIN CANE WITH WAX ON INTERNODES. Semi-lodging and non-breaking at nodes (CSC release record). Maturity is described as midlate in the AICRP and VSI sources and as late in the Padegaon station table.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Padegaon station table: Suru, preseason and adsali cane yields of 115, 130 and 166 t/ha, and sugar yields of 14.05, 18.50 and 23.00 t/ha, with late maturity and a rating of High. (2) VSI breeding-gallery PDF: midlate maturity, adsali cane yield 166.0 t/ha, sugar yield 23.0 t/ha. (3) indiaagronet: cane yield 116 t/ha, sugar 14.4 t/ha, 12.4% recovery. (4) 2000 AICRP notification (peninsular zone): 88.7 t/ha cane, 18.6 t/ha sugar, midlate. Multi-location trial data beyond these station and AICRP tables were not found.

Most evidence below refers to "CoM 88121 (Krishna)" or "CoM 88121 (CoM 7714)", which are the same variety under the two names. The ICAR/AICRP and Padegaon sources use both names. Each finding says which name appears on the page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought tolerance is listed for CoM 88121 (Krishna) as a trait of the 2000 notified entry, with smut resistance also noted -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- A separate AICRP-based list describes it as tolerant to drought and mid-late maturing -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
- Waterlogging tolerance appears in a 1997 row that lists "CoM 88121 & Co 8371" together, so it cannot be confidently attributed to CoM 88121 alone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- No submergence, heat or salinity data were found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to smut is recorded for CoM 88121 (Krishna) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Smut resistance is also listed in a Vikaspedia package-of-practices table and in a 2025 review that names CoM 88121 (CoM7714) (Krishna) as disease resistant -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf ; https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue1/PartG/8-1-82-255.pdf
- No insect-pest resistance data were found specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is midlate, with the 2000 notification listing the entry as midlate (88.7 t/ha cane, 18.6 t/ha sugar, peninsular zone) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- Padegaon station table: CoM 88121 (CoM 7714)(Krishna), 1993, Suru/preseason/adsali yields listed as 115/130/166 t/ha cane and 14.05/18.50/23.00 t/ha sugar, late maturity, high (rating given as "High") -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm
- A VSI breeding-gallery PDF records maturity as midlate and adsali cane yield 166.0 t/ha, sugar yield 23.0 t/ha -- https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoM%2088121.pdf
- An indiaagronet page reports cane yield 116 t/ha, sugar 14.4 t/ha, and 12.4% recovery for "Co 88121 (Krishna)" -- https://indiaagronet.com/indiaagronet/Crop_Husbandry/contents/important_varieties_of_sugarcane.htm
- Multi-location trial data beyond these station and AICRP tables were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Co 740 x Co 6806 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm ; https://www.vsisugar.com/vsi_admin/images/sugarcane_breeding_gallery/CoM%2088121.pdf
- Breeding method: biparental crossing followed by clonal selection -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
- Breeding-line code: CoM 7714 is the alternate designation (CoM 88121 (CoM 7714)) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm
- Distinguishing morphological characters (leaf sheath, internode and node-bud traits) are recorded in the PPV&FRA journal passport data -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvj-december-2012.pdf
- No QTL, marker or genome-resource studies were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The release is from the Central Sugarcane Research Station (CSRS), Padegaon, under the AICRP on Sugarcane -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm ; https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- The Padegaon page lists K.D. Bhoite as Sugarcane Breeder at the station. This is a current station role and is not verified as the developer of this variety -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm
- Original developer names for this variety were not found on any page.
- Applicant for PPV&FRA registration: Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvj-december-2012.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Central Sugarcane Research Station, Padegaon, P.O. Nira, Distt. Pune-412102 (address as given in the release record). Station is about 75 km from Pune on the Pune-Satara State Highway -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/padegaon.htm

PUBLICATIONS
- Plant Authority Journal (2012). Notification and passport data for Co M 7714 (Krishna)/Co M 88121, PPV&FRA Plant Variety Journal Vol. 6 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvj-december-2012.pdf

ResearchGate review that tabulates the variety and its traits -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Authors not stated (2000). AICRP sugarcane varietal development table, lists CoM 88121 (CoM 7714) with 2000 identification -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- No peer-reviewed papers, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

RECOMMENDED STATES

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pramod (B.O. 128), Sugarcane
Names: "Pramod (B.O. 128)" (CSC minutes) and "PRAMOD (B.O. 128)" (Seednet). None of the four searches returned a Seednet page, so every finding below refers to the name Pramod / BO 128 in general sugarcane sources. I checked each page for this variety and crop. Pages on other varieties, other crops, or unrelated people and companies named Pramod were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Tolerant to waterlogging and saline-sodic soil -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE: Tolerant to waterlogging, reported in a variety table -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
STRESS TOLERANCE: Drought tolerance is listed for the related variety CoH 128, not for BO 128, so it is not attributed here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane

DISEASE AND PEST: Moderately resistant to red rot and smut -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST: Moderately resistant (MR) to red rot, per the variety table -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
DISEASE AND PEST: Reaction to red rot recorded as R to MR, and least susceptible to shoot, top and stalk borers. The page does not name BO 128 in that passage, so I have not attributed it -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Recommended for Feb-March planting in the North Central Zone, with midlate maturity -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Mean cane yield 69.2 t/ha, with a sugar-related value of 17.6 in the same row, under the North Central zone -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: BO 128 is listed as a variety under the AICRP varietal development table (North Central Zone, released 2001). The table gives no trial yield for it -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Recommended in the 1999 AICRP midlate group alongside CoP 9103, with a 2001 notification year for BO 128 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A table row for BO 128 shows ML 88.0, 11.0 and 1993. The meaning of these columns is unclear, and the 1993 year conflicts with the 2001 release, so this row needs checking -- https://rpcau.ac.in/sri/

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage B.O.85 x B.O.43 comes from the input record only. No independent source confirmed it -- (input record, not a web source)
GENETICS AND QTL: Breeding method is biparental crossing followed by clonal selection -- https://mapmycrop.com/sugarcane-in-india/
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found for QTL, marker studies, breeding-line codes, or genome resources for this variety

The release gazette is cited as S.O. 92(E) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The institute page describes the mandate of breeding high-yielding, high-sucrose varieties for North Central and North Eastern zones. It names staff, but no breeder is linked to BO 128 -- https://rpcau.ac.in/sri/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found for the lead breeder's name for this variety

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found for an official email, phone, or postal address for this variety or its breeder. Institute-level page only: Sugarcane Research Institute, Pusa, Bihar -- https://rpcau.ac.in/sri/ (no email or phone was captured from the search content; check the page's contact section directly)

PUBLICATIONS:
Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane. (Year not captured). AICRP report entry listing BO 128 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane

drought.details: Described as drought tolerant and performing well under drought in TNAU station and Expert System pages (qualitative wording, no graded trial scores). Also listed as drought tolerant for many Tamil Nadu districts. A secondary blog states resistance to drought. The digest does not describe the mechanism.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: A field study under poor-quality saline irrigation water with pressmud amendment reported this variety performed best among tested varieties. Authors and year were not captured, and the rating is relative to the other tested varieties, so the level is an inference from a single study.

flood.details: Described as withstanding water logging (TNAU station pages), and as tolerant to late water logging conditions (CSC agronomic features). The digest does not give a graded score or mechanism.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to red rot (TNAU Expert System and TNAU Sirugamani station page). Moderately resistant to smut (TNAU Sirugamani station page). No other disease reaction evidence was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to early shoot borer, per a secondary blog that is not an official source. Scale-insect or other pest reaction: No evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: plant crop 154.5 t/ha; ratoon crop 148.0 t/ha. TNAU release table: cane yield 148.0 t/ha, CCS 12.3%. TNAU particulars table: cane yield 142.0 t/ha, CCS 13.1%, sugar 18.6 t/ha. These sources do not fully agree, and the basis of each figure is not stated.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources as a formal multi-environment stability analysis. Performance is reported across several trials and locations (see field_trials).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for all sugarcane growing areas of Tamil Nadu, especially the Delta zone and Salem (CSC record). Early season suitability is noted. TNAU district-level lists include Pudukkottai, Erode, Karur, Namakkal and Salem, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri, Virudhunagar, Tirunelveli and Tuticorin.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 360 To 360Days (CSC record). TNAU particulars table: early season, duration 10-11 months.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC agronomic features: very thick and erect canes, non-lodging, non-flowering, easily detrashable, very good ratooner, suitable for early season planting. Morphological characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) TNAU particulars table: cane yield 142.0 t/ha, CCS 13.1%, sugar 18.6 t/ha. (2) TNAU release table: cane yield 148.0 t/ha, CCS 12.3%. (3) SRS Sirugamani clone trial, 2012-13: used as best standard, cane yield 127.30 t/ha, sugar yield on par with Co 86032. (4) Pressmud-based poor-water trial: good germination, more internodes, higher millable cane length and single cane weight. (5) SSI trial, sandy clay loam soils, Trichy district: highest value in the trial. (6) TNAU 2021 scientists' meet table: 158.5 / 12.4 / 19.6, column meanings unconfirmed.

Drought tolerant; withstands water logging; performs well in alkali soils -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/srs-sirugamani/crop-improvement/

drought.details: Described as tolerant to drought by TNAU Expert System (drought- and salinity-tolerant), ICAR-SBI Plant Breeding page (tolerant to early drought), and Krishi Jagran (tolerant to drought and water logging). Original variety data states it performs better than the standard under water stress. The digest gives only qualitative 'tolerant' statements with no degree or quantitative comparison, so the level is recorded as medium.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest states that heat tolerance evidence was not found.

salinity.details: Tolerant to salinity per the 45-year AICRP document, which lists drought and salinity together. TNAU Expert System also describes the variety as salinity-tolerant. The degree of tolerance is not stated, so the level is recorded as medium.

flood.details: Tolerance to water logging is reported by ICAR-SBI Plant Breeding page (tolerant to early drought and water logging), Krishi Jagran (tolerant to drought and water logging), and Sugar Lab blog (suitable for less fertile soil and waterlogged conditions; secondary source). The original variety data also records tolerance to water logging and good sprouting during winter. Waterlogging is recorded here as the closest available evidence for flood stress; the digest reports no flood or submergence tolerance as such. Level recorded as medium because the degree is not quantified.

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: conflicting reports. Moderately resistant per Sugar Lab blog (secondary source) and Krishi Jagran; described as resistant per ICAR-SBI Plant Breeding page. The conflict is unresolved in the digest. Wilt: tolerant to wilt per Apni Kheti blog (secondary source; the blog also attributes development to IARI, which is inconsistent with the institution of record). No wilt claim is recorded from the 45-year AICRP document because the retrieved text does not clearly assign a reaction to this variety. Disease reaction in original variety data: Unknown.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to early shoot borer and stalk borer (original variety data, CSC). Tolerant to internode borer (TNAU Expert System). Tolerant to top borer (ICAR-SBI Plant Breeding page). Hard rind, so less damage from insect pests and rodents (Sugar Lab blog, secondary source). A research-literature group statement on insect pest tolerance covering Co 0118, Co 0238, Co 0239 and Co 98014 was excluded because the digest marks it as not variety-specific.

agronomic_details.yield: Original variety data: 76000 to 78000 kg/ha (76 to 78 t/ha) average yield; adaptation text gives 76 t/ha under normal conditions. Trial results are summarised under field_trials.
agronomic_details.stability: Performs better than the standard under water stress and water logging conditions (original variety data). Good ratooning ability, including winter-harvested ratoons (ICAR farmer guide; Sugar Lab blog). No multi-environment stability statistics found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation in Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttaranchal (Uttarakhand), and West and Eastern Uttar Pradesh (original variety data). Early maturity noted. Suitable for less fertile soil and waterlogged conditions (Sugar Lab blog, secondary source). Suitable for co-generation (Krishi Jagran). Maturity conflict: TNAU, Sugar Lab blog and Krishi Jagran describe it as early, spring-planted; ICAR-SBI Plant Breeding page describes it as midlate.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: BUD GERMPORE POSITION (A/M/ SUB M) : ABSENT; BUD GROOVE (P/A) : ABSENT; GROWTH RING COLOUR : YELLOW; LEAF WIDTH : 4.4 CM; LEAF LENGTH (OF 1ST TRANSVERSE LEAF AT 180 DAYS) : 153 CM; LAMINA COLOUR (LG/G/DG) : GREEN; LEAF CARRIAGE SHAPE : SPREADING WITH DROOPING LEAVES; LEAF SHEATH COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN WITH RED PATCHES; LEAF SHEATH WAXINESS (L/M/H) : VERY LIGHT; LEAF SHEATH SPINES (A/SMSF/HM/HF) : ABSENT; LEAF SHEATH CLASPING (ST/ET/TT) : EASY TRASHING TO SELF TRASHING; DEWLAP COLOUR (AT 10 MONTH) : YELLOWISH GREEN, BROAD, VERY LIGHT WAX; LIGULE (P/A) : CRESCENT W. LOZENGE; SHAPE OF THE AURICLE : LONG LANCEOLATE ON ONE SIDE; FLOWERING : ABSENT; ERECTNESS : LIGHTLY LODGING. Digest field habit: erect, early vigorous growth, dark green foliage, tall canes free of spines and splits, about 14% fibre, shy flowering; non-lodging and non-flowering early clone (original variety data).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) All-India Coordinated trial, NWZ: mean cane yield 76.29 t/ha, sugar yield 9.26 t/ha, sucrose 17.59%, versus CoJ 64 at 62.71 t/ha (+21.66%). (2) SBI Coimbatore AICRP table (area 0.346 lakh ha): cane yield 76.29 t/ha and sucrose 17.59%, matching trial (1). (3) ICAR farmer guide: yield gain of about 22% over CoJ 64 in cane and 8% in sugar. (4) 45-year AICRP document: adsali (18-month) crop about 200 t/ha, 16.9% above Co 86032. (5) TNAU Expert System: mean cane yield 116.69 t/ha and sugar yield 16.83 t/ha; test context not stated, treated as unverified and not used for conclusions. Trial locations, years and replication design are not stated in the digest.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to drought and salinity, moderately resistant to red rot, tolerant to wilt and internode borer, per the ICAR-SBI AICRP varietal development page -- http://www.iisr.nic.in/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- Tolerant to drought and salinity per the ICAR Sugarcane Breeding Institute genetic resources appendix -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Under a 2004-05 field drought trial, cane and sugar yield losses were smaller in Co 99004 than in the resistant standard Co 86032, and it transpired less water -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JSR/article/view/99240
- Among drought-screened clones, Co 99004 ranked as a drought-tolerant entry with yield held under drought -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343847825_Physiological_traits_imparting_drought_stress_tolerance_to_promising_sugarcane_Saccharum_spp_clones
- Recorded as tolerant to drought and salinity in the 2006 ICAR zone identification report -- https://www.isaaa.org/kc/CBTNews/2006_Issues/Nov/CBT_Nov_10.htm
- Waterlogging, submergence, flood and heat: No evidence found for this variety. The waterlogging tolerance in the ISAAA item refers to Co 99006 (Neeraj).
- Discrepancy: the ICAR AICRP page gives "moderately resistant" to red rot, while the TNAU expert system and the Springer appendix give "resistant" to red rot and wilt. Both are reported.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Red rot: moderately resistant (MR) per the AICRP "Forty Five Years" table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Red rot resistance and wilt resistance per TNAU expert system -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/season&varieties.html
- Red rot: moderately resistant per TNAU organic package -- https://sandakumar.blogspot.com/2014/03/crop-production-sugarcane-sugarcrops-sugarcane.html (listed; see Co 99004 red rot entry in the TNAU list) and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane
- Red rot, wilt and internode borer: tolerant to internode borer -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/popular-promising-varieties-of-sugarcane/
- Smut: No evidence found for this variety specifically.
- Early shoot borer, root grub: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: mid-late / midlate; shy flowering -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/popular-promising-varieties-of-sugarcane/
- Plant habit: erect, early vigorous growth, dark green foliage, tall canes without spines or rind splits, about 14% fibre, moderate tillering -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/plant-breeding/
- Mean cane yield 116.69 t/ha, sugar yield 16.83 t/ha, CCS yield 18.76 t/ha (ICAR SBI table) -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Cane yield 116.7 t/ha, CCS 18.8 (AICRP table) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Golden yellow A1-quality jaggery -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0168945226001354
- Good ratooner in ratoon trials (ratoonability study; Co 99004 listed among good ratooners) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273745999_Physiological_Studies_on_Ratoonability_of_Sugarcane_Varieties_under_Tropical_Indian_Condition
- Adsali crop yield of about 200 t/ha, reported as 16.9% above Co 86032; this appears in the AICRP table text and may not be specific to this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Seed rate 75,000 two-budded setts/ha (TNAU package for Co 99004 listing) -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/07_Sugarcane.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Co 62175 x Co 86250 -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/expert_system/sugar/season&varieties.html
- Parentage Co 62175 x Co 86250 with year of identification 2006 and year of release/notification 2007 -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Breeding method: clonal selection of a hybrid-derived clone, with Co numbers assigned to best-performing clones before zonal trials -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/plant-breeding/
- In vitro gamma-irradiation mutants (super shoot-root and rootless mutant lines) were derived from Co 99004 -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0168945226001354
- QTL, marker, genome sequence or SSR studies: No evidence found for this variety.
- Breeding-line code: Co 99004 is the code; variety code A0701022 (from the input) was not found in any retrieved source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/varieties
- Released through the Central Varietal Release Committee (listed among 23 varieties) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/from-the-director-s-desk?id=363
- Registered with PPVFRA (listed among 12 varieties) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/from-the-director-s-desk?id=363
- Notified as S.O. 122(E), commercialised from 06/02/2007 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvjjuly0112.pdf
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found. No individual breeder is named in any retrieved source for this variety.
- Regional testing: Clones suitable for North India were tested at the Regional Centre, Karnal -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: resistant under both natural and artificially inoculated conditions, with tall, thick, non-lodging canes (ejplantbreeding release paper). agronomic_details.yield: Average cane yield 88.16 t/ha and sugar yield 11.14 t/ha in North Western Zone AICRP trials (2000-01 to 2003-04), about 21% above CoS 767 and 13% above Co 1148. agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (no multi-environment stability analysis reported beyond the North Western Zone AICRP trials).
agronomic_details.adaptation: North Western Zone AICRP trials. The digest's Pantnagar and AICRP listings support Uttarakhand as the developing centre. The CSC record recommends irrigated conditions in Uttarakhand, Western and Central Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) North Western Zone AICRP trials 2000-01 to 2003-04: average cane yield 88.16 t/ha, sugar yield 11.14 t/ha, about 21% above CoS 767 and 13% above Co 1148. (2) Juice sucrose on par with CoS 767 and CoS 8436, and higher than Co 1148. Cane length, diameter and weight were higher than the checks. (3) AICRP zonal table: mid-late maturity, yield column 800-850 and 17.0-19.0 (units not stated). (4) Pantnagar trials in AICRP: 2-4 entries nominated per year; CoPant 97222 is one of 9 Pantnagar-developed varieties. (5) Field check on Co 7204 x CoPant 97222 hybrid clones: cane yield linked to millable canes, single cane weight and sucrose. (6) Pandey et al. 2018 trial: CoPant 97222 showed better mean performance on several traits and was a good parent; numeric values were not reliable enough to report.

- Commercial web story calls it drought-tolerant; low reliability, not from a research source -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/web-story/these-5-best-sugarcane-varieties-that-will-give-higher-yield
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The waterlogging-related article lists CoPant 97222 only as one of many clones, with no result for it -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-2-2020/Vikas%20Belwal%20and%20Sarfraz%20Ahmad.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Red rot resistance: see STRESS TOLERANCE (ejplantbreeding and AICRP table).

- Average cane yield 88.16 t/ha and sugar yield 11.14 t/ha in North Western Zone AICRP trials (2000-01 to 2003-04), about 21% above CoS 767 and 13% above Co 1148 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2491
- Juice sucrose was on par with CoS 767 and CoS 8436 but higher than Co 1148; cane length, diameter and weight were higher than checks -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2491
- Mid-late maturity; release year 2005 by CVRC; identified 2005 and listed in AICRP zonal table; notified 2007 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Notification under S.O. 122(E) dated 2007, GBPUA&T Pantnagar listed as developer -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- AICRP table entry: mid-late, Uttarakhand SVRC release, yield column 800-850 (units not stated in the extract) and 17.0-19.0 (likely CCS or sucrose, not stated) -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/12%20AICRP%20-%20SUGARCANE.pdf
- Pantnagar trials as tested in the AICRP: 2-4 entries nominated per year; CoPant 97222 is one of the 9 Pantnagar-developed varieties -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/12%20AICRP%20-%20SUGARCANE.pdf
- Field check with Co 7204 x CoPant 97222 hybrid clones shows cane yield linked to millable canes, single cane weight and sucrose -- https://www.academia.edu/83539390/Correlation_and_path_analysis_in_sugarcane_hybrid_clones_of_proven_cross
- Pandey et al. 2018 trial shows CoPant 97222 had better mean performance on several traits and was a good parent; numeric values in the extract are not reliable enough to report -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-4-2018/Deepankar%20Pandey,%20et%20al.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: open-pollinated cross on CoPant 84212 (the variety record's "General cross" wording is the same cross) -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2491
- Pedigree listed as CoPant 84212 in the breeding summary -- https://www.slideshare.net/kldpngr/current-status-and-future-prospects-of-sugarcane-breeding-in-india
- SSR marker study: CoPant 97222 coded S6; NKS9, NKS17 and NKS38 markers amplified it; similarity 0.44 with Co 05011 -- https://www.scielo.br/j/babt/a/6vXyshVtY6XjLWvZzTnL7Zg/?format=pdf&lang=en
- CoPant 97222 is the general (female) parent of CoPant 17224 in the same SSR study -- https://www.scielo.br/j/babt/a/6vXyshVtY6XjLWvZzTnL7Zg/?format=pdf&lang=en
