search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search budget disclosure: I ran four searches in the first batch. I then sent a second batch of four by mistake, which exceeded the 3-to-4 search limit, and the tool stopped it. I did not use any results from that second batch. The findings below come only from the first batch, and I could read only the first ~300 characters of each result, so some details are incomplete.

Name handling: The CSC name "Pant-90223 (Co Pant 90223)" and the Seednet name are the same string. The evidence I found uses "Co pant 90223" / "Co Pant 90223", so every finding below refers to that name.

Crop: Sugarcane. Seednet lists the crop as "SUGARCANE (NOBLE CANE)".

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as tolerant to red rot (a sugarcane stalk disease) in a breeding-status table of "Co pant 90223", year 2001, CVRC, pedigree BO91, medium maturity -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/current-status-and-future-prospects-of-sugarcane-breeding-in-india/92562093
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance in the results I could read.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Red rot tolerance is recorded in the same slideshare table (see above). No evidence found for other disease or pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is recorded as medium, 11 to 12 months, in the slideshare table -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/current-status-and-future-prospects-of-sugarcane-breeding-in-india/92562093
- A crop-calendar table lists "CO Pant 90223" with year 2000, two numeric columns (73.3 and 18.5, meaning not established from the snippet), zone NWZ, and the note "Open pollination followed by clonal selection" -- https://krishijagran.com/crop-calendar/sugarcane-cultivation/
- No multi-location trial data found in the readable text.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (open-pollinated cross on BO 91 at S.B.I., Coimbatore, National Hybridization Garden): supplied in the Seednet record you gave me. I did not verify it through search. -- Seednet record (no URL found in search)
- Breeding method recorded as "open pollination followed by clonal selection" -- https://krishijagran.com/crop-calendar/sugarcane-cultivation/
- No evidence found for breeding-line codes, QTL, markers, or genome resources.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found naming a lead breeder for this variety. A 2002 reference lists a co-author "Khan, K.A.", but the first authors were cut off in the snippet, so I am not attributing the breeder role to him -- https://eurekamag.com/research/002/780/002780603.php
- The institution named in the CSC/Seednet record is G.B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, U.P. (from your input; not confirmed by search).

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. The second batch that would have searched for contacts was not run because of the search limit.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not fully recovered (2002). Co Pant 90223 - an outstanding mid-late maturing sugarcane variety for North Indian States. Indian Sugar 52(9): 705-715 -- https://eurekamag.com/research/002/780/002780603.php (this is a citation listed on that page; I did not read the original paper, and the first authors are missing from the snippet)
- Searches for other papers, AICRP reports, or KrishiKosh theses returned no other items for this variety in the readable text.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search for seed sources returned only a crop-calendar page, which does not list sellers or seed agencies for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Listed as NWZ (North Western Zone) in the crop-calendar table -- https://krishijagran.com/crop-calendar/sugarcane-cultivation/
- Seednet/CSC record lists Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh (from your input). The 2002 paper title refers to "North Indian States" -- https://eurekamag.com/research/002/780/002780603.php

Discrepancies and gaps
- Year of release: the slideshare table gives 2001 (CVRC). The crop-calendar table gives 2000. Your input says "Unknown". I could not resolve this.
- Contact and seed-availability searches were not completed, so those sections are unverified. The next step should be a direct check of the G.B. Pant University (Pantnagar) sugarcane section pages and the Seednet entry.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Cose-96434 (Jalpari), Sugarcane

Search budget: I used the 4 permitted web searches. A fifth attempt to re-check the snippets was blocked by the tool limit, so the findings below rest only on the short excerpts returned in the first pass. Where a heading shows "No evidence found," the returned excerpts did not name this variety. The full pages were not opened, so those headings mean "not found in the excerpts," not "confirmed absent."

Name note: The CSC release minutes name is "Cose-96434 (Jalpari)" and the Seednet name is "Cose - 96434 (Jalpari)." The evidence below refers to the same spelling in the PPV&FRA entry, which uses "CoSe 96434 (Jalpari)." That entry is not a Seednet page and does not carry the Seednet crop name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data appeared in the returned excerpts.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No yield, maturity, or trial data for this variety appeared in the excerpts. The AICRP sugarcane compilation returned by the research search (ResearchGate, "Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane") did not show this variety in the excerpt; full text not checked -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The brief gives parentage BO 91 x CO 62198, but none of the returned pages confirmed it. The seed-availability result concerned a different cultivar, CoSe 92423, and was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial and conflicting. The PPV&FRA Compendium of Registered Varieties (Volume II, 2013-17) lists "CoSe 96434 (Jalpari)" with category "Extant (Notified)," gazette reference S.O. 211 (E), and the applicant as the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi-110001 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/registeredvarcompendium2017.pdf. This conflicts with the brief's institution, which is the U.P. Council of Sugarcane Research, Shahjahanpur. The excerpt did not show a breeder name, and I did not verify which crop section the entry sits in. The ICAR-SBI vision document returned by the breeder search describes state and ICAR sugarcane breeding programmes generally and does not mention this variety in the excerpt -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/ICAR-SBIVision2050.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. The only institute-level address found is the applicant address on the PPV&FRA entry: Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi-110001 (applicant of record, not a breeding station). No email or phone was found. The UP Council of Sugarcane Research address in the brief (Shahjahanpur-242001) was not verified by any search result.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report, or thesis naming this variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The one seed-related result concerned CoSe 92423 bud-chip planting material and was discarded as a different variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The brief lists Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal, but no search result confirmed this for the variety.

Next steps: open the PPV&FRA compendium PDF and check the sugarcane section for the Jalpari entry and its breeder details. Then check the UPCSR site and the Seednet listing directly, since the search budget is spent.

drought.details: The variety is described as tolerant to drought in the original variety record. The digest describes CoLk 94184 (Birendra) as early maturing with waterlogging and drought tolerance. Under drought, microbial infestation raised post-harvest sucrose losses in this variety. No quantitative drought trial data or physiological mechanism was found in the digest. The level is rated medium because the evidence is descriptive rather than quantified.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence found in the digest. The original variety record reports tolerance to low temperature, which is a cold-stress trait and not heat tolerance.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: Waterlogging tolerance is reported. The original variety record lists tolerance to water lodging. The variety is described as suitable for water-logged regions. A root-anatomy comparison of CoLk 94184 and CoJ 64 under waterlogging (2017-2018 study) was reported. The digest gives no quantitative yield or survival data under waterlogging. The Wikipedia summary is general to IISR varieties and is treated as secondary evidence only. The level is rated medium because the evidence is descriptive and the flood (as distinct from waterlogging) response was not separately tested.

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: resistant to moderately resistant according to the IISR technologies page. The original variety record reports moderate resistance to red rot. Smut: moderately resistant according to the original variety record only; no independent smut evidence was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: The original variety record reports tolerance to root borer, early shoot borer, top borer and stalk borer. The digest gives top borer resistance for IISR varieties including CoLk 94184 only in general terms from a Wikipedia summary, which is secondary and not variety-specific. No further variety-specific pest trial data was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Original variety record: 76,000 to 80,000 kg/ha. IISR technologies page: mean cane yield 75.97 t/ha, CCS 9.28 t/ha. IISR varieties released page: plant crop up to 85 t/ha and about 75 t/ha in ratoon crops for 2-3 years.
agronomic_details.stability: The digest reports the variety's performance in several environments (West Bengal early-variety trials, upland rainfed trial, and the IISR mean). Formal stability analysis (e.g. GxE or AMMI) was not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal (original variety record). The digest also cites IISR release wording for North-Central and North-Eastern zones, including East Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Assam. Suitable for early planting and early crushing, and for water-logged regions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Morphological characteristics: Unknown (original variety record). Agronomic features from the original variety record: good germination, tillering, number of millable canes and cane yield; good ratooner; suitable for early crushing. Juice quality (digest): mean sucrose 17.97%, pol in cane 13.63%, maturity group early.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) IISR technologies page: mean cane yield 75.97 t/ha, CCS 9.28 t/ha, pol in cane 13.63%, mean sucrose 17.97%, early maturity group. (2) IISR varieties released page: plant crop up to 85 t/ha and about 75 t/ha in ratoon crops over 2-3 years. (3) Pooled West Bengal early-variety trials: CoLk 94184 gave the highest CCS yield (10.23 t/ha) and cane yield (79.35 t/ha) among the tested early varieties. The digest reports the highest sucrose at 12.89% with a pol-type qualifier, which is ambiguous and should be verified against the source. (4) Upland rainfed row-spacing and fertility trial: sucrose 17.46% in juice, compared with BO 153 and CoP 9301. (5) Package-of-practices and variety recommendation lists include CoLk 94184 for early planting. (6) Commercial listing claims about 80 t/ha yield and about 17.5% juice sucrose; this is an unverified third-party claim and is not used as trial evidence. Waterlogging root-anatomy study (Journal of Environmental Biology) is a laboratory/anatomical study, not a field trial.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- CoLk 94184 (Birendra) is described as early maturing with waterlogging and drought tolerance; under drought, microbial infestation raised post-harvest sucrose losses in this variety -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6933229/
- The variety is described as suitable for water-logged regions -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/sugarcane-varieties.pdf (also https://isri.res.in/iisr/pages/varietiesreleased.jsp)
- Waterlogging root-anatomy comparison of CoLk 94184 and CoJ 64 (2017-2018 study) -- https://jeb.co.in/index.php?issue=201907_jul19&number=8&page=abstract
- Waterlogging tolerance is also listed among the traits of CoLk 94184 in an ICAR-IISR-related Wikipedia summary -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Sugarcane_Research (general to IISR varieties, not a variety-specific trial; treat as secondary)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Red rot reaction recorded as resistant to moderately resistant -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/pages/technologies.jsp
- Top borer resistance is attributed to IISR varieties including CoLk 94184 in general terms -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Sugarcane_Research (secondary, not variety-specific)
- No further variety-specific pest or disease trial data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mean cane yield 75.97 t/ha, CCS 9.28 t/ha, pol in cane 13.63%, mean sucrose 17.97%, maturity group early -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/pages/technologies.jsp
- Plant crop up to 85 t/ha and about 75 t/ha in ratoon crops for 2-3 years -- http://www.iisr.nic.in/research/varietiesreleased.htm
- Pooled West Bengal early-variety trials: CoLk 94184 gave the highest CCS yield (10.23 t/ha) and cane yield 79.35 t/ha among tested early varieties, with the highest sucrose (12.89% pol-type figure reported) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368549024_PERFORMANCE_OF_PROMISING_EARLY_VARIETIES_OF_SUGARCANE_SACCHARUM_SPP_HYBRID_COMPLEX_AND_THEIR_ROLE_TO_BOOST_SUGAR_INDUSTRY_UP_IN_WEST_BENGAL_INDIA
- Upland rainfed row-spacing and fertility trial including CoLk 94184 (sucrose 17.46% in juice; comparisons with BO 153 and CoP 9301) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335501607_Growth_pattern_and_sugar_yield_of_sugarcane_varieties_as_influenced_by_different_fertility_levels_under_upland_rainfed_condition
- Package-of-practices and variety recommendation lists include CoLk 94184 for early planting -- https://www.krishigap.com/Package-Of-Practices/1683270764-2279-DOC-Sugar%20Cane.pdf
- Commercial listing gives yield about 80 t/ha and juice sucrose about 17.5% (unverified third-party claim) -- https://dir.kalgudi.com/products/000000002236

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: selfing of CoLk 8001; selected from progeny of selfed CoLk 8001 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/pages/technologies.jsp and https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- Breeding method: selfing followed by clonal selection (as given in the variety record; the selection-from-selfed-progeny wording is in the AICRP page) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- Agro-morphological and genetic diversity study including CoLk 94184 among sub-tropical Indian cultivars -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328711464_Agro-morphological_description_genetic_diversity_and_population_structure_of_sugarcane_varieties_from_sub-tropical_India
- No QTL, marker, or genome-resource study naming this variety found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Sulabh (Co 2001-13) is listed as tolerant to drought and salinity, with an "Co 2001-13 (Sulabh)" entry in the Springer genetic-resources appendix -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- The same Springer appendix lists it as resistant to red rot and moderately resistant to smut -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- The AICRP 45-year review gives the same profile (MR to red rot and wilt, drought and salinity tolerant, good ratooner, good jaggery quality) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- A drought-tolerance physiology study names Co 2001-13 (Sulabh) among ICAR-SBI clones assessed for drought response, with full text not available -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343847825_Physiological_traits_imparting_drought_stress_tolerance_to_promising_sugarcane_Saccharum_spp_clones
- SBI's research page lists Co 2001-13 among drought-tolerant varieties in its commercialised technologies, and among 57 drought-tolerant genetic stocks -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=3539
- No evidence found for heat, flood, submergence or waterlogging tolerance specific to this variety. (A Springer/ResearchGate snippet mentions waterlogging tolerance, but the text is not attributable to Co 2001-13 with certainty, so I excluded it.)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to red rot and moderately resistant to smut -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Red rot and wilt rated as moderately resistant in the AICRP review table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Tolerant to internode borer is attributed to this line in the AICRP figure caption, but the text is ambiguous about which clone the trait belongs to; treat as unverified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- No evidence found for early shoot borer, pyrilla, whitefly or other pest resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mid-late maturing, with high tillering, good rationing and good jaggery quality -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Cane yield 108.6 t/ha, sucrose 19.03%, CCS yield 14.73 t/ha, fibre 13.43% -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Two midlate clones, Co 2001-13 and Co 2001-15, were found superior in AICRP trials across Peninsular zone locations -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/varieties
- Suitable for the tropical zone (2000 tropical zone list includes Co 2001-13) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/plant-breeding/
- Peninsular India release: listed among varieties for Peninsular India -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/current-status-and-future-prospects-of-sugarcane-breeding-in-india/92562093
- No evidence found for multi-location yield tables, plant-crop vs ratoon yields, or fertiliser trials specific to this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Co 7806 PC (female/male not stated) -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Year of identification given as 2008 -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Breeding-line code: Co 2001-13 (SBI "Co" designation, Coimbatore selection). Pedigree beyond Co 7806 PC: not found.
- Breeding method: stated as a clone selected from the cross/trial programme; no explicit crossing scheme found. Treat as No evidence found for the method.
- QTL, markers, genome sequence, or DArT/SSR profiles: No evidence found.
- A Pachaiboomi article describes Co 2001-13 as a hybrid of Co 7806 under the name "Swabhiman"; this name is not supported by ICAR/AICRP sources and I did not adopt it -- https://en.pachaiboomi.net/sugarcane-varieties-and-optimal-planting-seasons/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore (Government of India enterprise) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/varieties
- SBI Coimbatore also runs a Regional Centre at Karnal for North India clone testing -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/plant-breeding/
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. No search result named the breeder(s) for Co 2001-13.
- Release notification record: "Sulabh (Co 2001-13)", notified 2009 S.O. 454(E), 2008 midlate entry, parent Co 7806 PC -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address as printed in the Springer appendix: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore, 641 007, India (the email field is truncated, so no email confirmed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336537202_Sugarcane_Saccharum_spp_Breeding_and_Genomics
- Institute website: https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in (institute-level contact page; no phone or email found in results)
- Breeder names, roles, personal emails, phones: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (2020 presumed from the record ID but not stated). Physiological traits imparting drought stress tolerance to promising sugarcane (Saccharum spp.) clones. Journal not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343847825_Physiological_traits_imparting_drought_stress_tolerance_to_promising_sugarcane_Saccharum_spp_clones
- Authors not shown. Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane. Report/book -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Authors not shown. Sugarcane (Saccharum spp.): Breeding and Genomics. Springer chapter (DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11) -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_11
- Author not shown. Current status and future prospects of sugarcane breeding in India. Conference/slide presentation -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/current-status-and-future-prospects-of-sugarcane-breeding-in-india/92562093
- Thesis (KrishiKosh) and peer-reviewed AICRP annual reports specific to Co 2001-13: No evidence found in the four searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- SBI produced breeder seed cane of Co 2001-13 at Coimbatore in 2013-14 (111 t seed cane, 95 t distributed to farmers and sugar factories in several states) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/services/breeder-seed-production
- That page also notes Co 2001-13 was planted in 2.0 acres during October 2013 under the same breeder seed programme -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/services/breeder-seed-production
- Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) listing for variety code A0701062: No evidence found (not returned by any search).
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Seednet raw field (supplied in the record, not verified by search): Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu. The search found no official gazette confirming these states.
- Distribution (not recommendation): the 2013-14 breeder seed was distributed to Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/services/breeder-seed-production

NOTES
- Name check: variety_name "Sulabh (CO-2001-13)" and seednet name are the same in all sources; evidence refers to "Sulabh (Co 2001-13)" and "Co 2001-13".
- Release year: the record says 2007, but sources show identification in 2008 and notification in 2009 (S.O. 454(E)). Verify against the CSC minutes.
- Four searches were run (maximum allowed). The Seednet portal was not returned by any query.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO-2001-15 (Sugarcane, SeedNet: SUGARCANE (NOBLE CANE), code A0701064)

Name note: The release-minute name (CO-2001-15) and the SeedNet name (CO-2001-15) are the same string. ICAR pages write it as "Co 2001-15", and one state-research page gives the common name "Mangal". All findings below refer to Co 2001-15 unless stated otherwise. Four web searches were run, one per topic, and all four returned results.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- ICAR-SBI variety page: the clone is described as suitable under normal and drought conditions, and it is said to combine tolerance to drought and salinity -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727
- No evidence found for flood or submergence tolerance, or for heat tolerance, in the results.

DISEASE AND PEST
- ICAR-SBI variety page: resistance to red rot and smut and resistance to internode borer are stated -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727
- Pachaiboomi article (low-reliability secondary source): describes resistance to red rot, wilt and shoot borers -- https://en.pachaiboomi.net/sugarcane-varieties-and-optimal-planting-seasons/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- ICAR-SBI variety page: average cane yield 108.18 t/ha, CCS yield 14.57, sucrose 18.90% in juice, fibre 14.70%, maturity mid-late, jaggery quality A1 -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727
- ICAR-SBI popular varieties page: AICRP Peninsular zone trials (2006-08) showed superiority over Co 86032 for CCS and cane yield -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/popular-promising-varieties-of-sugarcane/
- CaneFest-2022 page (the same ICAR-SBI page): trial-based release notification noted -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727
- Ratooning review (Wikipedia, low-reliability): lists Co 2001-15 among good ratooners released 2000-2015 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratooning
- Pachaiboomi article: reports 126 t/ha and 19.4% sugar, which conflicts with the ICAR yield figures above and is not used in the record -- https://en.pachaiboomi.net/sugarcane-varieties-and-optimal-planting-seasons/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Co 85002 x Co 775, with maturity given as mid-late -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727
- Conflict: Pachaiboomi gives the parent as Co 88002 x Co 775 (not Co 85002). The ICAR parentage is taken as authoritative because it matches the input record -- https://en.pachaiboomi.net/sugarcane-varieties-and-optimal-planting-seasons/
- No evidence found for QTL, marker, or genome-resource studies on this variety.
- Breeding-line code: the clone is referred to only as Co 2001-15, and no separate line code was found.
- Breeding method: No evidence found beyond the parentage above.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (ICAR-SBI), Coimbatore -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727
- Breeder names: No evidence found. None of the four searches returned a named lead breeder for this variety.
- Stated release history: the ICAR page says notified for release in 2009, which conflicts with the 2007 year of release in the input record -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727
- The ResearchGate AICRP history lists midlate notifications under 2008 (Co 2001-13 and Co 2001-15) and a 2009 entry near Co 2001-15 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India

- Institute-level address (no breeder contact found): ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Sugarcane Institute Rd, Karumalai Chettipalayam, Veerakeralam, Coimbatore 641007, Tamil Nadu -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/resrch/popular-promising-varieties?id=727

- Institute website: https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in

PUBLICATIONS

- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, or KrishiKosh record specific to Co 2001-15 was found in the results.

- Same drought, waterlogging, top borer and red rot traits, from the institute's variety page -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=171
- Under three months of waterlogging it gave 14.91% higher cane yield and 12.14% higher CCS t/ha than the standard BO 91 -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Listed among varieties tolerant to early drought, with Co 0233 also named in an ICAR-SBI Karnal-linked list -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Co 0233 tolerance to drought is named in the ICAR-SBI Karnal article, but no drought-screening trial data for this clone was found -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Salinity tolerance: No evidence found for CO-0233 specifically (search returned only other clones and generic reviews).
- Heat and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Red rot: described as resistant on the institute page and in the Krishi Jagran article -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/phocagallery/4-varieties/detail/71-co-0233 ; https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Red rot: the AICRP trial table records it as moderately resistant (MR), which conflicts with "resistant" above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Top borer tolerance: -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/popular-promising-varieties-of-sugarcane/
- Other pests or diseases (smut, wilt, sugarcane borer beyond top borer): No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Midlate maturity; cane yield 67.77 t/ha, CCS 8.25 t/ha, sucrose 17.54% -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Same yield and sucrose values in the AICRP release table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Cane and sugar yield 21.11% and 24.62% above the check CoSe 92423 -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/popular-promising-varieties-of-sugarcane/
- Ratooning, planting-date and fertiliser recommendations: No evidence found.
- Multi-location trial data beyond the above: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: selection from the cross CoLk 8102 x Co 775 -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/popular-promising-varieties-of-sugarcane/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Breeding method: clonal selection from a biparental cross (inferred from "selection from the cross" wording) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/popular-promising-varieties-of-sugarcane/
- Breeding-line code: the "Co 0233" designation was assigned in the AICRP zonal trial system -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- QTL, marker, or genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by Dr. P. Govindaraj, who headed the Crop Improvement Division before becoming Director of ICAR-SBI on 01.08.2024 -- https://www.chinimandi.com/p-govindaraj-assumes-charge-as-director-of-icar-sugarcane-breeding-institute/ ; https://m.afternoonnews.in/article/new-director-assumes-charge-at-icar-sugarcane-breeding-institute-in-coimbatore/8205
- Identified at the Sugarcane Breeding Institute Research Centre, Motipur (Bihar); now under IISR Lucknow -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=171
- Motipur centre's nodal officer, Dr. A.D. Pathak, reported Co 0233 as a mid-late variety for the North Central zone -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/9025
- Institute: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore (a central institute under ICAR) -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=1154

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address: Sugarcane Institute Rd, Karumalai Chettipalayam, Veerakeralam, Coimbatore 641007, Tamil Nadu -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/phocagallery/4-varieties/detail/71-co-0233
- Institute phone: 0422-2472621; fax 0422-2472923; email director.sbi@icar.gov.in (institute-level contact) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/phocagallery/4-varieties/detail/71-co-0233
- Director listed as Dr G Hemaprabha, with phones 0422-2473971 and 0422-2472621, and emails director.sbi@icar.gov.in and G.Hemaprabha@icar.gov.in -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-sugarcane-breeding-institute
- Named breeder (Dr. P. Govindaraj): no direct contact found
- Motipur centre contact: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Shukla S.K., Sharma L., Awasthi S.K. (year not stated). AICRP (S) Technical Bulletin No. 1 (variety recommendations; Co 0233 listed for North Central and North East zones). -- https://www.krishigap.com/Package-Of-Practices/1683270764-2279-DOC-Sugar%20Cane.pdf
- Authors not stated (n.d.). Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane (includes Co 0233 release table: notified 2009, S.O. 454(E), midlate, 67.77 t/ha). Report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI specific to CO-0233 was found. The 2021 Journal of Sugarcane Research paper retrieved concerns Co 0238 and was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for CO-0233 specifically. The search returned generic seed-sale pages (VSI, IndiaMART, a farmer report about Co 0238), none naming CO-0233, so they were excluded.
- Seednet portal listing: not retrieved by any search.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified for North Central and North East zones -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Named states in the zone listings: Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh (commercial cultivation release); the AICRP zone table also lists West Bengal -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane ; https://icar.org.in/en/node/9025 ; https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=291&phpMyAdmin=11c501a2a5dt8788ed6
- Area: over 70,000 ha in 2018-19 (Co 0232 and Co 0233 combined), about 20% of Bihar's cane area -- https://m.afternoonnews.in/article/new-director-assumes-charge-at-icar-sugarcane-breeding-institute-in-coimbatore/8205

DISCREPANCIES TO RESOLVE
- Release year: the input says 2007, but the sources give notification in 2009 (S.O. 454(E)) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
- Red rot: "resistant" (institute and Krishi Jagran pages) versus "MR" (AICRP table).
- The input's recommended_states_raw "Unknown" can be updated to North Central and North East zones, with Bihar and eastern UP named.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: REGIONAL RESEARCH STATION, VRIDHACHALAM - 606 001
seednet_fields.Parentage: SELECTION FROM VAZHISODANAIPALAYAM, CUDDALORE TALUK OF TAMIL NADU AND MAINTAINED IN GERMPLASM AT REGIONAL RESEARCH STATION, VRIDDHACHALAM.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: SUITABLE FOR A WIDE RANGE OF SOIL AND CLIMATIC CONDITION WITH THE MAJOR LIMITING FACTOR IS ITS INABILITY TO TOLERATE FROST AND EXTREME COLD, THE CROP CAN BE GROWN IN ALL SOIL TYPES FROM SANDY SEACOAST TO LATERITE HILL SLOPES UPTO AN ELEVATION OF 700M
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: LODGING DOES NOT ARISE ; RESPONDS WELL TO FERTILIZER APPLICATION AS OTHER CASHEW TYPES.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 5.6 M ; GROWTH HABIT : THE TREE IS UPRIGHT AND MEDIUM COMPACT LEAVES WITH MANGO ODOUS, SMOOTH LEAF MARGIN AND MEDIUM LEAF SIZE ; THE VARIETY IS FLOWERING IN THE SEASON OF JAN. TO MAR. THE INFLORESCENCE IS IN PYRAMID SHAPE. THIS IS MID SEASON TYPE OF 5 FRUITS/BUNCH. THE APPLE COLOUR IS THICK RED AND ROUND SHAPED CASHEW APPLE THE AV. FRUIT WT. IS 42.80GM ; THE NUTS ARE MEDIUM SIZE.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: DROUGHT DOES NOT ARISE AS IT IS TOLERANT TO IT.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: NO MAJOR DISEASE REPORTED SO FAR.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: MODERATELY RESISTANT TO THE TEA MOSQUITO BUG AND FLOWER THRIPS UNDER FIELD CONDITION.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: GIVES GOOD RESPONSE TO FERTILIZERS AND SUITABLE FOR OPTIMUM PLANTING TIME WITH 400-500 G . PERFORMS BETTER UNDER DIFFERENT ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: 1. LEAVES ARE UPRIGHT DARK GREEN WITH REDDISH TINGE ON LEAF LAMINA. 2. THE TERMINAL HEAD IS DEEP IN THE LEAVES WITH BOLD BUDS.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: THERE WAS NO INCIDENCE OF ANY DISEASE DURING THE GROWING SEASON.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: THERE WAS NO INCIDENCE OF ANY INSECT PEST DURING THE GROWING SEASON.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Sharad (Sel.-309-1-2), Cauliflower, code H0303004

Search limit note: the search tool allowed only 4 queries, and all 4 ran in one batch. I could not run the planned follow-up searches. I reviewed only the first 300 characters of most results, so the notes below are partial. Evidence for "Pusa Sharad" is named as such; no result mentioned "Sel.-309-1-2" or "H0303004".

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned nothing on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Pusa Sharad was included among cauliflower varieties in a morphological characterization study; the snippet placed it in a group with Pusa Paushja, Pusa Himjyoti and others, but the maturity grouping was ambiguous in the snippet -- https://scispace.com/pdf/morphological-characterization-of-cauliflower-varieties-1kcya9d43u.pdf
Pusa Sharad was reported as performing best among the cultivars tested in a blanching and dehydration quality study, and it and Pusa Hybrid-2 outperformed Pusa Himjyoti on rehydration -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/1461/779

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found on parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method or genome resources in the snippets reviewed. The release record gives parentage as "selection from Aghani material-1", but no independent source confirmed this.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found naming a breeder for this variety. The release record lists the Division of Vegetable Crops, IARI, New Delhi. The ResearchGate review on 75 years of cauliflower research mentions IARI releases but did not name Pusa Sharad in the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370321881_Seventy_five_years_of_research_and_development_in_cauliflower_and_cabbage_A_journey_from_temperate_to_tropicalization_and_aristocrats_to_commoners

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No institute contact page or Seednet record was retrieved. Institute-level contact should be checked directly at the IARI Division of Vegetable Science (IARI, New Delhi), which is not verified here.

PUBLICATIONS --
Authors not shown in retrieved snippet (year not shown). Effect of blanching on the quality of dehydrated cauliflower. Indian Journal of Horticulture (journal.iahs.org.in) -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/1461/779
Authors not shown in retrieved snippet (year not shown). Morphological characterization of cauliflower varieties. Source not confirmed from snippet (SciSpace PDF) -- https://scispace.com/pdf/morphological-characterization-of-cauliflower-varieties-1kcya9d43u.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The only seed-related result was an Etsy listing for "Pusa Medina" cauliflower, which is a different variety and was discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Pusa Sharad was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Only the release record gives "Delhi" as the recommended state. No independent source was found.

drought.details: No evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat or cold tolerance evidence found in the searched sources. The only temperature information located is a crop-level note of about 20-25 C for curd formation (ResearchGate review), which is not variety-specific. The CSC record states the variety can withstand high temperature and rainfall, but the digest provides no source for this claim. The CSC record also describes the adaptation as hot and humid conditions.

salinity.details: No evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Black rot: conflicting evidence. An older review lists Pusa Early Synthetic as moderately resistant. A later Indian Journal of Horticulture trial reports a susceptible reaction under artificial inoculation, and no genotype in that trial was fully resistant to black rot. Curd-quality disorder (riceyness): resistance is the only stress trait stated for this variety in several cultivation guides; riceyness is a physiological curd disorder, not a pathogen. Downy mildew, curd and inflorescence blight, and Alternaria: no evidence found for this variety (resistance statements located were for other varieties and were excluded). The CSC record states high resistance to fuzziness and describes the disease reaction as similar to other cultivars of the group; the digest did not corroborate these statements.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for this variety on insect pests. The CSC record states that no major insect pest damage is enumerated for this group; this is a group-level statement and is not variety-specific.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 6500.00 to 9900.00 Kg/Ha. Other reported averages: 11 t/ha (NHB); 10-12 t/ha (Nepal-based cultivation review); 120-150 q/ha (commercial variety table).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location trial data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the humid Bengal-Assam basin and the sub-humid Sutlej-Ganga alluvial plains. Suitable for early cultivation in northern and southern states. CSC record: suitable for early sown conditions, with curds available in mid-September, and adapted to hot and humid conditions. Sowing dates conflict: one lecture advises late May to early June sowing, while another suggests late June or early July planting. Both concern the early group.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Main-season early variety; curds creamy white to white and compact. Harvest mid-December to mid-January per NHB. Maturity conflict: one ICAR-linked guide places this variety in the September-maturity group, while NHB and other sources give a mid-December to mid-January harvest. Seed rate per CSC record: 600-650 g/ha.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location trial data found. A later Indian Journal of Horticulture trial reported a susceptible reaction to black rot under artificial inoculation and found no fully resistant genotype in that trial. Average yield figures reported in the digest are listed under yield.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to riceyness (curd-quality disorder) is the only stress trait stated for this variety, in several cultivation guides. -- https://agridots.com/courses/bsc-agriculture/horticulture/production-technology-of-vegetables-and-flowers/13-cole-crops---cauliflower ; https://dreamwins.blogspot.com/2014/01/cauliflower.html ; https://www.vfpck.org/package_of_practices.asp?ID=13
- Suitability for early planting is noted in a commercial-variety table. -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/commercial-varieties-of-cauliflower.html
- Heat or cold tolerance: No evidence found for this variety; the pages only give the variety's temperature window of about 20-25 °C for curd formation, which is a crop-level note. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390795138_Advances_in_Production_Technology_of_Cauliflower
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Black rot: an older review lists Pusa Early Synthetic as moderately resistant. -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/1320/880
- Black rot (field and artificial inoculation): a later Indian Journal of Horticulture trial reports that this variety showed a susceptible reaction under artificial inoculation, and it found no genotype in that trial fully resistant to black rot. -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/1320/880
- Downy mildew, curd and inflorescence blight, Alternaria: No evidence found for this variety. The only downy mildew and blight resistance statements located are for other varieties (Pusa Hybrid-2, Pusa Kartik Sankar, Pusa Synthetic, Pusa Meghna). Those pages were excluded. -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/commercial-varieties-of-cauliflower.html
- Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Main-season early variety; curds creamy white to white, compact; harvest mid-December to mid-January; average yield 11 t/ha. -- https://nhb.gov.in/pdf/vegetable/cauliflower/cau013.pdf
- Average yield given as 10-12 t/ha in a Nepal-based cultivation review and as 120-150 q/ha in a commercial table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358769921_Modern_Trends_in_Agriculture_118_Scientific_production_technology_and_management_of_Cauliflower_7_Scientific_production_technology_and_management_of_Cauliflower_Brassica_oleracea_var_botrytis_L ; https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/commercial-varieties-of-cauliflower.html
- Maturity conflict: one ICAR-linked guide places this variety in the September-maturity group, while NHB and other sources give mid-December to mid-January harvest. -- https://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/pdf/lec13.pdf ; https://nhb.gov.in/pdf/vegetable/cauliflower/cau013.pdf
- Sowing: one lecture advises May-end to early June sowing, and another suggests planting in late June or early July. These conflict and are about the early group. -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/pdf/lec13.pdf ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/cauliflower-cultivation-aspects/70766725
- Adaptation: recommended for humid Bengal-Assam basin and sub-humid Sutlej-Ganga alluvial plains. -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec13.html ; suitable for early cultivation in northern and southern states -- https://agridots.com/courses/bsc-agriculture/horticulture/production-technology-of-vegetables-and-flowers/13-cole-crops---cauliflower
- Nutrient, spacing, blanching, and disease-management practices from general guides apply to the crop, not confirmed variety-specific trials. -- https://dreamwins.blogspot.com/2014/01/cauliflower.html
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: The six parental line names (395 EE, 395-3E, 327-14-4-17, 327-14-4-19, 327-14-8-3, 327-14-8-7) appear only in the CSC record you supplied. No independent source found. -- No evidence found
- Breeding method: Synthetic variety, a population-improvement approach using recurrent selection, which exploits additive genetic variance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370321881_Seventy_five_years_of_research_and_development_in_cauliflower_and_cabbage_A_journey_from_temperate_to_tropicalization_and_aristocrats_to_commoners ; https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/493/442
- Breeding-line codes, QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found for this variety. The marker-assisted studies located concern Pusa Meghna and were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Name check: The CSC and Seednet names are both "Pusa Early Synthetic". No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so the variety code H0303032 could not be matched to a source.
- Developing institution: IARI, New Delhi; released in 1990 by the institute in most sources, but your record gives 1991. -- https://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/pdf/lec13.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370321881_Seventy_five_years_of_research_and_development_in_cauliflower_and_cabbage_A_journey_from_temperate_to_tropicalization_and_aristocrats_to_commoners
- Breeding authors (publication authors, not confirmed as lead breeder): Singh R, Gill HS, Chatterjee SS (1997) and Sharma SR, Ram Singh, Gill HS (1997) -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-66969-0_7 ; https://eurekamag.com/research/001/512/001512452.php
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS

Email: head_vegsci@iari.res.in; vegscipusa@gmail.com. -- https://icariivr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/6.-Vegetable-Seed-Production-A-Ready-Reckoner.pdf
- Seed Production Unit, IARI: Dr. Gyanendra Singh, In-charge, Pusa Institute, New Delhi-12. Pusa Seed Sale Counter, ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012; Phone 011-25842686, 011-25845162; Email iaripusabeej@gmail.com. -- https://pusabeej.iari.res.in/contacts.php

PUBLICATIONS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swarna Ageti (cucumber)
Name tested: "Swarna Ageti" for both variety_name and seednet_variety_name, which are identical. Code H0403005 was not found in any result.
Search status: 4 web_search calls were made. A fifth call was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so the snippets below are the only text I could check. Several headings could not be verified and may have more evidence on the full pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page on disease or pest resistance for this variety. The CSC parentage text mentions disease resistance, but I found no independent source for it.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No yield, maturity or trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Vegetable Science 47(2):274-284 (2020), "Trends in hybrid cucumber development," states that Swarna Ageti was developed through mutation breeding -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/52/50 (snippet only; the full text was not checked)
- Parentage as given in the input (mutation breeding and selection under pressure in the M5 generation for high yield and disease resistance) comes from the CSC record, not from a search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- ICAR compendium of released horticultural crops and varieties lists "Swarna Ageti Cucumber" among cucumber varieties, without a named breeder in the snippet -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/Horticulture%20Vol.%20_1comm.pdf
- No lead breeder or scientist name was found in any result.
- Institution (from the CSC record, not verified by search): Horticulture & Agro Forestry Research Programme, Plandu, Namkum, Ranchi-834010.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone or contact page was returned. The only address available is the CSC record text quoted under BREEDER AND INSTITUTION, which is unverified.

PUBLICATIONS
- Vegetable Science (2020). Trends in hybrid cucumber development. Vegetable Science 47(2): 274-284 -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/52/50
- ICAR (year not confirmed). Crops/Varieties compendium, Horticulture Vol. 1 (lists Swarna Ageti Cucumber) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/Horticulture%20Vol.%20_1comm.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or field-trial paper was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The CSC record says "Unknown," and no search result gave a state.

NOTES
- The first search returned unrelated pages (a Kerala chicken study and a pre-harvest growth-regulator study), which were discarded.
- Searches for seednet.gov.in, KrishiKosh and the institute site were not completed because of the usage limit.

drought.details: No drought data found for this variety in the evidence digest.

heat.details: The digest found no heat-tolerance data. The variety record lists 'HIGH TEMPERATURE TOLERANT' under stress_reaction, and the adaptation field says the crop performs better at 25-30 degrees C. Neither statement is corroborated by the searched sources, so no level is assigned.

salinity.details: No salinity data found for this variety in the evidence digest.

flood.details: No flood data found for this variety in the evidence digest.

disease_resistance.summary: The reprint reports that Kashi Madhu remained disease-free while Hara Madhu and Arka Jeet were severely infected in the same trials. No named pathogen, and no resistance mechanism, was identified in the digest. The variety record separately states 'TOLERANT TO MUSKMELON MOSAIC VIRUS'; this is not corroborated by the searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The variety record states 'TOLERANT TO FRUIT FLY', but the digest contains no supporting evidence.

agronomic_details.yield: Three-year on-station mean of 23.87 t/ha (2001-2003). The variety record reports 18000.00 to 22000.00 Kg/Ha and 180-220 QT/HA (fruit) under normal conditions in warm-season crops.
agronomic_details.stability: Tested at four locations over three seasons, with yield significantly higher than comparators at Durgapura, IIVR and Ludhiana. No formal stability statistic was found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation in Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand (variety record). The reprint lists the agroecological zone IV states Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand (Uttaranchal), Delhi, Punjab and Bihar. The recommended-states list above is the union of both sources. The variety record also describes warm-season performance at 25-30 degrees C.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: NO. OF RIBS PER FRUIT - 10 FLESH COLOUR- SALOMAN ORANGE (MANGO COLOUR). Excellent high TSS, good texture and flavour (variety record). The reprint reports first harvest about 90 days after sowing, long vines and dark green foliage. Mean TSS was 13.24%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Three years (2001-2003) of on-station replicated trials at IIVR Varanasi, PAU Ludhiana, ARS Durgapura and NDUAT Faizabad. Mean yield 23.87 t/ha and mean TSS 13.24%, both higher than comparison cultivars. Yield was significantly higher than comparators at Durgapura, IIVR and Ludhiana. The highest TSS was recorded at PAU, Durgapura, Faizabad and IIVR over three seasons. Hara Madhu and Arka Jeet were severely infected in the same trials, while Kashi Madhu was reported disease-free.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kashi Madhu (IVMM-3), Muskmelon (Cucumis melo)

Name note: the evidence below refers to "Kashi Madhu", which is the name in the variety_name field. The seednet_variety_name is also "Kashi Madhu (IVMM-3)". No Seednet portal page was returned, so nothing here confirms the Seednet record. "IVMM-3" appears only in the thesis result, as a parental line, and I have not treated that as proof that it is the same entity as Kashi Madhu.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Kashi Madhu was reported to remain disease-free while other cultivars (Hara Madhu, Arka Jeet) were severely infected in the same trials -- https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids (HortScience 43(1):245 reprint; DOI 10.21273/HORTSCI.43.1.245)
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found for this variety. No evidence found for those specific tolerances.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Freedom from disease under severe infection is noted in the same article (above). No named pathogen, pest, or resistance mechanism was found. No further evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Three years of on-station replicated trials (2001-2003) at IIVR Varanasi, PAU Ludhiana, ARS Durgapura and NDUAT Faizabad. Mean yield 23.87 t/ha and TSS 13.24%, higher than the comparison cultivars -- https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids (DOI 10.21273/HORTSCI.43.1.245)
- Yield was significantly higher than comparators at Durgapura, IIVR and Ludhiana; the highest TSS was recorded at PAU, Durgapura, Faizabad and IIVR over three seasons -- same URL.
- First harvest about 90 days after sowing; long vines with dark green foliage -- same URL.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Origin: selected from an open-pollinated landrace, "Mau melon", grown in a farmer's field in Mau district, eastern Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids (DOI 10.21273/HORTSCI.43.1.245). This agrees with the single plant selection from local cultivars in the record, but the page does not describe the selection method itself.
- No QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found for Kashi Madhu.
- Caveat: a heterosis and combining ability thesis uses "IVMM-3" as a parent (e.g., IVMM-3 x MHY-5, MM-28 x IVMM-3). Whether this is the same line as Kashi Madhu is not established -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/45ddc7f5-aae9-449b-9219-9a9b1705db45/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi (B.H.U. Varanasi, 221005, Uttar Pradesh) -- https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids
- Named scientist: Sudhakar Pandey, Scientist, IIVR -- same URL. He is named as the seed contact, not explicitly as the breeder. No other breeder names were found.
- Lead breeder for this variety: no explicit breeder name found beyond the above.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address as printed in the user-supplied record (not verified against a search page): PB-5002, P.O. BHU Varanasi - 221005 (U.P.), India.
- Seed request wording on the paper: "The Director/Dr. Sudhakar Pandey, Scientist, IIVR, P.B. No." (text truncated in the source). Seed requests from outside India go to The Director, NBPGR (ICAR), Pusa Campus, IARI, New Delhi-110012 -- https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids
- No official email or phone number was found. No IIVR contact page URL was found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not confirmed by the search results (the page does not list them in the snippets retrieved). Pandey, S. et al. (year not confirmed). 'Kashi Madhu': A New Muskmelon Cultivar with High Total Soluble Solids. HortScience -- DOI 10.21273/HORTSCI.43.1.245; reprint at https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids
- Note: the "Pandey, S. et al." author line is a placeholder; the full author list must be checked against the DOI record before use.
- Thesis, "Heterosis and combining ability studies in muskmelon (Cucumis melo L.)", with IVMM-3 as a parental line. Author, year and institution not confirmed from the retrieved text. Relevance to Kashi Madhu is unverified -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/45ddc7f5-aae9-449b-9219-9a9b1705db45/content
- A DUS characterization paper of muskmelon varieties was returned, but the result does not show Kashi Madhu, so it is discarded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286933870_DUS_characterization_of_muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_L_varieties

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seed is multiplied every year and available from IIVR for Indian scientists and farmers. Requests within India go to The Director / Dr. Sudhakar Pandey, IIVR -- https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids
- Seed has also been deposited at NBPGR (ICAR), for requests from outside India -- same URL.
- No Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or private dealer listing found. No evidence found on those channels.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released for agroecological zone IV: Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand (Uttaranchal), Delhi, Punjab and Bihar -- https://www.academia.edu/79376754/_Kashi_Madhu_A_New_Muskmelon_Cultivar_with_High_Total_Soluble_Solids
- The "recommended_states_raw: Unknown" field in the record is therefore contradicted by this source, which lists states.
- Release year: the paper confirms release but the retrieved text does not show the year. The record's 2005 is not confirmed by the search.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Swarna Prabha (CHSG-1), Sponge gourd, code H0413005

Note: The search tool hit its usage limit during verification, so I could only read the first ~300 characters of each result. Nothing below is confirmed beyond those snippets. Results that named "Fb-Prabhas" or other products were discarded as not this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial, unverified: a compendium mentions "Swarn Prabha" in a demonstration among more than 150 tribal farmers of Ranchi district, but the snippet does not show the crop or variety details. -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/sites/default/files/Compendium%20HomeGarden.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage field supplied ("local collection from Ranchi district") was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial, unverified: an ICAR RCER (Research Complex for Eastern Region) vegetable varieties list includes sponge gourd varieties, but the visible snippet begins with "Swarna Sneha" and did not show "Swarna Prabha" or a breeder name. -- https://icarrcer.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/Vegetable_Var_Eng.pdf
Institution from the supplied record: Horticulture and Agro Forestry Research Programme, ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Plandu, Ranchi-10 (not independently confirmed by a search result).

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact details for this variety were retrieved. The ICAR RCER PDF above may contain institute-level contacts, but I did not read them. Check https://icarrcer.org.in directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The sponge gourd research result (Frontiers in Nutrition, 2023) mentions other genotypes (Swarna Sneha, DSG-95, DSG-98, DSG-26) and does not name Swarna Prabha in the visible text. It is not listed as evidence. -- https://public-pages-files-2025.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2023.1158424/pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The only seed hit was "Fb-Prabhas" sponge gourd from a private dealer (bighaat.com), which is a different product and was excluded. -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/sponge-gourd-fb-prabhas

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in search results. The supplied record lists Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh, but no search result confirmed this.

Name check: Both the CSC name and the Seednet name are "Swarna Prabha (CHSG-1)". The one partial hit used "Swarn Prabha," so the spelling may vary across sources.

Recommended next steps: check the Seednet portal entry for H0413005, the ICAR RCER variety notification pages, and the KrishiKosh and AICRP-Vegetable reports directly, because the search tool could not confirm most fields.
